https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-11/c.title: Tame Impala to headline Coachella alongside Dua Lipa, SZA and Madonna
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-11/c.author: Courtney Fry
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-11/c.text:
BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Tame Impala will headline Saturday night at Coachella in 2027. (Supplied: Julian Klincewicz)

The Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival, one of the planet's biggest music events, has unveiled its 2027 line-up, with headline performances from SZA, Dua Lipa and Tame Impala across two weekends in April.

It will be the fifth time Tame Impala's Australian multi-instrumentalist Kevin Parker has taken his psychedelia-driven work to the coveted Indio Valley festival in California.

The full line-up for the 2027 Coachella Festival features a bevy of Australian acts.  (Supplied: Coachella)

This also marks his second headlining slot after his mind-bending 2019 performance.

In what could possibly be a first in Coachella history, Parker has previously collaborated with the festival's other headliners.

He produced tracks on Dua Lipa's 2024 album Radical Optimism, and recently joined SZA on the Justice-produced track Flower In A Hurricane for the upcoming Grand Theft Auto VI video game soundtrack.

Could there possibly be some special appearances across the headline sets at Coachella in 2027?

Parker is not alone in representing Australia on the massive Coachella stages, with debuts and returnees joining him from our side of the globe.

Electronic producer Dom Dolla and sampling kings The Avalanches are set to return to the festival, and indie-electro favourites Empire of the Sun will take their shimmering show to the desert for the first time in a decade.

Double J gives you new Australian music you'll actually love, alongside the classic tracks you keep coming back to. Give your playlist a rest this Ausmusic Month and join us.

Meanwhile, Sydney's Gang of Youths, ARIA Award-winning Ghanaian Australian rapper Genesis Owusu, Brisbane DJ Odd Mob and Byron Bay-via-Berlin's Dream Boat will make their first big entrances on Coachella stages.

They join an impressive slate of acts for the festival's two weekends, including a performance from Madonna in the dance tent, a special Coachella moment not witnessed since 2006.

Otherworldly Quebec duo Angine de Poitrine, UK dancefloor masters Underworld, American rock icons Weezer, New York rap rock king Mike D and Daptone prodigies The Womack Sisters are also on the bill, with plenty more to explore.

The festival, which sold out in its advance sale earlier this year, is live-streamed on YouTube, giving artists an enormous potential audience that extends well beyond those on the ground.

Coachella Music and Arts Festival kicks off in Indio, California, on Friday, April 9, and runs over two weekends, finishing on Sunday, April 18.

https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-11/p.author: Isabella Kelly
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-11/p.text:
BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Topic:
Livestock Farming

The heifer was winched out of the mine shaft before happily wandering away. (Facebook: Barossa Veterinary Service)

A three-months pregnant heifer was rescued after falling three metres into a disused mine shaft.

Volunteers worked with a vet to lift the animal out with a purpose-built harness.

She was relatively unharmed, with minor scrapes and bruises.

A pregnant heifer has had a lucky escape after falling three metres into a disused mine shaft in South Australia's Barossa region.

The animal was recovered from an exploratory hole in an old quarry site at a farm near Keyneton on Tuesday.

Local vet Saul Morelli was on site with nearly 15 SES and CFS volunteers to assist with the rescue, which took about three hours.

Besides a few minor cuts and bruises, she emerged in a stable condition. (Supplied: State Emergency Service)

"It was just a pretty normal morning up until that point," Dr Morelli said.

"The first time I went down into the hole with her, she was definitely a little bit tense and not sort of keen to get too close to anyone, which is understandable. Pretty fed up with the situation.

Dr Morelli lightly sedated the heifer, and a specialist harness was used to lift her from the shaft.

"As soon as her feet touched the ground on the outside of the hole she was off, and it was a bit of a panic to quickly let all the straps loose," he said.

Saul Morelli said it was one of the more unique jobs he had attended. (Supplied: State Emergency Service)

"Despite the fact that after the sedation, just before we lifted her out, she was nearly about to fall asleep … I think the adrenaline rush of it all sort of took over."

Cow rescued from mine shaft in the Barossa. (Supplied: State Emergency Service)

Kapunda SES deputy unit manager Gunther Schulz said the disused shaft had been on the property for "at least a number of decades", and had previously been covered.

"At some point on Tuesday morning, the cow had wandered across the branches and sticks that were on top of it and fallen straight through," Mr Schulz said.

"The cow was actually very calm for the situation she'd managed to get herself in. She was standing sort of in the bottom of the hole, a few scrapes and bruises on her legs and stuff, but not any serious injuries."

A purpose-built lifting harness was used in the rescue.

"[It] allows us to place straps under and around the animal and then support that via a spreader bar, so it provides the maximum comfort and safety to the animal," Mr Schulz said.

The location of the shaft on top of a hill meant a traditional crane could not be brought up, he said, so a neighbour's loader was used.

The total rescue operation took place over about three hours. (Supplied: State Emergency Service)

"Thankfully it's not an incredibly common occurrence that we actually use the lifting equipment … we have a lot of other techniques and equipment that we can use to manoeuvre animals around," Mr Schulz said.

"When we rock up to an animal rescue, it's about making sure that we're creating a safe space for the animal, for our responding crews and for any members of the public."

AFLW playerThe AFLW saw record crowds in 2026. (Getty: Michael Willson/AFL Photos)

AFLW sides are more likely to finish down the bottom of the ladder when their players rate their workplace culture low, the players' association says.

Data collected from the union around the middle of the season suggests a strong correlation between workplace culture and on-field performance.

"If we look at AFLW, what we're seeing is there is a bit of a widening gap between the best of our workplace culture data and that which is more at the bottom," AFL Players Association chief executive James Gallagher told ABC Sport.

"We're seeing some of the highest scores ever reported at the top end, so that's fantastic. That's what we want to see, but we are seeing a gap between the best and the bottom end."

Former AFLW player and coach Lauren Arnell has criticised the standard of Collingwood, while emphasising the responsibility of coaches to "put on a show" to grow the game.

This year, four teams were assessed as having the best workplace culture on record and four teams the worst.

This was evaluated according to club care, mental breaks, off-field expectations, relationships, schedule flexibility and study/work support.

Five of this year's finals teams were in the top seven for "overall workplace culture". Non-finalist teams overwhelmingly rated on the lower end for workplace culture scores.

It comes after widespread media scrutiny on struggling clubs, particularly Collingwood.

James Gallagher says there is a correlation between successful AFLW sides and workplace culture ratings. (Getty: James Wiltshire/AFL Photos)

The Magpies, along with St Kilda, finished with one win each this season, while GWS and Essendon had just two victories out of their 12 games.

Of those four bottom-ladder clubs, all but the Giants parted ways with their head coaches.

The Magpies and Saints are now set to undertake external reviews of their women's programs,. Essendon has opted to conduct an expanded internal review.

North Melbourne, Geelong, Melbourne, Carlton, Gold Coast, Sydney, Western Bulldogs and Hawthorn finished in the top eight this year.

Sydney and the Western Bulldogs featured in the finals series this year. (Getty: Darrian Traynor)

The Kangaroos have lost one game in three years and the Demons have regularly finished in the finals.

The data also showed some players as having rated respect for the men's AFL club head of performance and head coach as low to extremely low.

Furthermore, men's players being embroiled in off-field news, such as the Sydney Swans saga involving allegations of sexual assault or GWS' "controversial couples" night leading to player sanctions, can impact the women's programs.

"There's no doubt they are extraordinarily challenging for all to navigate. I mean, do they have an impact on AFLW playing groups? In some cases, they do for sure," Mr Gallagher said.

"Making sure there's an opportunity for those players' views to be heard and considered is a really important part of how footy clubs in 2026 now operate."

As a tough season nears its end, Collingwood announces a strategic review into the struggling AFLW program, with the club's president admitting the Pies had not "got it right".

Crucially, with the seasons overlapping more every year, men's and women's programs require access to the same facilities, including the gym and communal areas.

Just half of all players said they felt their men's and women's programs were aligned.

"Those clubs that report the strongest workplace environments are much more likely to be successful, and that's reflected in the final series in front of us," Mr Gallagher said.

"The game is a high-performance game and to enable that to be successful you do need people who are fronting up, comfortable, confident, feeling like they're really well supported, and we're seeing that reflected in the wins and losses column now, for sure."

Women's teams with strong workplace culture are more likely to make the finals, according to the AFLPA. (Getty: Kelly Defina)

Workplace culture includes club support for players outside football commitments, including work and study.

While players have seen huge strides in increased contact hours since season one, more than half of all players still work outside football.

Sixty-four per cent engage in casual work, 32 per cent work part-time and 4 per cent full-time. None of the 45 Irish players can work due to their visas.

The players' association expects next year's AFLW season to accommodate more double-headers. The start date is yet to be announced.

Merril Kelly, 70, was allegedly murdered in her rural Victorian hometown. (Supplied )

Brian Robert Barnes is standing trial for the murder of 70-year-old Quambatook woman Merril Kelly.

The prosecution alleges Mr Barnes snuck into Ms Kelly's house and killed her after she banned him from the local pool.

The trial continues in Bendigo.

A court has heard a man allegedly snuck into a woman's bedroom in the middle of the night and killed her after she banned him from the local pool.

Merril Kelly, 70, a community leader and president of the Quambatook Memorial Swimming Pool, was found dead in the town's cemetery in north-west Victoria in January 2025.

Brian Robert Barnes has pleaded not guilty to murder and is standing trial in the Supreme Court in Bendigo.

The 68-year-old, known in his hometown of Quambatook as Bert, sat in the dock at the back of the courtroom wearing a white T-shirt and glasses.

Brian Barnes has pleaded not guilty to murder. (Supplied: Instagram)

Crown prosecutor Patrick Bourke KC told the court today Mr Barnes allegedly admitted to his brother what he had done.

The court heard an autopsy found Ms Kelly died from head injuries.

In his opening address, Mr Bourke told the jury a dispute arose after Ms Kelly arranged for Mr Barnes to fix a leak at the community swimming pool in November 2024.

Ms Kelly texted Mr Barnes to say the work would be unpaid, and he replied saying she may need to pay him "with cake".

The court heard Ms Kelly eventually gave Mr Barnes $200 in cash for the work, however, he then demanded $2,000, before escalating the figure owed to $2,500 and threatening legal action.

The day before the alleged murder, the court heard Mr Barnes went for a swim at the pool and was reprimanded by a volunteer for diving in the shallow end.

The Quambatook Memorial Swimming Pool was run entirely by volunteers. (ABC News)

Mr Bourke said Mr Barnes splashed the volunteer in the face, grabbed her glasses and threw them away.

The police were called and spoke to Mr Barnes at his home.

The court heard later that day, about 8:20pm, Mr Barnes posted a video online talking about the incident and said he had been banned from the pool by Ms Kelly.

The prosecution alleges Mr Barnes drove to Ms Kelly's house about 1:40am, likely entering through an unlocked door, and attacked her in her bedroom, "bashing her over the head".

"The accused dragged [Ms Kelly] out the back door, down a brick paved path … along a gravel driveway and we say, put her in the back of his ute," Mr Bourke said.

Mr Bourke said Mr Barnes drove to the Quambatook cemetery, about 4.5 kilometres away.

Firefighters found Merril Kelly's body at the Quambatook cemetery. (ABC News)

"The accused relates to his brother and sister-in-law, that at the cemetery, he asked [Ms Kelly] why she'd not paid him for the work, she doesn't respond, 'so I then poured petrol on her and set her alight'," Mr Bourke told the court.

The court heard Mr Barnes had arrived at his brother's house about 4:30am.

Mr Bourke told the jury when Mr Barnes's brother asked him about some injuries to his face and arms, Mr Barnes told him "she bloody scratched me up".

CFA firefighters called to the cemetery fire discovered Ms Kelly's body about 5am, Mr Bourke said.

Mr Barnes was arrested the next day near Castlemaine in central Victoria.

Mr Bourke said Ms Kelly was a carer for her husband who had late stage dementia, and they slept in separate bedrooms.

He said her autopsy found extensive injuries to her head, and a black cable tie around her neck.

The court heard neither elevated carbon monoxide levels nor soot was found in her body, suggesting she was already dead when her body was allegedly set on fire.

The prosecution opening will continue when the trial returns tomorrow, before the defence response from barrister David Cronin SC.

A perpetrator of child sexual abuse has had his jail sentence extended in the ACT. (ABC News: Ian Cutmore)

South Australian man Mike Worsman was 12 years old when he was sexually abused in Canberra in the 1990s by a then 15-year-old.

The man, now in his 40s, was initially jailed for more than two years but after an appeal, he was re-sentenced to four years and seven months.

Mr Worsman said that was still inadequate and called on the justice system to start "listening to victims".

A child abuse survivor says the extension of his abuser's jail sentence by an ACT court still "falls short" of reflecting the seriousness of the offences.

Warning: This story contains details some readers may find distressing.

South Australian man Mike Worsman was 12 years old when he was sexually abused in Canberra in the 1990s, by the then-15 year old.

His abuser — now aged in his 40s — pleaded guilty to five charges, including acts of indecency, in 2024.

Last year, ACT Supreme Court Justice David Mossop jailed the man for two years and seven months — to be suspended after 16 months.

Prosecutors appealed the decision and today the man was re-sentenced to four years and seven months' jail — not to be suspended until June 2028.

The court's reasons for the decision on the appeal are yet to be published.

At the time of the initial sentencing last year, Mr Worsman said he felt let down by the system.

Today, he said the new sentence still was not long enough.

"What I'd hopefully allowed the ACT court to do is find one of these people and put them where they need to be, I hoped, for life," Mr Worsman said.

"We've found that that's not the case today.

"They've been given some extra time, but certainly not what I was hoping for."

Mr Worsman says he felt compelled to report the assaults to police in 2019, when he discovered someone else had suffered at the hands of his abuser.

He took part in a five-hour interview with police in South Australia before he was told the incidents needed to be reported to the Australian Federal Police in the ACT.

Mr Worsman said it took 18 months for his case to be passed on to the AFP.

After going through another interview process with police, he had to wait for his abuser to complete a sentence in a South Australian jail, before the man could face court proceedings in the ACT.

He says the appeal process after last year's sentencing added to the trauma.

"But it has put a strain on me and my family to go through seven years of fighting against courts, fighting against the system to get this extra 18 months in prison."

He said he believed "better support starts with listening to victims".

"You know, it starts with actually seeing us as people and that the system is there to serve victims, rather than it being the other way round where I'm asking something of them," he said.

"When it gets that rare opportunity — that really rare opportunity — to put a serial child sex offender behind bars where society is safe from them, and this just falls short … it falls short."

https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-11/v.author: Alex Brewster

BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

The Queensland government has introduced legislation to crack down on the creation of non-consensual sexually explicit content with artificial intelligence. (ABC News: Michael Lloyd)

Advocates have raised concerns a loophole in proposed legislation to crack down on AI deepfakes could see offenders escape more serious sentences.

Victims' Commissioner Kate Connors welcomes the crack-down but says clashes between the new policy and existing child protection laws could see offenders plead to lesser sentences.

A parliamentary committee will report back to the government before the legislation returns to state parliament for debate.

A loophole in proposed AI deepfake laws could see predators escape with lesser convictions, Queensland's Victims' Commissioner says.

Legislation introduced to state parliament last month would criminalise the creation of non-consensual sexually explicit images or audio through artificial intelligence or other digital technology.

It would carry a maximum penalty of three years behind bars for adults, and 18 months for children.

Attorney-General Deb Frecklington told the House that the government was ensuring the state's laws kept pace with technology.

"The target of every deepfake image is a real person — increasingly, a young person whose natural vulnerabilities and often tenuous grip on self-esteem and confidence collapse with the viral spread of hyper realistic images, videos and audio that implicate them.

"The bogus content is overwhelmingly sexual in nature, with certain AI tools complicit in the peddling of this filth."

Deb Frecklington says the government is ensuring laws keep pace with changing technology. (ABC News: Luke Bowden)

But in a parliamentary committee submission, Victims' Commissioner Kate Connors, while welcoming the crackdown, raised concerns.

She noted adults who created sexually explicit deepfakes of children would currently be charged under the existing offence of child exploitation material and face up to 20 years in prison.

Ms Connors submitted the new legislation could overlap with child exploitation laws, "which means an offender could theoretically plead to the lesser new offence".

"That would mean that the offender could receive a lesser sentence and not fall under the reportable sex offender scheme," she said.

Ms Connors recommended the proposed AI deepfake laws not apply to adults who offend against minors, to avoid the overlap.

Addressing parliament, Ms Frecklington said deepfake content "humiliates the victims who have been depicted without their consent".

But Ms Connors noted the proposed laws didn't cover 'humiliating or degrading' depictions of people and were limited to sexually explicit images and audio.

Artificial intelligence provides an opportunity for anyone to create realistic and misleading content, including fake sexualised material. (ABC News: Berge Breiland)

She called for the government to go further in its clampdown and expand the scope to include such content.

"In school environments, anecdotally, many cases which cause harm include content designed to humiliate and exclude and may not necessarily involve sexual content," she submitted.

"Limiting the offence to sexual content sends the message to victims of non-sexual deepfake harm that causes humiliation or degradation that their harm is not important."

The legislation differs from interstate jurisdictions such as New South Wales and Victoria, where non-consensual intimate images or audio must be created with intent.

Legal Aid Queensland submitted there needed to be changes to ensure a person was not accidentally acting illegally.

As the first case under new anti-deepfake legislation goes before the courts, authorities and experts say the rise in the creation of the non-consensual sexually explicit material is concerning.

"As drafted, a person who prompts a tool for a generic image could commit an offence carrying three years imprisonment because of a resemblance they neither intended nor knew of," the submission said.

"An intent element would ensure that criminal liability targets intentionally wrongful conduct rather than accidental, unintended or legitimate behaviours."

The Queensland Sexual Assault Network accepted the rapidly evolving nature of the technology.

It called for the government to strengthen its approach with training for first responders, and education in schools and the community.

The parliamentary committee will report back to the government before the legislation returns to state parliament for debate.

BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Lawyers seek to question Premier Chris Minns and Police Minister Yasmin Catley. (ABC News: Monish Nand)

NSW Premier Chris Minns and Police Minister Yasmin Catley could be forced to give evidence in court in a case related to February's protest at Sydney's Town Hall.

The pair, along with Tourism Minister Steve Kamper and senior police, have been served subpoenas to shed light on planning of the police operation.

The politicians and police have been approached for comment.

The NSW premier and two ministers could be forced to give evidence in court during the week of the state election, in the criminal case against protesters who opposed the visit of Israeli President Isaac Herzog.

Chris Minns, Police Minister Yasmin Catley and Tourism Minister Steve Kamper have been served with subpoenas to give evidence on March 8, just five days before voters head to the polls on March 13.

More than a dozen demonstrators are facing charges, including assaulting police, over the rally outside Sydney Town Hall on February 9.

Mr Kamper is being called after making the major event declaration at the February protest. (Facebook: Steve Kamper)

The defence is seeking to question the politicians about their involvement in the planning of the police operation, which it claims was unlawful.

Defence solicitor Nick Hanna told the ABC the premier had openly admitted his government was involved in operational decisions about the Herzog protest.

"We want to question him about that involvement, which we expect to argue likely amounted to improper interference in what should have been independent police-decision making," Mr Hanna said.

Solicitor Nick Hanna, who is representing the protesters. (Supplied)

Mr Hanna pointed to the premier's comments at a press conference held a few days after the rally.

"We can't blame the police for doing what we asked them to do, and that is to keep the people of New South Wales safe, protect mourners who were down at the ICC [where Mr Herzog was speaking] on that evening," Mr Minns said on February 12.

Police Commissioner Mal Lanyon, Assistant Commissioner Paul Dunstan, and the chiefs of staff of the premier and police minister have also been subpoenaed to give evidence.

On October 19, the day the Law Enforcement Conduct Commission (LECC) began hearings examining police conduct at the protest, Mr Minns said the government was involved.

"I'm not gonna be in a situation now that LECC is looking at police operations where I try and distance myself from it," he said.

The government appeared to give police access to two sources of additional power on the night of the protest.

One was a Public Assembly Restriction Declaration (PARD) made under a post-Bondi Beach attack law that was later ruled unconstitutional by the Court of Appeal.

The other was a Major Events Declaration, which the protest organisers unsuccessfully challenged at the eleventh hour.

The Major Events Declaration was made by Mr Kamper in his capacity as tourism minister, which is why the defence seeks to question him.

Spokespersons for Mr Minns, Ms Catley and Mr Kamper said it would be inappropriate to comment as the matter was before the courts.

The NSW Police Force has been approached for comment.

"What the premier knew, and the warnings he was given about the [PARD] laws being invalid and the dangers of relying on them at the Herzog protest, will be live issues," Mr Hanna said.

Those subpoenaed may avoid giving evidence if they successfully apply to have the subpoenas set aside.

In the video clips, police can be seen grabbing protesters by the head or neck at a rally against the Israeli president in Sydney.

Last month, the defence showed the court footage of what it alleged was unlawful force by police, as it sought communications between senior officers and the parliamentarians.

Local Court judge Scott Nash agreed with the protesters that the correspondence was relevant and dismissed the police commissioner's attempt to block its release.

Police have withdrawn 10 of the 30 original prosecutions over the rally, with a trial involving at least 16 protesters expected to take place in July 2027.

Topic:
Extreme Weather Events

A roof torn off by strong winds at Regents Park in Logan. (Supplied: Nicholas Thompson)

More than 81,000 households across south-east Queensland were left without power on Wednesday night when "very dangerous" storms and destructive winds swept across the region.

Almost 60,000 of the outages occurred in the Logan area, which bore the brunt of the wild weather.

Energex said there are more than 400 fallen powerlines reported around the south-east, with more expected.

A tree fell on a car on Chambers Flat Road at Munruben.  (Supplied: Harvey's Towing)

Power was also cut in the Scenic Rim, the Moreton Bay Region and the Brisbane and Gympie council areas.

Energex spokesperson Justin Coomber said initial reports showed "extensive damage" to the network and that some customers were not expected to have power restored until "well into tomorrow".

Mr Coomber said about 120,000 lightning strikes were recorded.

"Obviously some of those lightning strikes unfortunately hit our equipment and have caused lots of damage as well," he said.

The SES had 300 tasks in Logan on Wednesday night, responding to people trapped in cars and houses.

A number of schools are expected to be closed on Thursday.

Flash flooding was reported on multiple roads around Bahrs Scrub, Belmont, Gumdale, Loganholme, Logan Reserve, Logan Village, Rochedale, Stockleigh and Wellington Point.

The Bureau of Meteorology reported a wind gust of 96 km/h was recorded at Brisbane Airport just after 5pm.

Almost 80mm of rain was recorded at Wishart, in Brisbane's south, over a 30-minute period.

Floodwaters entered this bus as it travelled from the city to Victoria Point. (Supplied: Alleah Newman)

75mm of rain was recorded in 30 minutes at Chandler and Leslie Harrison Dam.

At Canungra in the Scenic Rim, 2cm hailstones were observed.

The wild weather took a toll on public transport and Translink has warned of delays of up to one hour on the Beenleigh lines and half-hour delays on the Cleveland, Ferny Grove and Shorncliffe lines.

Bureau meteorologist Harry Clarke said the dangerous storm had now moved out to sea.

The majority of the storm damage was concentrated on suburbs in Logan. (Supplied: Nicholas Thompson)

He said the wind was the "primary factor" in the storms.

"It missed our official wind observation stations unfortunately but no doubt some gusts over 100 km/h based on some of the damage we've seen."

A severe thunderstorm warning for destructive winds, giant hailstones and heavy rainfall was issued by the bureau on Wednesday afternoon.

Storm damage at Chambers Flat in Logan.  (Supplied: Sarah Haskmann)

The bureau said several severe storm cells had developed across south-east Queensland, with areas including the Brisbane CBD, Buperngary, Caboolture, Kilcoy and Mount Tamborine expected to see storm activity.

Areas that could be affected over the next hour include Cleveland, Victoria Point, Ormiston, Peel Island and Brisbane Airport.

Hailstones at Jimboomba (Supplied: Justin Jackie)

A spokesperson for Brisbane Airport said one inbound flight from Sydney to Brisbane had been diverted to the Gold Coast due to storm activity.

The spokesperson said delays and cancellations are expected and advised passengers to check with their airline for updates.

The weather bureau has predicted further storm activity on Thursday.

Mr Clarke said the focus will likely be further inland.

"Tomorrow afternoon we're likely to see storms kick off out towards the Scenic Rim, Lockyer Valley and the Ipswich area. They will struggle to make it to the coast."

Marnus Labuschagne is back in Shield action for Queensland. (Getty Images: Bradley Kanaris)

Marnus Labuschagne's return to first-class cricket following his axing from the Test team lasted 36 balls for Queensland in the Sheffield Shield on Wednesday.

Labuschagne made 12 runs before nicking off to Tasmania's Jake Doran off the bowling of Riley Meredith.

The 32-year-old's dismissal looked similar to so many of his recent failings at Test level, prodding on fourth stump without a hint of foot movement.

Ordinarily Sheffield Shield games retain some semblance of importance for Test players searching for form ahead of The Summer of Cricket.

Uniquely for Queensland's captain, this match means nothing — at least in the short-term.

He's already been flung on the Test scrap heap, a dire run of form eventually hastening his demise from an Australian Test team that crushed England in last year's Ashes, but has won just two of its last five Tests against Bangladesh and South Africa, without claiming a series victory.

Spectators didn't mind that though, and more than a handful had turned out to show support to their beleaguered skipper.

Those who arrived on time had to wait an hour and 20 minutes before Labuschagne came to the crease after Angus Lovell (18 off 60 balls) edged Beau Webster into the slips. The opener furiously smacked his bat after doing so much of the hard work on a pitch that offered plenty of zip.

Labuschagne's arrival was greeted with warm applause, the clapping briefly drowning out the incessant jackhammering of the building sites around the Gabba.

"Come on Marnus," one punter among the hundred or so faithful called out as he took his mark.

Marnus Labuschagne lasted 36 balls in his first return to the crease since South Africa. (Getty Images: Bradley Kanaris)

Labuschagne wasted no time in getting into the thick of the action, crushing a square drive for four off the very first ball he faced from former Test teammate Webster.

A streaky edge past third slip off the bowling of Jackson Bird though, reiterated that Labuschagne's rebuild could be a process as drawn out as the redevelopment around the ground.

As good as his opening salvo was, the idiosyncrasies that all too often verged towards idiocies during his faltering stays in the middle during Test matches, were still there.

There was a wave of his hands here, a period of shadow-batting there that were as prevalent at the Gabba as they were in Gqeberha, where he scored 14 and 39 in Australia's innings defeat.

As Bell got closer to the off-stump, Labuschagne's leaves became ever more flamboyant, a batting matador daring the bull to crash into his stumps.

He lasted until lunch, walking off with eight runs to his name.

His demise came soon after the break when edged a delivery he didn't need to play at into the gloves of the keeper.

Labuschagne waited a moment at the crease, miffed at his dismissal, before trudging off.

Fortunately for him, it was far from a bumper day of scores around the country.

Sam Konstas scored 24 and Kurtis Patterson a duck for New South Wales as they were bundled out for 204 against South Australia, while Marcus Harris managed just 15 on an MCG pitch that looked good for batting, given Peter Handscomb's century for Victoria.

It is far too soon after his return from South Africa to rectify any wrongs in his technique or banish the demons residing within his head.

As much as the hammering taking place outside the Gabba, the work to build Labuschagne back into a principle Test batter will take time.

Finnish Ambassador Arto Haapea has welcomed the explosion of interest in their Instagram page. (Supplied: Embassy of Finland to Australia)

In recent days, the Finnish Embassy has become something of a meme, but its ambassador does not mind at all.

"As long as it's positive and good and brings us more visibility to the work we do to bring Australia and Finland closer," Arto Haapea said.

It all began when Mr Haapea fronted a video promoting a campaign encouraging singles to enter a competition where they could travel to the Nordic country and dine with others looking to date.

Then, three days later, the embassy published another more hum-drum post informing the community it would be closed for a day for a team planning event.

Each post now has about 80 million views, according to the ambassador, far surpassing anything the embassy has seen before on its Instagram page.

Reaction to the first video was understandable to embassy staff — the somewhat tongue-in-cheek reel included lines such as "maybe the problem is not you, maybe it's your postcode".

"You've tried Tinder, you've tried Bumble, but have you tried Helsinki?" Mr Haapea asks in the video.

But responses to the second post about the embassy's temporary closure took things to another level.

"Bad day to be a Finnish embassy in Canberra enthusiast," one person commented.

"There go my plans," said another.

More notable commenters included the official Canberra Raiders account, which simply said: "Bugger".

And travel company Contiki added its own thoughts, saying: "day's ruined now, cheers".

Finland's embassy in the Czech Republic also chimed in:

"For anyone affected by this closure, the Embassy of Finland in Prague will be open as usual tomorrow."

Mr Haapea said the team was amused by the reaction to the closure for their planning day, but their initial focus was work.

"We were all gathered outside of Canberra for a planning day with the team, and we just basically started laughing because we saw the memes and we thought they were hilarious," he said.

"We decided just to carry on obviously with the planning day agenda, because we had lots of things to plan and sort of talk about with the team for next year."

He said 99 per cent of the online interaction had been positive and he hoped it would encourage people to visit their country, while also continuing to strengthen the relationship between Finland and Australia.

A post by Special Adviser to the Prime Minister of Finland Matias Pajula responding to the closure at the Australian embassy. (Instagram)

He said the goal was to "help more people discover Finland and know about Finland, be curious about what Finland has to offer".

The reasoning behind the singles campaign was to promote Finland's cuisine, Mr Haapea said.

The Finns eat a diet similar to that eaten in Tasmania, he said, including plenty of salmon.

"The Finnish cuisine is quite innovative these days. It's not what it used to be maybe 20 years ago," he said.

"It's not like everyone has to walk out of Finland with a ring on their finger or a partner that they have found, quite the contrary.

"The whole model is that they will have group dinners, so there will be eight international guests and two Finnish singles. So, it's more about getting to know people and enjoying the food and the company."

And, while an image circulating online that appears to show a huge queue of people outside the embassy is AI-generated, Mr Haapea said the interest in the embassy was not entirely a red herring.

In addition to the overwhelming online response, some people are indeed stopping by.

"We've had small groups of visitors, like three or four or five at a time, and they've been just taking pictures," he said.

https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-11/w.author: Keane Bourke
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-11/w.text:
BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Topic:
State and Territory Government

Colleagues shield WA Labor MP Jags Krishnan from media in extraordinary scenes (ABC News)

A group of WA Labor MPs have attempted to shield one of their own from answering questions from the media in extraordinary scenes outside state parliament.

Questions about the business dealings of Riverton MP Jags Krishnan and his disclosures to parliament about his debts have been growing since it emerged he was being sued in the United States over a million-dollar loan.

He has vowed to "vigorously defend" his position and launched a defamation case in response.

Jags Krishnan was blocked by his colleagues from answering journalists' questions. (ABC News: Andrew O'Connor)

Journalists tried to ask the second-term MP questions as he arrived at parliament on Wednesday but were blocked by a group of colleagues including Terry Healy and David Scaife.

Terry Healy blocked media from Dr Krishnan outside parliament.  (ABC News: Andrew O'Connor)

Mr Healy stood between the under-pressure MP and the media at one stage.

"It's all getting sorted," Dr Krishnan said as upper house Labor MPs Pierre Yang and Kate Doust walked close by.

A Western Australian MP embroiled in a legal dispute over a million-dollar loan in the United States insists everything he did was above board.

"Sorry guys, this is our workplace," Mr Scaife said.

"This is outrageous."

Asked if he would make a statement, Dr Krishnan said "not at the moment, when all is settled I will make a statement", which he said would happen in "a couple of weeks".

Dr Krishnan then appeared to be pulled into the building by Mr Yang before Mr Healy again stood in front of the cameras.

Mr Scaife then yelled to the media "you should be ashamed of yourselves" from inside the building.

Opposition Leader Basil Zempilas said Mr Scaife's comments were out of line.

"It would seem to me that the member for Cockburn has suggested the men and women of the press doing their job are a disgrace for doing their job," he said.

"The member for Cockburn should have a long, hard think about how things operate in here and around this space."

Basil Zempilas has taken a swipe at the group of Labor MPs.  (ABC News: Keane Bourke)

Mr Zempilas described the incident as "one of the most extraordinary things I have ever seen" and said the premier and Dr Krishnan needed to address the issue publicly.

"This government, for far too long, have done as they have pleased. Now, when questions are being asked, they don't like it," he said.

When asked about the incident, Premier Roger Cook said he could not provide answers about “how members of parliament choose to conduct themselves going into or out of parliament”.

He said he did not believe Dr Krishnan needed to provide an explanation of his business dealings to the parliament.

WA Premier Roger Cook said there was no need for Dr Krishnan to explain his business dealings to parliament. (ABC News: Nicolas Perpitch)

“Members of parliament, through their own private undertakings, have these issues all the time," he said.

“And Dr Jags has undertaken to meet all the requirements ... for members of parliament to one, be transparent, and two, to assure the people of Western Australia that these issues do not interfere with their obligations and duties.”

https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-11/w.author: Stephanie Richards
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-11/w.text:
BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

By Stephanie Richards

Topic:
Local Government

Adelaide Oval Number 2, also known as the "Village Green" is located on the western side of the stadium. (ABC News: Daniel Taylor)

The state government has accused the Adelaide City Council of stifling events, after it voted to change a community land management plan for the "Village Green" in the Adelaide Oval precinct.

But the council said it had approved “everything" the Stadium Management Authority (SMA) had requested.

The SMA says additional restrictions would make it harder to host events at the venue.

A bitter feud between the South Australian government and Adelaide City Council has escalated, with the state's premier accusing the local government of "complete madness" over a decision to change event restrictions near Adelaide Oval.

The latest dispute threatens to further strain an already fractious relationship between the two levels of government, amid simmering tensions over the controversial North Adelaide Golf Course and MotoGP circuit developments in the parklands.

It also follows consecutive days of barbed attacks from SA Premier Peter Malinauskas and his ministers towards other levels of government, including criticisms of the federal government over a shortage of aged care beds, and a plan to ban councils from issuing ticketless parking fines.

The Village Green is a marquee hospitality precinct set-up by the Stadium Management Authority on the western side of Adelaide Oval.  (ABC News)

On Wednesday, Mr Malinauskas accused the city council of "stifling" the city and "repelling people away", after it voted to change a community land management plan for Adelaide Oval Number 2, also known as "The Village Green".

The council voted to allow events to be hosted at the site for a maximum six days each year — not including on days Adelaide Oval is in use.

It also voted not to allow events to run for more than three consecutive days, and to retain the 15,000-person attendance limit — which could be reviewed on application to the council.

According to Lord Mayor Jane Lomax-Smith, the council last night approved "everything the Stadium [Management] Authority asked for".

"If the Stadium [Management] Authority have made a mistake and they now don't want us to make the changes they specifically asked for, I think they need to communicate with us in a better way," she said.

But Mr Malinauskas said the council had a "well-established reputation of knocking back opportunities" and, under the revised plan, the local government retained the power to approve or reject events at Adelaide Oval Number 2.

He also raised concerns about the cap of six days of events each year.

"It is complete madness," he said.

"They (the council) say they're in favour of major events but at the first opportunity restrict them and stifle them.

Jane Lomax-Smith said the Adelaide City Council approved "everything" the Stadium Management Authority requested. (ABC News: Daniel Taylor)

Stadium Management Authority (SMA) chairperson Jamie Briggs said he was "surprised and very frustrated" the council had added "additional restrictions" to the land management plan, which he said would make it harder for the authority to host events at Adelaide Oval Number 2.

He said the SMA was speaking to the state government about how the council's decision could be repealed, arguing the requirement to seek prior council approval to hold events of more than 15,000 people at the site could deter event promoters.

"You're just not going to get promoters that are willing to take that chance that a city council chamber will be able to vote an event down," he said.

Jamie Briggs said additional restrictions may deter promoters applying to hold events at the Adelaide Oval. (ABC News: Daniel Taylor)

Adelaide city councillor Phil Martin said the requirement to seek council approval for events of more than 15,000 was in place to ensure council could "manage the roads, make sure there are enough rubbish bins, make sure there is enough toilets".

"It is about event management, not about frustration," he said.

Cr Martin said the state government had never previously asked to host more than six days of events at Adelaide Oval Number 2.

"If the government wants more than six days, ask and you shall receive," he said.

"This is a council that actually loves events.

Peter Malinauskas described the Adelaide City Council's approval of a maximum six additional days for events at Adelaide Oval Number 2 as "madness". (ABC News: Daniel Taylor)

The argument follows a separate Adelaide City Council decision to rescind a motion to ban fossil fuel advertising on council assets.

The state government previously argued the motion could have affected Australia's biggest cycling event, the Tour Down Under, whose major sponsor is gas giant Santos.

"The ludicrousness, the insanity of their [the council's] position is that last night, they decided to repeal the decision to ban sponsorships from South Australian companies like Santos, but then on the same night made a decision to stifle activity at Adelaide Oval," Mr Malinauskas said.

Asked if he was laying the groundwork for putting the council into administration, Mr Malinauskas said: "It's not about putting the council into administration, it's about having a council that sees a bigger picture".

https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-11/j.author: Sandy Powell
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-11/j.text:
BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Hellyer Metals is one of six companies that owned the Hellyer gold mine. (Supplied: Hellyer)

The liquidator of a company that part-owned a Tasmanian gold mine has been removed from the role by a federal judge, who said the man had failed to properly investigate the company's transactions.

Liam Bailey was removed as Hellyer Metals' liquidator on Tuesday.

Hellyer Metals is being pursued in court for damages totalling more than $36 million over a failed business deal.

A federal judge has fired the liquidator of Hellyer Metals, which part-owned a north-west Tasmanian gold mine, saying he failed in his duties and behaved in "objectively concerning" ways.

The decision comes 12 months after the Tasmanian government ordered the Hellyer Gold Mine be shut down temporarily over unpaid debts, which occurred at about the time a "highly questionable" transaction was made from Hellyer Metals to an associated company, Celestial Group.

At the same time, Hellyer Metals was being pursued in court by resources company Goshawk Mining and investment firm Saxby Capital for damages totalling more than $36 million over a failed business deal.

The Hellyer mine and tailings dam in Tasmania's north-west. (Google Earth)

On Tuesday, federal court Justice Shaun McElwaine removed Hellyer Metals liquidator Liam Bailey and ordered him to hand over all relevant records to Adam Johnston, who he appointed in Mr Bailey’s stead.

Justice McElwaine said "very real" questions on Mr Bailey's impartiality had been raised, and that along with his lack of action since his appointment in January, it was clear "a new liquidator with a laser-like focus" was required.

In a lengthy decision, Justice McElwaine detailed a complex timeline over recent years that resulted in Hellyer Metals entering voluntary administration in January this year and appointing Mr Bailey as liquidator.

Justice McElwaine said at that time Hellyer Metals had recently conducted the transaction in question, after which Goshawk Mining obtained a Supreme Court order freezing $36.4 million worth of assets in Hellyer's associated companies.

He said, in the following months, Mr Bailey failed to properly investigate the company he was liquidating and the circumstances of the transaction, despite having access to voluminous records and financial resources.

The former bosses of Hellyer mine, in Tasmania's north-west, have been ordered to repay a combined $8.5 million in allegedly misappropriated funds after failing to set aside a bankruptcy ruling.

Justice McElwaine said the plaintiffs, Goshawk Mining and Saxby Capital, sought the federal court's intervention and Mr Bailey's removal as they had lost confidence in him and his impartiality.

Mr Bailey submitted to the court that no proper cause for his removal had been shown, but Justice McElwaine disagreed.

"He was spurred into action because of it."

Topic:
Emergency Services

Justice McElwaine also criticised Mr Bailey's decision-making in choosing a lawyer known to Hellyer Metals to represent him in this case.

He also said Mr Bailey provided a draft of his statutory report of the liquidation to Hellyer's directors.

"These are the very people intimately involved in the transaction," the judge said.

The state government issued Hellyer gold mine a three-week stop-work order in October 2025, over alleged compliance failures and unpaid mining royalties. (Supplied: www.hellyermetals.com.au)

Justice McElwaine said a "reasonable liquidator … would have acted with more haste".

"For more than eight months Liam Bailey has had the benefit of a detailed analysis of the transaction … which manifestly warranted urgent investigation," he said.

Judge McElwaine said a "reasonable liquidator … would have acted with more haste". (Supplied: im-mining.com)

Justice McElwaine said removal of a liquidator is a discretion "not lightly exercised", but in these circumstances Mr Bailey's removal was "justified, indeed required".

"The liquidation of Hellyer Metals is still at an early stage, despite Liam Bailey's appointment on January 22, 2026.

"A new liquidator with a laser-like focus on the need to thoroughly and quickly investigate the transaction with adequate funding is in the best interests of the administration."

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.title: Nintendo sells 5.2 million copies of ‘Zelda’ remake in four days
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.author: Vlad Savov
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.text:
Nintendo sold 5.2 million copies of its “The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time” remake in just four days, invigorating the Switch 2 platform that had been waiting for a blockbuster hit.

Released on Nov. 5 for $59.99, the 2026 edition is a complete recreation of the 1998 classic action-adventure game for the Nintendo 64 console, replete with new graphics, level and character designs. It ranks among the best-reviewed video games of recent times, earning a score of 96 out of 100 from both players and professional reviewers on aggregator Metacritic.

The Switch 2 console has had an uneven first year on the market, challenged by the rising cost of memory pushing hardware prices up. The fast start by the new “Ocarina of Time” takes the Zelda game past the cumulative sales of “Donkey Kong Bananza,” another popular title from 2025. Only “Mario Kart World,” which was part of a launch bundle with the Switch 2 console, has sold more units so far.

The first Switch, released in 2017, got a huge boost from having “The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild” as a launch-day title that helped draw in gamers from outside the Nintendo ecosystem. Though a remake, the new “Ocarina of Time” may have a similar effect as Nintendo heads into the crucial holiday season.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.title: Nissan pares car sales forecast on tougher China competition
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.author: Nicholas Takahashi
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.text:
Nissan lowered its annual car sales outlook due to weak demand and mounting competition in China, where buyers are shifting to locally made electric vehicles faster than it expected.

The Japanese manufacturer now projects at most 3 million vehicle deliveries this year, from 3.15 million previously, it said Wednesday. Nissan reported second-quarter operating profit that came in significantly below analyst expectations.

“China remains our biggest challenge,” Chief Executive Officer Ivan Espinosa told reporters in Yokohama.

The results show how far the embattled Japanese carmaker still has to go in its efforts to come back from its worst financial crisis. Nissan has started a broad cost-cutting campaign that includes cutting jobs and shutting down factories. But it still faces sizeable debt obligations and is struggling to compete with the industry’s shift toward EVs with complex software, particularly in China.

Nissan’s sales in the world’s biggest car market fell 15% during the first half of the fiscal year. The company is looking to turn things around by adding more EVs and plug-in hybrid cars to its lineup, some of which will be exported to other markets.

Business was better elsewhere. Deliveries increased 6.3% in Japan and 2.1% in North America — regions where the shift to EVs is happening at a slower pace.

Nissan’s operating profit came in at ¥2.12 billion ($13.3 million) for the three months through September. That’s well below the ¥49.3 billion projected by analysts. The company maintained its full-year financial forecast on expectations that profitability will improve in the second half due to new models and higher sales volumes.

Nissan will announce a new business strategy in February that will go beyond its current restructuring plan, Espinosa said.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.summary: Nissan's sales in the world's biggest car market fell 15% during the first half of the fiscal year. The company is looking to turn things around by adding more EVs and plug-in hybrid cars to its lineup.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.title: Exiled Cambodian opposition leader urges Japan to aid democracy
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
Sam Rainsy, a Cambodian opposition leader currently living in exile in France, called on Japan to provide support for democracy in his country.

In a recent interview in Tokyo, Rainsy criticized former Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Sen, 74, and his family for establishing a “dictatorship” in the Southeast Asian nation.

Rainsy said that he asks “the Japanese government to help consolidate democracy in Cambodia, because Japan is a model of democracy in Asia.”

After serving as prime minister for 38 years, Hun Sen stepped down and handed the position to his son, Hun Manet, in 2023. Since then, however, Hun Sen has filled influential positions and currently serves as president of Cambodia’s Senate.

In recent years, the Cambodian government has taken an authoritarian approach to suppress anti-government forces, resulting in the dissolution of the Cambodia National Rescue Party, the country’s largest opposition party, in 2017. Rainsy once served as head of the party.

Rainsy said that he was visiting Japan to inform the Japanese government and lawmakers of Cambodia’s current situation.

Democracy in Japan is “deep-rooted,” with the country having the “most stable democracy in Asia,” he said.

“Japan is a model ... at least for Asia, to ensure that there is respect for human rights, respect for the fundamental freedoms and respect for the democratic principles,” he said.

In October last year, Rainsy announced the establishment of a so-called independent government in Paris. “We conduct our activities to express the will of the Cambodian people inside Cambodia,” he said.

“The main objective is to ... give hope to the Cambodian people,” he said.

“You don’t trust (and) you don’t believe in the current government in the country, but there is a government in exile outside which represents you,” he said. “We give them an alternative.”
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.summary: Sam Rainsy, a Cambodian opposition leader, is currently living in exile in France. He says he is visiting Japan to inform the Japanese government and lawmakers of Cambodia’s current situation. He calls on Japan to help consolidate democracy in Cambodia.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.title: Japan, eight others get fossil award over leaders skipping climate talks
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
ANTALYA, TURKEY – An international nongovernment environmental group on Tuesday gave Japan and eight other countries its Fossil of the Day award for inadequate climate action, citing their leaders’ failure to attend the ongoing U.N. climate talks in Turkey.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is absent from the two-day leaders’ meeting of the climate talks through Thursday for scheduling reasons, marking the third straight year that a Japanese prime minister has skipped the summit.

From the Group of Seven countries, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is the only leader expected to attend the summit.

The Climate Action Network said that the absence of the leaders from the meeting could delay the progress of negotiations and raise concerns that climate change measures would be put on the back burner.

The fossil award will be presented daily until the conference ends on Nov. 20.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/202.title: ‘Three Millimeters to You’: A hokey but heartfelt tale of cross-cultural first love
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/202.author: James Hadfield
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/202.text:
Teenagers in the first flush of love can do the darnedest things. Tatsuhiko (Soya Kurokawa) is an unambitious high schooler living in a sleepy coastal town in Kyushu, southern Japan, who falls hard for visiting South Korean exchange student Yoon-seul (Kim Ji-an).

They embark on a tentative courtship, only for her to suddenly get whisked back to her native Busan after parting on less-than-amicable terms. Determined to make amends in person, Tatsuhiko pulls out a ruler and measures a map in his textbook to determine the distance between their respective homes: just three millimeters! He initially tries to swim it, then elects to take the ferry instead.

Yes, we’re firmly in seishun eiga (youth film) territory, a genre in which no expression of adoration is too ridiculous, as long as it doesn’t involve the characters getting past first base.

“Three Millimeters to You” leans into the conventions of the genre, yet this international co-production still represents a risky commercial proposition — and not only because of its cross-border romance. It’s based on an original screenplay by first-time feature director Chun Jin-rung, rather than pre-existing IP, while neither of the leads comes from an idol group with a built-in fanbase.

Chun, a third-generation Zainichi (ethnic Korean living in Japan), even has the audacity to bring up the historical grievances between the two countries, although these play a less central role than in his earlier short, “Minwoo and Rie” (which took top prize at the Yamagata International Movie Festival in 2022).

After Yoon-seul reveals that her grandmother once worked in the mines in Tatsuhiko’s hometown, she’s upset to learn that he knows nothing about Japan’s colonial rule of the Korean Peninsula during the first half of the 20th century. (“I always sleep during history class,” he offers, lamely.)

The film doesn’t dwell on the subject, instead giving its hero a chance to redeem himself. Tatsuhiko’s subsequent trip to Busan, armed with little but a phrasebook and Google Translate, shows that he’s open-minded and willing to learn. He even manages to charm Yoon-seul’s uptight, workaholic mother (“Parasite” star Jang Hye-jin).

As Tatsuhiko, Kurokawa confirms the promise he showed in Hirokazu Koreeda’s “Monster” (2023) and Lee Sang-il’s “Kokuho” (2025), playing the character without a trace of affectation (and with age-appropriate zits). Kim is endearing as Yoon-seul, at least when cinematographer Lim Won-geun isn’t trying to make her look like she’s been airbrushed. Her Japanese dialogue is also pitched at a level that’s just about believable, even if I’m not sure a new arrival would be so quick to understand the thick Kyushu dialect.

Chun’s storytelling can be slipshod at times, giving the impression that he hasn’t figured out the best way to get where he wants to go. Big moments come out of nowhere: After Tatsuhiko goes on a lengthy adventure trying to find Yoon-seul in Busan, she just kind of shows up. The film’s aesthetic is also wildly inconsistent, wobbling between slice-of-life naturalness and attempts at hyperreal stylization that mostly fall flat.

There’s room for more than a few millimeters of improvement, then, but the performances and the film’s good-natured sweetness ultimately carry the day. Chun genuinely seems to think that it’s possible to bridge cultural differences if we just try. By the time the credits roll, you may believe it, too.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/202.summary: Tatsuhiko (Soya Kurokawa) is an unambitious high schooler living in Kyushu, southern Japan. He falls hard for South Korean exchange student Yoon-seul (Kim Ji-an) He is determined to make amends in person, but he ends up in Busan.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.title: Japan Supreme Court rules 2025 election was held in unconstitutional state
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
The Supreme Court ruled Wednesday that the July 2025 Upper House election was conducted in an “unconstitutional state” due to vote-value disparities of up to 3.13.

The top court’s Grand Bench, presided over by Chief Justice Yukihiko Imasaki, issued the ruling on a total of 16 lawsuits filed by two groups of lawyers seeking to invalidate the election across the country. It dismissed requests to invalidate the election.

Imasaki said that the maximum disparity in the election was at a level that raises constitutional concerns. The ruling was backed by 10 of the 15 justices, while the other five found the 2025 election to be constitutional.

This is the first time the top court has found an Upper House election with a maximum vote-value gap of less than 4.00 to be held in an unconstitutional state. The court last recognized such a state for an Upper House election in 2013, when the maximum disparity was 4.77.

The 2025 election was held under the same framework as the previous poll in 2022. However, the maximum disparity rose to 3.13 from 3.03.

Prior to the top court’s decision, high court rulings were split on the lawsuits, with 11 finding the election to be in an unconstitutional state and five finding it constitutional.

The sequel to the 2023 smash hit “Godzilla Minus One,” Takashi Yamazaki’s “Godzilla Minus Zero” had a Nov. 3 domestic opening as thunderous as the titular monster trampling a Tokyo street: ¥910 million ($5.75 million) from 590,000 admissions, a first-day box office record for a live-action film in Japan.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/community/2.title: As JET Programme turns 40, alumni and ministers stress its importance in age of AI
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/community/2.author: Jessica Speed
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/community/2.text:
Japan celebrated the 40th year of its flagship international exchange program this month, marking four decades of a project that has brought young people from around the world into Japanese classrooms and communities.

The Japan Exchange and Teaching Programme, more commonly referred to as JET, was launched in 1987 to promote foreign-language education and grassroots cultural exchanges, and has grown from an initiative involving 848 participants from four countries into one of the world’s largest international exchange programs.

However, the program is facing mounting pressure in recent years as translation work dries up due to the proliferation of artificial intelligence and as a weak yen makes Japan a less attractive destination for prospective participants.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.author: Cecilia D'anastasio
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.text:
Yang Liu’s parents planted roots in suburban Michigan hoping their son, who was born in China, would find success in the world’s biggest economy. In early 2020, they got their wish: End Game Interactive, the mobile game startup he co-founded in their home, raised $3 million on the back of breakout hit “Zombs Royale.”

Then, the U.S. still commanded a major slice of what’s now a $121 billion global industry thanks to games like “Temple Run,” “Plants vs Zombies” and “Pokemon Go.” But now, Liu is one of a generation of American game designers despairing as Chinese studios churn out games that are faster, cheaper and able to extract more spending from players. Operating costs in the U.S. are now so high that Liu is building out his business in Latin America, where he employs more than 40 people.

“It’s extraordinarily hard for startups like ours — despite having an incredible amount of capital — to find individuals to compete on the global stage, which gaming has become in the past 10 years; and one in which the U.S. is no longer the dominant force,” Liu said.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
A western intelligence estimate says Iran can build about 50 ballistic missiles per month — roughly half its prewar capacity — providing a formidable means of retaliation if hostilities resume, despite months of airstrikes.

The U.S. has said since the early days of the war that Tehran’s arsenal, and its ability to reconstitute it, had been thoroughly degraded. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth reiterated that in remarks on Tuesday, saying 80% of Iran’s industrial base had been destroyed.

Iran’s conventional military has largely been wiped out by U.S. and Israeli airstrikes. But it most likely has at least 1,700 ballistic missiles remaining and is building more at roughly half the rate possible before the war, according to a western official citing military intelligence reports. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps — the most powerful wing of Iran’s military — also released footage on Tuesday of what it described as the unveiling of a new underground “missile city.”

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/environment.title: Disaster warning systems race to keep pace with galloping climate risks
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/environment.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/environment.text:
LIMA/KATHMANDU/ANTALYA, TURKEY – Twice a day during the rainy season, Raquel Izarra climbs to the roof of her home in the eastern Lima suburb of Santa Ines Bajo and measures how much rain has fallen using a homemade gauge, before sending the data to the authorities using WhatsApp.

Together with more than 60 other volunteers, she is trying to ensure her community will have time to prepare should heavy rains trigger flooding and mudslides in the low-income area, as they did in 2017.

“Every year the rainfall situation has been getting worse,” Izarra said. “Now, with this, we feel safer.

“We know that when it rains for more than, I don’t know, three, four or five days and it maintains a certain level, that means that the ravine above is going to give way, the ravine is going to activate. That means we start giving warnings.”

Global warming has increased the risk of extreme weather events and equipping communities such as Izarra’s to cope will be one of the debates at the COP31 talks in Turkey, which end on November 20.

A draft U.N. report seen by Reuters, which measured progress across risk knowledge; detection, monitoring and forecasting; warning dissemination; and preparedness and response, found gaps remained, especially around operational readiness and financing.

The head of the U.N.’s Office for Disaster Risk Reduction said a 2027 target of full coverage for everybody was unlikely to be met.

More than two-thirds, or 136, of countries, have some early warning capacity. That represents a 143% increase since reporting began in 2015, but still only 64 of them had capability across all four pillars, the report found.

Data from the Lloyd’s Register Foundation’s World Risk Poll cited in the U.N. report also showed that in low-income and lower-middle-income countries, fewer than half of those warned were able to act on the warning compared with three-quarters in upper-middle-income countries.

Of people surveyed in 2025 who said they had experienced a disaster in the previous five years, 80% had received at least one warning, the poll found, but the distribution varied. In East Asia, 95% of people had been warned, compared with 47% in Central and Western Africa.

James Kinyangi, head of Climate and Policy at the African Development Bank, said the extra investment required in Africa ranged between $5 billion and $10 billion. He said the bank was working with more than 30 countries to develop systems, but more than 20 others needed financial and technical support to build infrastructure, capacity and early-warning services.

The U.N. report said 38 countries have fully operational cell-broadcast warning systems and another 17 are in the final stages of developing them. It said $500 million would be enough to extend coverage to every country and maintain it for three years.

A rock and ice avalanche and flood in Nepal in August that left thousands of people dead, injured or missing and caused almost $3 billion in damages showed that all systems have their limits.

Monsoon flood warning systems were in place, but the scale and speed of a torrent caused by the collapse of a glacier meant many people were swept away before they could transmit data to trigger warnings.

Phone call warnings from those further up the valley helped to save some lives, though, including at the Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School after headmaster Rajendra Dawadi decided to evacuate 900 pupils.

“We had no official alerts. If we had waited for the official alert we would all be killed. I would not be able to speak with you now,” Dawadi said.

In Peru, home to the world’s largest number of tropical glacial lakes, including 528 considered at risk of overflowing, real-time monitoring was crucial, said Paola Moschella, head of glacier research at the National Institute for Research on Glaciers and Mountain Ecosystems.

“Information is updated minute by minute because in these types of events, if a debris flow begins, authorities need to evacuate people immediately, as the response window is only 15 to 20 minutes,” she said in the aftermath of the Nepal flood.

The U.N. report said more support was needed for community preparedness. In Lima, Raquel Izarra said help to cover basic costs was especially necessary in poorer areas, where even paying the monthly phone bill — vital to almost any warning system — can be difficult.

“Sometimes people stop monitoring for economic reasons because they have to work to support themselves and their families,” she said.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.title: Man arrested over theft of watch that was returned days later to Tokyo mall
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
A 30-year-old man was arrested Wednesday on suspicion of stealing a luxury wristwatch — which was sent back to the shop days later — at the Nakano Broadway shopping complex in Tokyo, according to investigative sources.

The theft occurred on Oct. 29 at a watch shop on the third floor of the complex in Nakano Ward. The suspect allegedly tried on a luxury Audemars Piguet watch worth ¥46 million ($290,000) and fled with it.

The suspect was believed to have taken a bullet train from Tokyo Station following the incident and headed west, NHK reported.

The Metropolitan Police Department investigating the case located the man in Nagoya and apprehended him.

He has largely admitted to the allegation, telling investigators, “When I tried on the watch, I looked at myself in the mirror and really liked how it looked. Before I knew it, I had walked out of the store wearing it.”

The stolen wristwatch was returned to the store via a delivery service on Nov. 1, accompanied by a handwritten note of apology. He reportedly told police that he was the one who had sent the wristwatch.

After checking its serial number, the shop’s staff confirmed that it was indeed the stolen item.

The package had been sent from Aichi Prefecture. A name and address were also written on the package, but police believed the information to be false.

In a separate incident at the same shopping complex in August, four luxury watches with a combined retail value of about ¥200 million were stolen from another shop on the first floor. Two Chilean nationals were arrested on suspicion of theft in connection with the incident and subsequently indicted.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.summary: The 30-year-old man was arrested Wednesday on suspicion of stealing a luxury wristwatch. The watch was sent back to the shop days later, according to investigative sources. The suspect allegedly tried on a luxury Audemars Piguet watch worth ¥46 million ($290,000) and fled with it.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.title: Thailand to raise arsenic-tainted rivers in talks with Myanmar
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
Thailand will seek urgent action from Myanmar over suspected mining pollution in cross-border rivers after arsenic levels surged to as much as 30 times the Thai standard, threatening drinking water and farmland in the country’s north.

Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow will raise pollution in the Kok, Sai and Ruak rivers when he meets Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing in Naypyidaw on Thursday, Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said. Myanmar officials weren’t immediately available to comment.

While Thai authorities have yet to identify the source of the latest arsenic spike, officials suspect the contamination is from upstream mining in Myanmar’s Shan State, where environmental groups have alleged Chinese companies operate diggings. The problem is particularly difficult to tackle because the rivers cross borders, and some of the suspected mines lie in areas beyond the Myanmar government’s full control.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.summary: Arson levels in Thai rivers are 30 times the Thai standard. The problem is particularly difficult to tackle because the rivers cross borders. Officials suspect the contamination is from upstream mining in Myanmar’s Shan State.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.title: Behind Bangladesh’s garment boom, workers cut food and healthcare as wages fall short
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: Ruma Paul
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
GAZIPUR, BANGLADESH – Before dawn each day, garment worker Shilpi Khatun cooks over a wood-fired clay stove because her family cannot afford gas, before heading to a factory in Gazipur, an industrial hub on the outskirts of Dhaka.

The 27-year-old is the sole breadwinner in a household where her husband is unemployed and her parents and in-laws depend on her wages.

Rising prices have left Khatun struggling to afford basic necessities despite five years in the garment industry, a frustration shared by thousands of Bangladesh’s garment workers who staged protests last week demanding the minimum monthly wage be raised to 30,000 taka ($242.82) from 12,500 taka.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.summary: Shilpi Khatun is the sole breadwinner in a household where her husband is unemployed. The 27-year-old is struggling to afford basic necessities despite five years in the garment industry.

One obvious difficulty with assessing the first three days of any Grand Sumo Tournament is that the sample size is too small to conclude much beyond “rikishi A looks good, and rikishi B doesn’t.”

A hot start puts a wrestler on the front foot, of course, but with four-fifths of a basho remaining most outcomes are still possible.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.title: Opposition presses for consumption tax cut details as Upper House debate begins
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: Kenji Yoshida
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
As the Upper House opened debate Wednesday on a bill to cut the consumption tax on food, opposition lawmakers pressed Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on how much shoppers would actually save and who would qualify for income-linked cash payments.

The bill would lower the consumption tax on food and nonalcoholic beverages from 8% to 1% for two years starting in April 2027. Income-linked cash payments for low- and middle-income workers would begin that fiscal year only to offset the 1% and take on an envisaged fuller form of support when the tax rate returns to 8%, with no set end date. The bill leaves the eligible income cutoffs and payment amounts up to a Cabinet order.

The Lower House passed the bill last week, despite opposition objections.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.summary: The Lower House passed the bill last week, despite opposition objections. The bill would lower the consumption tax on food and nonalcoholic beverages from 8% to 1% for two years starting in April 2027.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/202.text:
Publishing house Kodansha launched a new manga label Wednesday focused on creating fictional comic renditions of historical and reported content in an appeal to adult readers who are increasingly moving away from traditional books.

“Kaqreal” aims to bridge the reportage background of Kodansha’s preexisting news media imprints Weekly Gendai and Friday and the company’s historic strength in manga as the publisher of internationally acclaimed series like “Attack on Titan,” “Akira,” “Pretty Guardian Sailor Moon,” and “Blue Lock.”

“We want to connect with new readers through the messaging of journalism and the empathy that manga offers,” said Kaqreal chief editor Toshihiro Tsuchiya.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.title: EU to make addictive app features easier to switch off
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.text:
BRUSSELS – The European Union will on Wednesday unveil new rules to crack down on influencer marketing, ban online features that trick Europeans and force platforms to give users the right to turn off “addictive” features.

The EU already has a raft of laws covering data protection, artificial intelligence and online content but Brussels and campaigners argue there are gaps that leave consumers exposed to harmful digital practices.

The bloc’s executive will unveil a much-needed update of consumer rules dubbed the “Digital Fairness Act” (DFA) that will give it the power to slap fines on companies of up to 6% of their annual turnover in large-scale cases.
