https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/11/nvidia-j.title: Analysis: Jensen Huang’s exit tests Nvidia’s role as the ‘central bank of AI’
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/11/nvidia-j.author: Matt Peterson
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/11/nvidia-j.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday follow revelations that he had extramarital affairs.

Nvidia has made substantial financial commitments to AI infrastructure companies, including cloud-service purchases and project guarantees.

The Federal Reserve and other financial institutions are examining how leverage and interconnected financing could amplify an AI downturn.

Financial experts distinguish potential losses for technology investors from the more serious risk of losses spreading through banks and credit markets.

Nvidia
 CEO Jensen Huang’s shock resignation is raising a worrying question: Could trouble at the chipmaker spread through the tightly connected financial network Nvidia has built to support the artificial intelligence boom?

Serious problems with Nvidia could do far-reaching economic and financial damage. The company has made hundreds of billions of dollars in financial commitments to other firms to help the industry grow, earning it the nickname the “central bank of AI.” The Federal Reserve and other financial institutions are closely watching the AI buildout to monitor for the possibility that an unexpected event could destabilize the global financial system.

Even back in July Fed officials were discussing the possibility of a “broad-based repricing of assets” in the event of problems in the AI sector.

A rerun of the 2007-2008 financial crisis isn’t likely, according to analysts and current and former financial officials. Nvidia isn’t “too big to fail in a bank sense at all,” said Sheila Bair, a former government regulator who ran the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. Unlike a troubled bank, Nvidia isn’t vulnerable to a sudden loss of confidence and would still produce a product customers want to buy even if something went wrong. And its massive equity gives it a cushion.

But regulators need to watch carefully for exposure by the banks and the wider financial system to Nvidia and other firms like it, Bair said.

“Nvidia going down would be a pretty seismic event,” she said.

Investors still have high hopes for Nvidia, which reports earnings on Tuesday. Analysts expect its revenue to more than double in the current fiscal year, and then to roughly double again over the following two years, according to LSEG data. But Huang’s exit from the company Thursday following a pair of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman The New York Times reported was suspected of spying for China, makes the company’s fate extraordinarily hard to predict. Huang had led the company since co-founding it in 1993.

Nvidia didn’t respond to a request for comment. The company named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO.

Nvidia’s stock fell 33% from its Oct. 6 peak through Thursday morning. Still, people who closely track the financial flows underlying AI say that even sharper losses by Nvidia likely wouldn’t trigger the kind of systemic problems that regulators guard against.

And yet the risks flowing from AI are keeping some finance officials up at night. They are watching for the possibility that many of the factors that have helped the AI boom could reverse simultaneously. If the value of Nvidia’s GPU chips fell, for instance, it could prompt investors to ask whether companies that borrowed money to buy them would be able to pay off their debts.

In that case, the financial assistance big tech firms have extended to others in the industry could suddenly become drags on their growth. Tech companies would have credit problems at the same time that their equity is falling. Problems among giant tech firms wouldn’t stay contained to tech investors’ portfolios, but could cause problems across the economy.

“I think that’s a real concern because both the economy and financial markets are standing on the same leg, which means a drawdown could have reinforcing effects between the two,” said Jason Wu, an assistant director at the International Monetary Fund who oversees the Global Markets Analysis unit.

Wu was the lead author of a chapter of the IMF’s Global Financial Stability report published in October that warned about the potential for growing leverage among AI firms and investors to trigger broader problems. The so-called hyperscalers — the biggest tech firms — have grown from just 1% of bond issuance in the $15 trillion investment-grade debt market to 10% in just two years. Hedge funds and retail investors are making risky bets even riskier by taking on debt to buy stocks or investing in funds that have embedded leverage.

Nvidia is at the center of all of that. The company has repeatedly stepped in to help backstop smaller AI companies known as neoclouds, which build data centers using Nvidia chips and lease capacity to other firms. Among other obligations, Nvidia disclosed in July that it has committed to buy up to $36 billion in cloud services from those companies. That helps Nvidia ensure that there will be more customers for its AI chips, and it helps those companies find easier financing.

Wu and others refer to these kinds of arrangements as circular financing. When business is growing, it can be productive for bigger firms to help their customers buy their products. But if Nvidia couldn’t honor its obligations, it would ripple through the firms that borrowed the money and the banks that lent to it. Relatively opaque private credit funds have also lent heavily into the AI boom, and how they would fare is a subject of debate among regulators.

Nvidia didn’t reveal its specific partners, but some neoclouds such as CoreWeave and IREN have separately disclosed their relationships with the bigger firm.

Many neoclouds have been under stress in recent weeks. The cost of insuring CoreWeave debt, as measured by credit-default spreads, rose by 94% — nearly doubling — from Oct. 1 to Nov. 5, before settling, according to LSEG data. The price of an IREN convertible bond maturing in 2029 fell 23% from Nov. 3 to Nov. 5, amid a 26% decline in the company’s share price.

Nvidia’s other obligations include a $105 billion phased guarantee to a major data center project in Ohio planned by OpenAI and SB Energy, subject to certain conditions. Nvidia promised to backstop up to $125 billion of a $500 billion credit program by Wall Street financial firms.

These obligations come in different forms and are unlikely to come due all at once, if ever. Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh, a Columbia Business School finance professor, estimates them at $400 billion overall.

That is a huge sum, but still a small fraction of the roughly $3.9 trillion market capitalization Nvidia has even after its stock decline. “The company would have to get to the brink of extinction before all these guarantees come into jeopardy.”

“I don’t want to say it’s a safe system, but I do want to say there’s a lot of equity in the system right now,” Van Nieuwerburgh said.

But in the past few days, Nvidia’s troubles have separated it from the pack. Most neoclouds’ equity prices have recovered this week as Nvidia’s share price has fallen. That suggests investors see Nvidia’s problems as specific to the company, for now.

Meanwhile the basic laws of economics are driving other firms to try to move into Nvidia’s lucrative chips business. AMD
, Broadcom
, Intel
, Google
, Microsoft
, and OpenAI all have efforts underway to build their own AI chips, Van Nieuwerburgh said.

Over time, they could replace Nvidia’s products. That could cap the economic fallout of any potential troubles at the company.

And yet it’s impossible to entirely write off the financial risks of the AI trade suddenly hitting a wall, added Van Nieuwerburgh, who spoke to me over Zoom from the sidelines of a bimonthly meeting of finance officials in Basel, Switzerland.

Central bankers “are clearly very, very, very anxious about this and thinking hard about these questions,” he said.

https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/jensen-h.title: ‘A dark day for Nvidia’: Here’s what analysts have been saying about Jensen Huang’s departure
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/jensen-h.author: Liz Napolitano,Chloe Taylor
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/jensen-h.text:
Global markets reacted to news of Jensen Huang’s resignation from his role as CEO of Nvidia.

The company’s board convened Wednesday evening after reports emerged of Huang engaging in a second extramarital affair, this time with an employee.

Before the decision, one analyst said Huang was “toast,” while another described the developments as “a dark day for Nvidia.”

Nvidia
 investors are preparing for a future without Jensen Huang after the CEO’s resignation was announced on Thursday.

Markets were on tenterhooks ahead of the decision amid reports that the chip giant’s board had convened to discuss his future with the company. By the time of the announcement, at least six analysts had downgraded the stock between Wednesday night and Thursday morning.

The New York Times on Wednesday reported that Huang had engaged in a second extramarital affair with an employee. The CEO was already under scrutiny after Huang admitted to having a romantic relationship with a woman U.S. intelligence believes is a Chinese spy.

Nvidia announced on Thursday morning that, following a board meeting, Huang would step down after more than 30 years at the company’s helm.

CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO.

Those downgrading the stock included longtime Nvidia bull Ben Reitzes of Melius Research.

Nvidia shares were seen down more than 12% shortly after the open on Wall Street, bringing losses for the last month close to 25%.

Here’s what analysts and investors are saying about the company and the stock.

Reitzes changed his rating for Nvidia to hold from buy. His price target is now $185 — down from $315 — is 6% above the level at which shares last closed.

“We thought we had experience, but nothing prepares you for what has happened at Nvidia over the last few weeks - and especially since Saturday. The only situation remotely close to this we can recall was HP in 2010. Waiting to see what that Board would do (and who they would hire) that time didn’t work out. It was really cheap, too, at ~9x EPS right after its initial swoon. Nvidia is a much stronger, more important company, but its market moves far faster, and this story touches geopolitical flashpoints. In this unique crisis, we have decided (reluctantly) to step aside on Nvidia (now a Hold) after recommending it since we launched our AI platform coverage universe in July 2023,” he said.

Analyst Mark Lipacis downgraded Nvidia to in line from outperform. He also lowered his price target on shares to $186 from $465, implying 7% upside from Wednesday’s close.

“The Wall Street Journal reported Nvidia’s Board was ‘preparing to oust’ its CEO after he had two extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The NY Times reported that Nvidia’s Board hired law firm Wachtell Lipton to lead an investigation into the matter. While Nvidia’s Board said that it ‘has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised,’ we believe that the investigation will take time and we expect NVDA’s P/E multiple will continue to compress consistent with our ‘Late-Innings of the Semi Cycle’ thesis, especially since Nvidia has no obvious succession plan or number 2 operational executive,” he said.

William Blair’s Sebastien Naji downgraded Nvidia to market perform from outperform.

“After a head-spinning week of news and allegations around CEO Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s board is reportedly preparing to remove him, according to the Wall Street Journal. The full story will take time to emerge and may require several investigations, including the board’s own independent probe and a requested U.S. House briefing. What is already clear is that Huang’s likely departure and heightened scrutiny of the company will be a significant overhang on NVDA shares in the near term. Meanwhile, the potential for a slower AI buildout and more intense competition from other chipmakers will only add to execution risk...governance and regulatory pressure, the potential for more serious fallout, and a sudden change in management are likely to muddle both execution and sentiment. As a result, we are downgrading NVDA to Market Perform and will wait for the dust to settle before reassessing,” he said.

Analyst Rick Schafer downgraded the AI stock to perform from outperform.

“We are downgrading shares of NVDA and removing our price target following reports (WSJ, NYT) of founding CEO Jensen Huang’s imminent departure amidst allegations of a 2nd extramarital affair. Credible media reports circulated Wednesday evening that NVDA’s board is preparing to part ways with Huang following a widely reported relationship with an alleged Chinese spy compounded by new allegations of a relationship with an NVDA executive. This ‘one-two’ punch appears to have forced the board’s hand...While we see upside to the F3Q (Oct.) print and F4Q (Jan.) outlook, we expect fundamentals to take a backseat near term. The departure of Mr. Huang could, in our view, translate to a lingering share overhang,” he said.

Analyst Stacy Rasgon slashed his price target from $400 and downgraded the stock from market outperform.

“So now what? On the positive, the fundamentals of the business (if not the leadership) are
clearly still intact with numbers that remain massive (and probably still headed higher). We don’t think the company should have huge issues operating while engaged in a search for new leadership. And (of course) the shares are almost absurdly cheap (and getting cheaper as we speak); clearly there is a lot of bad news getting priced in here,” he said.

“On the other hand, we find it hard to advocate stepping in here in size as there will no doubt be more allegations to come (there is a trope that says if you find two ants in your kitchen the best estimate of the total number of ants in your kitchen is not two...), both from internal issues as well as headlines related to the business, new governmental investigations etc. Adding on the new variable of who will take the reins (internal? external?) and anything else they may or may not uncover creates additional uncertainty (and we can’t even begin to speculate as to who they might find to fill Jensen’s shoes),” he added.

Analyst John Vinh downgraded the stock from overweight.

“We believe Huang’s departure represents a material increase in strategic, organizational, and execution risk that warrants a higher risk premium and lower valuation multiple for the stock. While we expect core fundamentals to remain strong for the foreseeable future, we believe it will be challenging for NVDA to find a successor with the same leadership and strategic vision as Huang,” he said.

“In our view the writing is on the wall that Jensen’s days at Nvidia could be numbered and we would expect this to be a very fluid situation over the next 48 hours,” renowned tech bull Dan Ives said in a note overnight.

“Jensen has created a black eye moment for himself and Nvidia and now has created a spider web of complexity that Wall Street, Silicon Valley, DC, and the global tech ecosystem are trying to figure out what is next.”

“We believe Nvidia’s value is $300 per share with Jensen as CEO and $225 per share without Jensen as CEO,” Ives added.

“The stock will clearly be under pressure with this fluid news but the reality is its a dark day for Nvidia, but the company will navigate this turmoil and get through to the other side and remain a core foundational piece of the AI Revolution.”

Citi analysts said overnight that they had trimmed their target price for Nvidia to $225, down from $285.

“If Jensen were forced out, it would mark the end of an era,” Malik and Sylla said in their note.

“Under his leadership, Nvidia became the dominant force in AI infrastructure, the primary beneficiary of the global AI spending cycle, and one of the world’s most valuable companies. A leadership transition creates an overhang on the stock given his central role in strategy, product vision, customer relationships, and investor confidence.”

They said Nvidia CFO Colette Kress could serve as interim CEO while the board evaluates external candidates.

“As much as there is a lesson here for Nvidia around corporate governance, around key man risk… the reality is there is still 40,000 other employees at Nvidia, and there is some real talent there, and I have no doubt that there are some executors within Nvidia that the board will be able to tap to execute on their existing plans and continue to manage the company,” Nathan Thooft, the firm’s CIO, told CNBC’s “Squawk Box Asia” on Thursday.

“I think the bigger risk is the foresight in the next several years, where Nvidia was driven by a lot of the mindset and thoughts that come out of their CEO, and if he’s no longer there they’re going to have to find that replacement.”

“You can’t deny the board has done a horrible job of succession planning,” Greifeld told CNBC’s “Morning Call” on Thursday.

“What the board has to find out in the next days or weeks is, did Jensen lie to them? Right? Did he lie to them repeatedly on different topics? We don’t know. Does he lose their trust basically on lying to them over the years? I’m sure the board would love to keep Jensen in place in some role. Right, his value to the company is quite large.”

Greifeld said he does not see a premium in Nvidia stock, noting that it trades at a low multiple “so there’s no bubble to burst here with respect to the valuation.”

“If there’s a new CEO in, they don’t have to make any decisions day one, day 30, day 60. They have time to really get their footing and come up with their own strategic vision,” he told CNBC. “You’re not going to change what is in the development plan for chips that exists today. So I think certainly it would be a loss, but given the nature of the business and the long lead time for these chip developments and the long contractual relationships they have with customers, it would give them certainly room to maneuver.”

CIO Richard Reyle told CNBC’s “Squawk Box Asia” that Nvidia’s board had painted themselves into a corner by not having any kind of succession plan in place.

“I’ve heard him compared to Steve Jobs being removed from Apple, but [Jobs] put in place a succession plan and cultivated and groomed Tim Cook for years, so that when he passed away and [Cook] took over, there was a real leader there,” he said. “Right now, Nvidia doesn’t have that person in place, so it’s going to be a choice of keeping Jensen and being faced with … all kinds of interrogations, or they’re going to have to move on from him, and that’s just going to make the stock uninvestable. That doesn’t make the AI trade uninvestable, but it certainly makes Nvidia uninvestable.”

Reyle said he saw the stock moving “lower and much lower from here.”

“There’s no obvious [replacement] there that can step right in and take over, so they may kind of try to ride this out and retain him,” he said. “But there’s going to be a lot of difficulty in doing so because he’s going to become something of a liability.”

“NVIDIA upheaval puts tech concentration risks in focus,” Mark Haefele, global wealth management chief investment officer at UBS, and his team said on Thursday morning.

“Without taking any views on individual companies, the episode reinforces the importance of investment diversification and selectivity as the AI trade matures. We retain our conviction in AI’s long-term potential, with compute demand remaining robust and earnings resilient. But elevated expectations and potentially wide differences in company outcomes can leave concentrated portfolios exposed to company-specific setbacks.”

“Jensen Huang is toast,” Bill Blain, founder and principal, said in his morning newsletter. “Nvidia’s dependence on Jensen Huang is now exposed as a major market risk. The dominant firm within the AI industry lacks clear succession planning and Huang was seen as the acceptable face of AI by the public.”

“Confidence in the AI sector has been wobbling for months,” he added. “Huang’s departure could lead to instability and trigger another collapse.”

The company's board convened Wednesday evening after reports emerged of Huang engaging in a second extramarital affair with an employee. Nvidia shares were seen down more than 12% shortly after the open on Wall Street.

https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/inside-j.title: Jensen and Lori Huang's Nvidia fortune is jointly controlled. How that makes things complicated now that he's resigned
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/inside-j.author: Hayley Cuccinello,Robert Frank
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/inside-j.text:
A version of this article appeared in CNBC’s Inside Wealth newsletter, a weekly guide to the high-net-worth investor and consumer. Sign up to receive future editions straight to your inbox.

Jensen Huang’s $140 billion stake in Nvidia is largely held by trusts that are co-owned with his wife, Lori, creating added uncertainty for the shares and his financial future following his resignation from the company, according to attorneys and SEC filings.

Huang and his wife jointly own about 800 million Nvidia shares worth roughly $135 billion through a complex web of trusts and LLCs created for tax and estate planning purposes, according to SEC filings. Jensen Huang directly owns about 70 million shares valued at about $12 billion.

While owning company stock through a trust is common among tech founders and CEOs, it’s less typical for a founder to have equal ownership with a spouse, tax experts say. The arrangement further complicates Huang’s sudden exit from the company, but could prove to be a stabilizing force for the shares, since the trusts make it more difficult for either Huang or his wife to quickly sell.

“Each of Mr. Huang and his wife may be deemed to have shared beneficial ownership of, and to exercise shared voting and investment power over,” according to an SEC filing.

According to the filings, Jensen and Lori Huang own about 530 million shares as co-trustees of the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Living Trust, created in 1995. They’re also co-trustees of the Huang 2012 Irrevocable Trust, which owns 31.4 million shares, and the Huang Irrevocable Remainder Trust, which owns 109 million shares. About 135 million shares are held by LLCs that have the Living Trust as the sole member, according to the filings.

Lori Huang is the president of the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation, which owns 69 million shares and reported $9 billion in net assets in 2024, according to IRS filings.

Each of the trust structures serves different tax or estate purposes, according to trust and estate attorneys. The living trust is likely a revocable marital trust, since it was created 10 years after the Huangs married and two years after Nvidia was founded in 1993.  Attorneys say living trusts help couples avoid the potentially expensive and public probate process  when one spouse dies. Many couples, for example, create living trusts for homes they purchase or other assets.

The main tax benefit of living trusts is that when one spouse dies, the surviving spouse gets a step-up in basis for the entire trust’s assets, rather than just their half, according to attorneys.

While the rules of each living trust vary, attorneys say shares in the living trust can typically be sold or divided fairly easily in the case of a divorce.

“It’s like a joint checking account,” said Kathleen Martone, partner at Varnum LLP.

While the revocable trust would typically allow each of them to sell their shares, lawyers said it is common for executives or their trusts to have agreements with the company limiting the sale or transfer of shares to prevent large-scale liquidation.

“In the event they divide shares in their revocable trust, there’s probably transfer restrictions. He may have to hold them for her benefit, and she would get the monetary benefit of the shares but not voting or management rights,” said Leslie Evans, partner at Withers. “He could retain the stock while Lori receives other assets or an equalization payment.”

The more complicated structures used by the Huangs, and the ones with the largest tax benefits, are the irrevocable trusts. The SEC filings state that “Mr Huang and his wife are co-trustees” of both trusts. With an irrevocable trust, the creator transfers ownership of an asset into the trust and the terms can’t be changed without the consent of the beneficiaries or a court.

Attorneys say the 2012 irrevocable trust is likely an “intentionally defective grantor trust,” a type of irrevocable trust where the creator gifts assets but is still treated by the IRS as the owner of the property for income tax purposes.

The structure allows the creator to lend money to the trust to buy the shares, as well as pay income taxes for the trust when it earns money. The result — an unlimited gift to the trust that escapes the estate tax.

What’s more, the trust can avoid capital gains taxes on any appreciation of the shares in the trust.

“The trust principal is staying high, my own taxable personal assets are being used to pay the tax, and I’m able to funnel more and more money into the trust,” said Azriel Baer, trust and estates partner at Farrell Fritz, P.C. in New York.

Their other irrevocable trust, the “Huang Irrevocable Remainder Trust,” was likely created for the benefit of their children.

By definition, the trustees and terms of an irrevocable trust are difficult to change. Since Jensen Huang and Lori Huang are both co-trustees, neither can likely remove or sell the Nvidia shares held by the trust, experts say.

“An irrevocable trust is its own entity that has its own operational provisions, and so it has some estate and asset protection planning,” Martone said. “Theoretically an irrevocable trust would be protected from a divorcing spouse as a creditor.”

Of course, the protections all depend on the terms of the trust, attorneys say. Whether an irrevocable trust can be changed or “decanted” in legal parlance depends in part on state law. California, where the Huangs live, is strict when it comes to changing irrevocable trusts.

For Nvidia shareholders, the irrevocable trusts could provide stability for the shares, since it would be difficult for either Jensen or Lori Huang to remove the shares from the trust and sell them.

Attorneys say it’s unlikely the Huangs would change a trust created for the benefit of their children.

“If (the trusts) are for benefit for kids, there’s no reason to pull them back into their estate,” said Rochelle Schultz, shareholder at Weinstock Manion.

https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/nebius-q.title: Nebius falls 16% as company expects increased 2026 capex spend, issues weak outlook
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/nebius-q.author: Jordan Novet
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/nebius-q.text:
Nebius’ earnings report comes after fellow neoclouds IREN and CoreWeave showed better-than-expected results in the past week.

The companies’ stocks have bounced back this week after a brutal past month that reflected concerns about a slowdown in the AI buildout.

Nvidia, which invests across the neocloud space, is creating added volatility due to the crisis surrounding CEO Jensen Huang.

Nebius
 shares sank 16% on Thursday as one of the biggest publicly traded neoclouds reported third-quarter revenue that beat analysts’ estimates, but issued disappointing guidance.

Here’s how the company performed relative to LSEG consensus:

It was not immediately clear if the loss per share was comparable to the 69 cents expected by analysts.

Revenue jumped 571% in the quarter, according to a statement. The company reported a net loss of $37.5 million, a loss of 13 cents per share, compared with $119.6 million, a loss of 50 cents per share, a year earlier.

The stock move also comes amid the resignation of Nvidia
 CEO Jensen Huang, after stinging revelations about multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

Nvidia, which has developed the neocloud market by investing in the companies and backstopping some of their projects, held about $329 million in Nebius shares at the end of June, according to a filing.

In a letter to shareholders, CEO Arkady Volozh said the company expects fiscal year 2026 revenue at the low end of the company’s $3 billion to 3.4 billion range. FactSet expected full-year revenue of $3.35 billion.

Nebius also shared an initial outlook for 2027, expecting revenue of $12 billion to $13 billion, “reflecting a conservative approach to the pace of our build-out.” FactSet expected 2027 revenue of $12.09 billion.

The company expects FY2026 capital expenditures of $27 billion, higher than its previous capex guidance of $20 billion to $25 billion and the FactSet expectation of $23.85 billion.

Nebius’ expected FY2027 capex of $40 billion to $45 billion came in much higher than the FactSet expectation of $28.77 billion.

Nebius’ results come after fellow neoclouds CoreWeave and IREN reported better-than-expected financials in their earnings announcements over the past week. That’s provided a boost to the companies’ stocks, which had suffered steep selloffs in recent weeks on concern about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence buildout.

The neocloud companies posted a robust rally on Wednesday, with Coreweave booming nearly 25%, Nebius climbing 15%, Applied Digital rising more than 7% and IREN adding nearly 6%.

Each of the stocks fell Thursday premarket after the Nebius Q3 report.

Last week, CoreWeave’s
 bond yields spiked past the 16% mark. In its earnings report on Tuesday, CoreWeave told analysts it expects to keep parent-level debt financing under $5 billion through 2027. During the quarter, Nebius said it raised $5.75 billion in debt financing.

The political backdrop has created further volatility as Nebius races rivals to open up new data centers. Last week U.S. voters supported dozens of ballot initiatives to restrict the development of such facilities, while Democrats won sweeping victories in both houses of Congress.

Executives will discuss the results with analysts and issue guidance on a conference call starting at 8 a.m. ET.

https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/scout-mo.title: Scout Motors has 212,000 vehicle reservations as $2 billion South Carolina plant nears completion
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/scout-mo.author: Michael Wayland
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/scout-mo.text:
Scout Motors has roughly 212,000 reservations for its Terra pickup and Traveler SUV, CEO Scott Keogh told CNBC.

Construction of Scout’s more than $2 billion South Carolina Production Center is in its final phase.

Keogh said roughly 87% of reservations are for extended-range models and about 75% are for the Traveler SUV.

BLYTHEWOOD, S.C. — Electric vehicle startup Scout Motors has notched roughly 212,000 reservations for its upcoming EVs as the company nears completion of its new $2 billion plant in South Carolina, CEO Scott Keogh told CNBC.

The reservations are for the Volkswagen-backed company’s Terra pickup truck and Traveler SUV, which are expected to start full production next year before deliveries begin to customers in 2028.

Reservations do not necessarily translate to sales, as the U.S. automotive industry has learned during the past decade, especially with highly anticipated all-electric trucks such as the Ford
 F-150 Lightning, Tesla
 Cybertruck and others that garnered strong interest that didn’t lead to meaningful numbers of purchases.

Keogh said he expects Scout could roughly double those reservations by the time customer production begins, but he said the more important thing is to convert early interest into actual sales as production nears.

“It’s been a consistent drumbeat,” Keogh said during an interview at Scout’s plant site outside Columbia, South Carolina. “I think we could easily be up over 400,000 with reservations without doing too much effort. The big thing for us is how much of the initial production can we 100% presell.”

Keogh said achieving an order book of 12-to-18 months “would be great” and something he thinks the company can do before production. Scout on Thursday said construction is “in its final phase.”

Scout’s vehicles will be offered as all-electric versions as well as electric hybrid variants, known as extended-range electric vehicles, or EREVs, that include an engine as a backup generator for the electric motors and batteries.

Scout, a former American vehicle brand from 1961 to 1980, was expected to exclusively offer EVs in a bid for the German automaker to expand its presence in the U.S. However, slower-than-expected adoption of EVs and higher costs led the company to decide to offer EREVs as well.

Keogh said the EREVs and SUV are dominating reservations thus far, with roughly 87% choosing EREV models and 75% being SUVs.

The CEO also said the company is drawing interest from its target markets, which include owners of off-road vehicles such as the Ford Bronco and Jeep Wrangler as well as full-size pickup trucks and U.S. EV leader Tesla

Given the interest signaled by reservations, Keogh said the company is expected to launch with the EREVs first, followed by the EVs. He also said the company plans to launch with mid-level models first, a deviation from many companies that begin with their highest-priced models.

Both the Traveler and Terra are expected to start under $60,000. The EREV models are expected to feature more than 500 miles of range, according to the company, compared with 300 miles of range for the all-electric models.

“The No.1 thing for me is I want to go get the best volume as soon as possible,” Keogh said. “In my mind, it’s how quick can you get to 100,000 units? It’s at 100,000 units where you can start to punch through.”

His comments come months after Rivian Automotive
 received criticism online for launching its R2 SUV with its highest-priced models first, despite that being a common practice across the automotive industry.

Keogh said Scout’s South Carolina plant is about 85% complete, but supporting infrastructure and a $300 million supplier park continue to be installed.

Reservations for Scout’s vehicles initially opened in October 2024, when it revealed the Traveler and Terra, which feature sleek, yet rugged, exterior appearances that pay some homage to the brand’s historic models.
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/scout-mo.summary: Scout Motors CEO Scott Keogh says roughly 87% of reservations are for extended-range models. The company's Terra pickup truck and Traveler SUV are expected to start full production next year before deliveries begin to customers in 2028.

https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/star-war.title: Disney's 'Star Wars' is coming to Cosm domes ahead of 50th anniversary as part of multiyear film deal
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/star-war.author: Sarah Whitten
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/star-war.text:
Cosm has partnered with Disney on a multiyear, multifilm deal that will kick off with “Star Wars: A New Hope” early next year.

This is Cosm’s third studio deal — it already has partnerships with Universal and Warner Bros. — and sixth theatrical release.

Cosm is working directly with studios Lucasfilm and Industrial Light and Magic as well as creative studio MakeMake to create the visuals and the sound mixing for a unique presentation of the film.

The Force is strong with Cosm.

On Thursday, the immersive entertainment technology company announced a new studio partnership with The Walt Disney Company
 that will bring the original “Star Wars” to its domes early next year as part of a multiyear, multifilm collaboration.

The financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

Cosm’s massive concave screens will drop film fans into a galaxy far, far away starting in March, just ahead of the Academy Award-winning film’s 50th anniversary in May.

“We are thrilled to add the Disney partnership,” Alexis Scalice, head of Cosm Studios, told CNBC. “We do look for those opportunities of these like anniversary and commemorative moments. We look for those opportunities to celebrate with the fans, but also find this mutually beneficial partnership between both parties.”

This will be Cosm’s sixth theatrical collaboration with Hollywood, having already partnered with Warner Bros.
 to bring “The Matrix,” “Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory,” “Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone” and “It” to its locations. The company is set to launch immersive screenings of Universal’s
 “Shrek” in December.

Each Cosm dome has stadium-style seating, with booths and tables set on each level. The dome’s width fills much of the viewers’ periphery, giving the sensation that they are part of the onscreen environment.

In this case, “Star Wars” will be displayed in a large rectangle in the center of the dome while the background is transformed into the iconic planets of Tatooine and Yavin IV that are featured in the film as well as the infamous Death Star. Audiences will also see elements that will make it appear like they’re traveling at lightspeed and getting trapped in an intergalactic trash compactor.

Cosm is working directly with studios Lucasfilm and Industrial Light and Magic as well as creative studio MakeMake to create the visuals and the sound mixing for the unique presentation of the film.

“We look for those moments where sound, music ... listening to Darth Vader’s breath for the first time ... you feel those moments differently in an 87-foot diameter dome and 12k resolution with the sound system we have,” Scalise said. “And it’s one of the things that with experiential cinema and our technology that we were so excited and honestly privileged that we can take these defining moments for fans and work closely with our partners that doesn’t really change the authenticity of it, it just enhances it in a different manner.”

The premium experience will also be paired with a themed menu. Cosm has done this with other titles, such as “Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone,” serving guests throughout the screening with house-made shepherd’s pie, pretzel wands with cheese dip and a box of Bertie Bott’s Every Flavour Beans.

Cosm is trying to establish itself as a destination for fandom — both for sports and for film. It has a wide variety of live event offerings, which it telecasts using proprietary cameras mounted in arenas that broadcast back to the dome, as well as its expanding library of movies.

“What I love is that we really are kind of building these Cosm communities built on fandom,” Scalise said. “It’s the No. 1 foundation for our business.”

And Star Wars is a powerful fandom. The franchise remains one of the top-ranking pieces of intellectual property across film, television and retail annually, and Disney is gearing up for a massive celebration of its semicentennial including merchandise launches, theatrical re-releases, its biannual Star Wars Celebration convention and collaborations with other brands.
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/star-war.summary: Cosm has partnered with Disney on a multiyear, multifilm deal that will kick off with ‘Star Wars: A New Hope’ early next year. This is Cosm’s third studio deal — it already has partnerships with Universal and Warner Bros.

https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/oil-pric.title: Oil prices mixed after Trump says no Iran deal needed: 'We've got their Strait'
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/oil-pric.author: Deena Zaidi,Fred Imbert
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/oil-pric.text:
U.S. oil prices were mixed Thursday, as comments from President Donald Trump stoked worries that an end to the U.S.-Iran war was not in sight.

Brent crude
 traded 1.1% higher at $93.73 per barrel. West Texas Intermediate futures
 were up just 0.3% at $86.76 per barrel.

“We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!” Trump said in a Truth Social post.

Thursday’s moves come as oil prices have been under pressure after comments from Trump following the U.S. midterm elections eased fears of further strikes on Iran. WTI is down 16% in November, and Brent has lost 20%.

Trump said Sunday that fresh attacks were highly unlikely as talks to end the conflict progressed, despite both ⁠countries reporting that shipping had been hit in or near the Strait of Hormuz. He also said further military action did not appear necessary “at this point,” easing concerns about prolonged disruptions to Middle East oil supplies.

John Kilduff, a partner at Again Capital, said investors may have been too quick to price in an end to the fighting.

“The market may have gotten ahead of itself on pricing in a cessation of hostilities,” Kilduff told CNBC. He warned that renewed doubts about a deal would push the security premium in oil prices higher.

Trump’s assertion that the U.S. controls the Strait of Hormuz could spur further Iranian attacks on shipping, increasing the risk of prolonged supply disruptions, according to Kilduff.

“The President may be thinking that given enough time, the economic blockade of Iran will force them to either negotiate with the USA or result in a regime change as the Iranian economy collapses. The Iranians might have different ideas and continue to attack Middle East Infrastructure that results in higher prices and forces the President to the negotiating table,” said Andy Lipow, president of Lipow Oil Associates.

“In any event, it does not seem to me that either side’s negotiating position has changed. Iran wants the blockade to end, sanctions to be lifted and a ceasefire including Lebanon to be declared. The USA wants Iran to get rid of its entire nuclear stockpile and allow free transit through the Strait of Hormuz,” he said.

—CNBC’s Pippa Stevens contributed to the report.
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/oil-pric.summary: President Donald Trump said Sunday that fresh attacks were highly unlikely as talks to end the conflict progressed. Trump said that the U.S. controls the Strait of Hormuz could spur further Iranian attacks on shipping.

https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/democrat.title: Unions helped Democrats win big in 2026. Now they want action
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/democrat.author: Alex Harring
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/democrat.text:
Unions spent millions of dollars and mobilized thousands of members to get out the vote for Democrats in the midterm election.

The CNBC Voter Poll showed a 22-point Democratic margin among union households in 2026, reversing a recent decline.

Labor leaders say they expect newly elected Democrats to act on affordability and workers rights if they want to keep their support in the future.

When Brody Rutledge wasn’t working 60-hour weeks or raising his four children this year, he was busy helping secure political victories for Democrats.

The 25-year-old was part of a group of Ohio union members who planned social-media blitzes in support of Amy Acton’s campaign for governor and Sherrod Brown’s effort to reclaim a Senate seat. On his lunch hour, during break times and after his kids went to sleep, the electrician helped create posts and videos to help raise the profiles of the two candidates among blue-collar voters.

The posts attracted more than 15,000 views.

Rutledge’s efforts paid off: Acton and Brown won their respective races, part of the blue wave that swept Democrats to power in Washington and in state houses across America — including in many states, like Ohio, that had been considered Republican-leaning, or reliably Republican.

“People are realizing that there needs to be a change,” Rutledge told CNBC. “We are extremely excited with the results.”

Rutledge was a part of what organized labor considered one of its biggest political efforts yet. Unions spent millions of dollars and mobilized thousands of members to get out the vote for Democrats in the midterm election. Now, they expect newly elected politicians to deliver.

Democrats, they say, need to get a handle on inflation, enact worker protections and deliver union jobs.

The AFL-CIO launched a seven-figure paid media campaign for the election and said its members since Labor Day had engaged with nearly 15 million voters. By the AFL-CIO’s count, more than 600 members of unions themselves were elected in the midterm, including dozens heading to Washington and hundreds who are bound for statehouses.

The CNBC Voter Poll shows midterm voters who were union members or lived in a union household went for Democrats over Republicans by a margin of 22 percentage points, the highest of the last four election cycles. That’s more than double the margin for the rest of the electorate: When looking at voters in non-union households, the gap shrunk to 10 percentage points.

“We are very proud of the impact that the labor movement made on this election,” said Liz Shuler, president of the AFL-CIO, a federation of unions that represents almost 15 million workers. “It was our biggest and boldest effort ever.”

In some cases, unions got involved before party nominees had been decided.

In Michigan, the United Auto Workers organized behind Democrat Abdul El-Sayed ahead of what became a contentious primary race for U.S. Senate that he eventually won against Haley Stevens. The union believes that about one out of every 10 early voters in the August primary were UAW members.

“It was incredibly impactful,” Connor Farrell, a progressive fundraiser who worked with El-Sayed, said of the UAW’s endorsement. “I’m not sure we would have won without them.”

El-Sayed and Jocelyn Benson — the Democratic nominee for Michigan governor, who also had early backing from the UAW — cruised to victory in last week’s general election. It was a sharp reversal for the Wolverine state, which backed President Donald Trump in 2016 and 2024.

The UAW held a rally on the eve of Election Day headlined by El-Sayed and Benson, along with other Democrats running for statewide office. The Detroit-based union said its volunteers knocked on more than 100,000 doors and made half a million phone calls for the election.

The CNBC Voter Poll showed union households made up about 22% of the electorate in Michigan in the 2026 midterm, above the 16% mean nationwide. Union households in Michigan broke for El-Sayed and Benson by higher-than-average margins of 25 and 27 points, respectively.

“There’s a direct correlation between a ballot box and a bread box,” said UAW President Shawn Fain, who described the union’s 2026 political efforts as the largest in his lifetime. “What we bargain for today can be taken away in the legislative halls tomorrow.”

In Nevada, another swing state, members of AFL-CIO unions canvassed for a list of candidates including Aaron Ford, the Democrat who unseated Republican Gov. Joe Lombardo. Down ballot, the AFL-CIO endorsed candidates in state assembly, mayoral and city council races.

Vladimir Ortega, a member of the National Association of Letter Carriers living in North Las Vegas, said displeasure with how Republicans had managed the economy led him to volunteer to canvas with the AFL-CIO for the first time. The 34-year-old met Ford and other candidates at political events, and he plans to volunteer for candidates backed by AFL-CIO again in 2028.

“People felt like they had to be there,” Ortega said. “Their money hurt, and they want to do something about it.”

For generations, union voters and their families were a core bloc of the Democratic base. But the party’s iron grip on organized labor had slipped in recent election cycles as union members, like other working-class voters, grew frustrated by high inflation and affordability challenges, according to Paul Clark, a Pennsylvania State University professor.

The National Election Pool’s Poll showed union households voted for Democrats by a margin of 16 and 15 percentage points in the 2020 and 2022 contests, respectively. That narrowed to just 8 points in 2024, when voters’ economic frustrations led Republicans to win a trifecta of power in Washington: the presidency and both houses of Congress.

The Teamsters declined to back either Trump or former Vice President Kamala Harris in 2024, snapping a long history of Democratic endorsements. The union, with more than one million members, said internal polling showed members preferred Trump over Harris.

Teamsters General President Sean O’Brien said on social media that he voted for Ashley Moody, the victorious Republican candidate for U.S. Senate in Florida, in the 2026 midterm. The Teamsters didn’t respond to a CNBC request for comment.

“Obviously, 2024 was very disappointing for unions and the American labor movement,” said Clark at Penn State, who has authored books on collective bargaining and organized labor. “That caused some introspection on the part of unions in terms of their political strategies and how they communicate with their members about politics.”

This time around, there appeared to be more excitement among card-carrying union members heading to the polls. AFL-CIO polling showed 83% of union voters were “very motivated” to vote, an increase of 10 points from the last midterm election in 2022.

Following their midterm defeat, Clark said he wouldn’t be surprised to see Republicans courting unions ahead of the 2028 presidential election. But that could be an uphill battle, given the party’s history of advocating for business interests over workers, Clark said.

Looking ahead, organized labor has big expectations for Democrats after helping the party to power in Washington and state capitols across the country.

In Ohio, Rutledge said that his International Brotherhood of Electric Workers chapter is focused on ensuring new data center construction projects use union labor. In Michigan, UAW President Fain said the union expects a majority-Democrat state legislature to approve a law guaranteeing unemployment insurance for striking workers.

“The days of just blindly giving our endorsements to people because of party affiliation are over,” Fain said. “They’re going to earn our support.”

If Democrats don’t act when they have legislative majorities in Washington, union leaders warn that they will pull their support in 2028 and beyond.

Across the nation, Shuler, the AFL-CIO president, said union voters went to the polls last week in hopes of enacting policy that will level the economic playing field. The CNBC Voter Poll found that 70% of respondents believed the U.S. economy favors the wealthy over the middle- and working class.

“Republican, Democrat, independent, we’ll be with you if you’re with us,” Shuler said. “It just so happens that we had a big wave of Democratic candidates who were talking about working-class issues.”
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/democrat.summary: The Teamsters declined to back either Trump or former Vice President Kamala Harris in 2024. The union, with more than one million members, said internal polling showed members preferred Trump over Harris.

https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/medical-.title: As credit card balances hit a record high, medical bills can become 'shadow debt,' expert says
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/medical-.author: Stephanie Dhue
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/medical-.text:
Medical bills can move onto credit cards and other forms of borrowing, making their medical origin harder to see in broader debt totals.

Collectively, Americans held a record $1.29 trillion in credit card debt in Q3 2026, according to the New York Fed.

Review medical bills for errors and ask providers about financial assistance before moving a balance onto a credit card or financing plan.

Total household debt rose $334 billion in the third quarter, to $19.1 trillion, according to new data from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. That total doesn’t include medical debt — at least, not directly.

An estimated $220 billion in medical debt exists, according to an analysis of 2021 federal survey data by KFF, a national nonprofit healthcare research group. But medical expenses can become hard-to-track “shadow” debt if consumers pay them with a credit card or other forms of borrowing, said Jim Triggs, the CEO of Money Management International, a nonprofit credit counseling organization.

“Technically, as soon as that consumer pays that debt off with another mechanism, now it becomes credit card debt, or housing debt, or whatever mechanism you used to pay it off,” Triggs said.

He said 20% of MMI’s debt and budget counseling clients in 2025 cited a medical hardship as the reason they went into debt.

Separately, about 17% of households surveyed in 2024 reported still owing money on a loan or credit card used to pay a medical bill, according to a 2025 study by researchers at the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.

Here’s a look at more stories on how to manage, grow and protect your money for the years ahead.

Americans’ credit card debt rose to a record $1.29 trillion in the third quarter, the New York Fed found, while home equity lines of credit saw their biggest quarterly jump since 2005, to $481 billion. Those increases come amid broader affordability pressures for consumers, including pricier everyday expenses amid persistent inflation.

It is “kind of hard to parse” how much of Americans’ debt load comes from medical expenses, said Julie Margetta Morgan, president of The Century Foundation, a New York-based progressive nonprofit think tank.

“There’s a big piece of medical debt that is about people being on high-deductible health plans, so they have insurance, but they’re still getting these big medical bills that they can’t pay,” Margetta Morgan said.

Nationwide, among households with medical debt, the median amount in collections is $1,492, according to the Urban Institute. The nonprofit research organization’s report drew the data from more than 10 million anonymized credit bureau records from August 2026.

Jessica Colon has used credit cards to pay medical debt. She and her husband were both self-employed at the time with a high-deductible health insurance plan. Colon, now 50, says the debt started with an unexpected $16,000 hospital bill for her son’s care in the mid-2010s.

“Because I could barely keep up with that payment, I kept charging on my credit card all my monthly payments, and that’s where it all compounded,” Colon said. “I was just drowning.”

The credit card debt grew to more than $45,000 before she turned to a nonprofit credit counselor, who negotiated lower rates and put together a five-year plan to pay it off. “It’s embarrassing, honestly, how much money was interest, and then of course you’re building the interest on the interest,” Colon said. She zeroed out that debt in early 2024.

Before taking on debt, experts advise reviewing medical bills and billing codes for errors, including duplicate charges.

Consumers should also ask medical providers if they offer assistance before signing up for a medical credit card, experts say. Many nonprofit hospitals are required by law to have a written financial assistance plan.

“A lot of nonprofit hospitals are not actually offering this plan to people, and in many cases, they’re offering them a medical credit card before they offer that financial assistance,” said Margetta Morgan, a former associate director of research, monitoring and regulations at the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.

Colon said she wishes she had tried to negotiate the medical bills before putting the balance on a high-interest credit card. “You don’t want to confront the place that’s helping your child. So I didn’t realize that I could do that,” she said.

https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/11/democrat.title: Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate election over incumbent Republican Hyde-Smith
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/11/democrat.author: Dan Mangan
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/11/democrat.text:
Democratic nominee Scott Colom won the Mississippi Senate election over Republican incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, the Associated Press reported.

Colom will be the first Black senator from Mississippi since the post-Civil War Reconstruction Era.

Democrats will have a majority of at least 55 seats in the Senate, having flipped at least eight seats from Republicans.

Alaska is the only remaining Senate election to be called.

Democratic nominee Scott Colom won the Mississippi Senate election over Republican incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, the Associated Press reported Wednesday.

Colom, a local district attorney, will be the first Black senator from Mississippi since the post-Civil War Reconstruction Era.

His projected victory — which was not considered likely by national analysts before Election Day — is the latest in a series of stunning wins by Democrats this midterm cycle.

Two sources close to Colom’s campaign said Hyde-Smith called him late Wednesday afternoon to concede.

“While this is not the outcome we worked for, or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters,” Hyde-Smith said in a video posted on X.

“I want to congratulate Scott Colom and wish him well as he takes on the tremendous responsibility of representing our great state,” Hyde-Smith said.

Democrats now will have a majority of at least 55 seats in the Senate, having flipped at least eight seats from Republicans.

Alaska is the only remaining Senate election to be called. In that state, Democratic nominee Mary Peltola, a former House member, has a narrow lead over Sen. Dan Sullivan, the Republican incumbent.

“Blue Mississippi is here,” Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., said in a post on X.

“Scott Colom is the only person who could’ve gotten this done. I knew it from the moment I met him,” Schumer wrote.

In addition to the Senate, Democrats have won more than enough seats to take control of the House of Representatives when the next Congress begins in January.

https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/11/canarx-o.title: Feds arrest top official of healthcare company, alleging illegal drug importation
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/11/canarx-o.author: Scott Zamost
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/11/canarx-o.text:
U.S. authorities are accusing the two top officials of a Canadian company of operating a long-running scheme to illegally import prescription drugs into the U.S., according to court records.

John Thomas Howard, treasurer and a director of the company, CANARX, was arrested Sunday on smuggling and conspiracy charges. His brother Bob Howard, CANARX president and director, is wanted in the investigation, according to records.

CANARX was featured in a CNBC investigation “RiskyRX” last year that revealed how the company and others known as alternative funding programs, or AFPs, are becoming more pervasive around the U.S. as drug costs skyrocket.

U.S. authorities are accusing the two top officials of a Canadian company of operating a long-running scheme to illegally import prescription drugs into the U.S., according to court records filed Tuesday.

John Thomas Howard, treasurer and a director of the company, CANARX, was arrested Sunday on smuggling and conspiracy charges, according to the records.

Bob Howard, his brother, who is president and a director of CANARX, is also wanted in the federal investigation, according to an affidavit from Dustin Dobbs, a special agent with the Food and Drug Administration’s Office of Criminal Investigations. He has not yet been taken into custody.

Besides conspiracy and smuggling, the arrest warrant said John Thomas Howard was charged with introducing misbranded drugs into interstate commerce and illegal drug importation. No plea has been filed.

CANARX was featured in a CNBC investigation last year that revealed how the company and others known as alternative funding programs, or AFPs, are becoming more pervasive around the U.S. as drug costs skyrocket. The investigation found these companies have penetrated the country’s healthcare system by offering high-cost specialty drugs at more affordable prices through private and public employers. In some cases, employers are requiring their staff to use an AFP.

AFPs often obtain the medications overseas and ship them directly to patients, a practice that federal authorities have said is illegal and poses safety risks. CNBC traced the trail of drugs from abroad to the U.S. via a supply chain that the pharmaceutical companies producing the medications have not authorized.

On its website, CANARX, founded in 2002 and based in Windsor, Ontario, Canada, described its business as the first international prescription provider for the U.S. and the safest such program in the industry. The company said it sources its medications from Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia and New Zealand.

But the affidavit said that the FDA’s investigation found “there is probable cause to believe that (CANARX) illegally imported or caused the illegal importation of prescription drugs into the United States ….”

The affidavit does not specify which medications the agency believes were illegally imported. The criminal complaint covers the period from Feb. 22, 2017, through April 15, 2026.

The company’s general counsel, Joseph Morris, told CNBC in a statement: “The Howards deny all the charges against them, will defend vigorously, and expect to be vindicated in court.”

The company has been under FDA scrutiny for several years. In 2023, the agency seized medication being shipped by CANARX that it says was potentially misbranded and counterfeit, according to an email sent to a patient that was obtained by CNBC.

And in 2019, the FDA sent a warning letter to the company, saying it was operating “in a manner that substitutes the FDA-approved drugs prescribed by the U.S. healthcare provider with unapproved drugs.” Morris, in response to that warning, argued CANARX was not misleading patients, but agreed for the company to stop importing drugs that need to be administered by a doctor.

In an interview as part of the CNBC investigation, Morris said last year that the medicines shipped to U.S. patients come from highly regulated countries. He said CANARX was operating legally.

The central question for AFPs is the legality of importing prescription drugs into the U.S. for personal use. The FDA allows Americans to import medications for individual use in some cases if the drug is not available domestically. That is the basis on which the AFPs built their models for shipping medicines directly to patients.

But an FDA spokesperson told CNBC last year that “in most circumstances, a person cannot import prescription drugs from other countries into the U.S. ... as substitutes for FDA-approved drugs.”

In a separate civil lawsuit that is pending, Gilead Sciences accused CANARX and other companies of illegally importing Biktarvy, its medication to treat HIV.

In a statement to CNBC on Wednesday, a Gilead spokesperson said the company “has taken strong legal action to protect patients and the integrity of the U.S. medicines supply chain. We welcome the government’s efforts to hold accountable those whose conduct may put patients at risk.”

CANARX has not responded to the Gilead lawsuit.

— CNBC’s Paige Tortorelli and Melissa Lee contributed to this report

https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/starlink.title: Ukraine warns of fresh Starshield disruptions as U.S. envoys arrive in Moscow for talks with Putin
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/starlink.author: Elsa Ohlen,Sam Meredith
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/starlink.text:
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Thursday that fresh restrictions on Starshield operations over Ukraine had been imposed.

He said Ukraine is trying to establish all the circumstances with the American side.

Similar speed limitations were imposed last month at speeds above 160 kilometers per hour.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine was investigating what he described as fresh restrictions on SpaceX’s Starshield service over the country, after similar speed limitations were temporarily imposed last month.

“Our units have been recording significant disruptions to Starshield’s operations over the territory of Ukraine for several days now – along the entire front line and in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine,” he wrote on X early Thursday.

Starshield is SpaceX’s
 satellite network for government and national-security use, built on Starlink technology.

CNBC has reached out to SpaceX and the White House for comment.

“The Ukrainian military have already investigated the circumstances, and these are not random errors but systematic speed restrictions,” he said, adding that they are trying to establish the circumstances with the U.S.

Zelenskyy said the restrictions imposed an effective speed limit on terminals moving at speeds above 161 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour), disconnecting anything that was moving faster and making it harder for Ukraine to intercept Russian jet-powered drones.

“There have already been strikes that got through because our interception systems cannot reach sufficient speeds and are unable to intercept in time.”

On Oct. 14, Ukrainian officials accused SpaceX of undermining the country’s ability to defend itself by cutting connectivity speeds and thereby disrupting military operations. On October 24, Zelenskyy confirmed that systems had returned to their previous operating speeds.

According to The Wall Street Journal, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk ordered those restrictions, rendering some Ukrainian strike and interceptor drones virtually unusable. The newspaper later reported that U.S. President Donald Trump had asked Musk to reverse the move. Trump has denied that the White House ordered Starlink restrictions in Ukraine.

Musk initially appeared to pin responsibility for any restrictions on the U.S. government, writing on X that “Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government.” He later claimed Ukraine had violated Starlink’s terms of service, prompting the company to restrict its access to the high-speed satellite technology, something that Ukrainian officials have strongly contested.

Serhii Beskrestnov, a defense tech advisor to Zelenskyy, said at the time that Ukraine cannot use commercial Starlink for medium- or long-range drone strikes because the service does not operate over Russian territory and had imposed drone speed limits of 70–90 kilometers per hour for months.

On Thursday, Beskrestnov confirmed that “the speed of Starlink operation during movement was again limited.”

“We did not rejoice for long,” he said, adding that “any terms can be changed and discussed, instead of leaving our country without sky protection.”

The comments came as U.S.-brokered peace talks wrapped up in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday and U.S. special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow for further talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Witkoff and Kushner were met by Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev as they arrived at Vnukovo Airport on Thursday morning, according to Russian state news agency Tass. The pair were expected to discuss a lasting resolution to Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, which has now raged for more than four-and-a-half years.

Later on Thursday, Witkoff and Kushner are poised to meet with Zelenskyy on the sidelines of a political summit held in Ireland.

Trilateral talks in the United Arab Emirates between Ukrainian, Russian and American negotiators ended earlier this week without a major diplomatic breakthrough on a ceasefire or territorial settlement.

https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/lutnick-.title: Lutnick should ban Chinese memory maker CXMT from U.S., Sen. Cotton says
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/lutnick-.author: Jeffrey Kopp,MacKenzie Sigalos
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/lutnick-.text:
Sen. Tom Cotton is urging the Commerce Department to add Chinese memory maker CXMT to its “Entity List,” which would sharply restrict its access to U.S. technology.

Cotton, in a letter obtained first by CNBC, warned Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick against allowing the company to grow its global footprint.

The company is challenging memory heavyweights Micron, Samsung and SK Hynix — and pushing into HBM, the high-bandwidth memory used in AI chips.

Sen. Tom Cotton, R-Ark., is urging the Trump administration to take a harsher stance toward Chinese memory maker ChangXin Memory Technologies
.

“CXMT, one of Communist China’s national memory chip champions, poses a growing risk to our economic prosperity and military superiority,” Cotton wrote in a letter sent Thursday to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. “The U.S. must take action to prevent CXMT from gaining a stronger foothold in the global market.”

CXMT is the world’s fourth-largest producer of DRAM  – or dynamic random access memory – which powers many basic functions of computers and smartphones.

Cotton, in a letter first obtained by CNBC, is asking Lutnick to push CXMT onto the department’s Bureau of Industry and Security Entity List, which would significantly restrict U.S. firms’ ability to do business with the company.

“It basically means that U.S. companies are not allowed to do business with that entity-listed company, and that entity-listed company does not get access to U.S. technology,” said Kyle Chan, a Brookings Institution fellow who studies China’s technology development.

DRAM is a “commodity,” MS Hwang, research director at Counterpoint, told CNBC, meaning it is made to a global standard and is generally interchangeable from one manufacturer to another.

However, with the right production technology, it can also form the building blocks of HBM, or high-bandwidth memory. HBM is an extremely high-demand product that powers AI chips made by Nvidia
, Google
 and Amazon
 Web Services, which are central to the growth of artificial intelligence giants including Anthropic and OpenAI. It’s made by just three main companies: Samsung
, SK Hynix
 and Micron
.

The Commerce Department and CXMT didn’t immediately respond to CNBC’s requests for comment.

Those same three companies control the lion’s share of the DRAM market, but CXMT has made inroads. The company’s share of the DRAM market jumped from 4% to 10% by revenue in a year, from the second quarter of 2025 to the same quarter of 2026, according to Counterpoint using the most recent reporting available. And in July, the company went public and its stock price soared, making it the most valuable company listed in China at the time.

While the company’s HBM capabilities are nascent, according to Counterpoint, Reuters reported that the company was to begin production of the chips, even though yields are low at just 20% to 30%. That means that the majority of the chips it produces are faulty.

CXMT is already on the Pentagon’s “1260H” list, which identifies several dozen Chinese companies with ties to Beijing’s military. But Chan says that list doesn’t come with stringent restrictions for U.S. businesses.

“It’s not a list that has that much teeth to it, in terms of restrictions to U.S. companies working with Chinese firms on that list,” Chan said.

The Wall Street Journal reported Aug. 9 that Apple
 was considering using CXMT’s memory in iPhones and Macs in light of the global shortage driven by the AI buildout. Being on the Entity List could change that.

“From the U.S. government standpoint, their concern is that working with CXMT would – even as a customer, just buying their products – would help to improve their ability to ramp up memory chip production, and also maybe help China get further down the road towards HBM,” Chan said. “It’s part of the broader effort to stymie or slow down China’s own chip development.”

Cotton alluded to CXMT’s efforts to break into the HBM market in his letter.

″[CXMT’s] decision to move forward in less than ideal conditions highlights both Communist China’s desperation for chips and manufacturing struggles without advanced equipment and knowledge,” he wrote. “More can be done to ensure that CXMT is cut off from the financial and technological resources that aid its supply chain and undercut American growth.”

https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/11/canada-a.title: Canada’s ambassador warns Trump tariffs are driving up costs, threatening U.S. investment
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/11/canada-a.author: Luke Fountain
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/11/canada-a.text:
Canada’s ambassador to the U.S., Mark Wiseman, warned that uncertainty surrounding President Donald Trump’s tariffs is raising investment costs and discouraging businesses from expanding.

New York Fed research found that roughly 90% of tariff costs were passed on to U.S. importers, with additional consumer price pressures expected in 2027.

Canada is seeking to attract investment with a lower effective business tax rate, as trade tensions persist and Democrats prepare to challenge Trump’s tariffs in Congress.

Canada’s ambassador to the U.S. warned Wednesday that President Donald Trump’s tariffs are driving up investment costs and discouraging business expansion, as new Federal Reserve research points to more price hikes for American consumers next year.

“Uncertainty increases your cost of capital,” Ambassador Mark Wiseman said at the B20 summit, a gathering of global business leaders in Washington hosted by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce.

“If you’re going to build a new plant, add a new shift, spend money on R&D, the more certainty you have, the more likely you’re going to do that,” said Wiseman, a former BlackRock executive who became Canada’s ambassador in February.

His warning comes as Washington and Ottawa struggle to resolve a tariff quarrel affecting one of the U.S.’s largest trading relationships. The two countries exchanged roughly $570 billion in goods during the first nine months of 2026, according to U.S. Census Bureau data. That’s an increase from the same period in 2025, the first year of Trump’s second term, but lower than the comparable nine months during the previous three years, when Joe Biden was president.

U.S. customs duties calculated on imports from Canada reached $10 billion in 2025, compared with $400 million in 2024, according to the Congressional Research Service.

An October study by New York Fed researchers found that nearly 90% of tariff costs were passed on to U.S. importers, with about a quarter of tariff increases eventually reaching consumer goods prices and further price pressures expected in 2027.

The findings come as Labor Department data showed consumer prices rose a higher-than-expected 0.4% in October, adding to inflation concerns after Republicans’ sweeping midterm losses.

Trump has defended his tariffs as necessary to protect U.S. manufacturers and workers, accusing Canada of discriminatory trade practices that disadvantage U.S. exporters.

The two governments have resumed negotiations after talks collapsed in August, with discussions focused on reducing tariffs on Canadian steel and automobiles. Trump has imposed duties of up to 50% on certain Canadian products, prompting retaliatory measures targeting billions of dollars in U.S. exports.

Wiseman called for the removal of tariffs imposed under Sections 232 and 338 of U.S. trade law, saying a resolution would help businesses make long-term investment decisions.

“The sooner, the better,” he said.

The political stakes have shifted following the midterms, with Democrats preparing to challenge Trump’s tariffs when they take control of Congress in January.

Still, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Tuesday that the Trump administration remains Canada’s principal negotiating partner.

“We’ve had comprehensive free trade with the United States since 1988,” Wiseman said, describing Canada’s objective as returning “as close as we can to free trade” while creating the certainty businesses need.

European ambassadors echoed those concerns at the B20 summit. Germany’s ambassador to the U.S., Jens Hanefeld, said businesses could adapt to tariffs but struggled with an “ever-changing regulatory environment” that forced companies to spend more on lawyers to navigate shifting trade rules.

Speaking on the same panel, France’s ambassador, Aurélien Lechevallier, urged greater cooperation on AI and energy rather than continued trade disputes.

“We’ve spent, I think, a lot of time the last years working and dealing with regulations, tariffs,” he said. “Businesses are eager to do more business.”

— Correction: This story has been corrected to reflect that Wiseman spoke about adding shifts to plants. A previous version misquoted the ambassador.

https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/11/meta-inf.title: Meta head of infrastructure will leave and be succeeded by former AWS cloud exec
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/11/meta-inf.author: Jonathan Vanian
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/11/meta-inf.text:
Meta’s head of infrastructure and co-head of engineering Santosh Janardhan will leave in 2027.

Janardhan’s successor, former AWS senior vice president David Brown, will lead Meta’s infrastructure efforts of the Meta Compute initiative, spearheaded by Dina Powell McCormick and Daniel Gross.

The executive move underscores Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s efforts to expand the company’s data center operations under newer leaders at a time of increasing investor scrutiny on capital expenditure spending by the social media giant and its hyperscaler rivals.

Meta’s long-time infrastructure leader will leave the company in the new year, setting the stage for a recently hired former Amazon Web Services executive to oversee its massive data center technical operations.

Santosh Janardhan, Meta’s head of infrastructure and co-head of engineering, revealed his upcoming departure on Wednesday in an internal memo obtained by CNBC. Janardhan, who has worked at Meta since 2009, said “it’s time to pass the baton” to former AWS senior vice president David Brown, who joined Meta in July from AWS.

The executive move underscores Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s efforts to expand the company’s data center operations under newer leaders at a time of increasing investor scrutiny on capital expenditure spending by the social media giant and its hyperscaler rivals.

Brown will now formally lead Meta’s infrastructure efforts as part of the Meta Compute initiative, which is spearheaded by the company’s president and vice chairman Dina Powell McCormick and technical leader Daniel Gross. Zuckerberg is relying on these new executives to continue developing cutting-edge data centers and related infrastructure needed to support its AI ambitions.

The company said during its recent third-quarter earnings report that it expects full-year capex to fall in the range of $135 billion to $145 billion. Meta also logged negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion, which S&P Global Ratings noted as part of its decision in late October to revise Meta’s credit rating from AA- stable to AA- negative.

Janardhan said in the memo that he will help support Brown through the first quarter of 2027 as part of “the transition.”

“As we make the next set of choices about our priorities, this is the right time for Dave to take the lead in shaping that work,” Janardhan said in the memo. “Dave has spent his career building and operating dependable infrastructure for a wide range of demanding workloads. He has the instincts, depth and judgment this moment requires.”

Bloomberg News first reported on the executive transition.
