It will bring together potential presidential candidates for 2028, newly elected lawmakers, party strategists, and established Democratic leaders. The gathering was planned in advance of the midterms by a new group called Majority Democrats.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: Palestinian baby dies from cold in Gaza amid Israeli restrictions on aid
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.author: Al Jazeera Staff
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
A Palestinian infant has died from the cold in a tent sheltering his displaced family in southern Gaza, his father and a doctor said, as Israel continues to impose severe restrictions on winter supplies to the war-ravaged territory.

Nine-month-old Kinan Ahmed Raqiq “died from hypothermia” in Khan Younis, in the southern region of the enclave, a doctor who spoke on he condition of anonymity told the AFP news agency on Thursday.

Ahmed Raqiq, the baby’s father, told AFP that Kinan died after cold temperatures hit Gaza overnight.

“I woke up only to see his skin had turned blue so I rushed him to Nasser Hospital, but he had already died from hypothermia and frozen to death,” he said.

“I am in complete shock. I found myself holding my son wrapped in a burial shroud,” he said outside the hospital, dried tears on his face as he held his son wrapped in a white sheet.

Gaza’s Civil Defence spokesman, Mahmoud Basal, confirmed the infant’s death after exposure to extreme cold, Palestinian news network Al-Quds reported.

The death comes as the United Kingdom, Qatar and Jordan led a coalition of more than 50 countries and organisations calling on Israel to provide immediate entry of critical items for shelter, fuel, water, sanitation and health to Gaza.

With winter arriving, the group said, “far too many people in Gaza are still without adequate shelter, and risk exposure to hypothermia, respiratory infections, waterborne diseases and other preventable illnesses”.

The statement echoed recent criticism of Israel over its restrictions by the United States-led Board of Peace and United Nations humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher.

Responding to the Board of Peace, Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said that Israel had allowed in supplies including 91,000 tents and that “Hamas alone is responsible for the suffering of the people of Gaza.”

As well as the cold, Gaza has experienced flooding this week following heavy rains, affecting tens of thousands of people’s tents. Five people, including three children, died the day after the flooding when a sandy embankment eroded and collapsed onto their tents.

The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said that as of November 8, 26,000 households were affected by storms.

Around 65 percent of Gaza’s people are still living displaced in tents or other temporary shelter, OCHA said.

James Elder, spokesman on Gaza for the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF), warned that the flooding was just the beginning of the cold season.

“It’s very important to know how bad things are in Gaza. It’s not yet winter,” Elder said.

“We’re weeks away from winter, so we are getting unprecedented rain and cold.”

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: US nonprofits sue tech giants to halt AI development
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.author: Hoda Sherif
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
California lawsuit demands freeze training on ‘catastrophic’ artificial intelligence models.

A coalition of digital safety and consumer watchdogs has filed a lawsuit against the world’s top artificial intelligence (AI) developers, requesting a court-ordered freeze on AI model training and deployments.

The civil complaint, filed Thursday in San Francisco Superior Court by the Irreplaceable Education Fund, Public Citizen, Heat Initiative and the Alliance for Secure AI, comes on the heels of a sweeping Democratic midterm victory that many analysts note could reshape, and ultimately tighten the regulatory framework for Silicon Valley.

The suit targets five tech giants – Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceX – alleging the industry leaders cannot prevent their AI creations from causing “catastrophic harm”. They are demanding the companies pause their technologies until safeguards are put in place.

The lawsuit cites documented instances of AI-driven cyberattacks and other harmful behaviours, alongside the companies’ own grave admissions that their unregulated technologies could go rogue and pose an existential threat to humanity.

The nonprofits are seeking an immediate emergency injunction on next-generation models from major tech firms. They are demanding the companies only be allowed to resume operations once they can prove the technology is under human control.

“No other industry is allowed to treat its own development of unsafe products — much less ones that could kill us all — as inevitable,” reads the complaint. “Plaintiffs bring this suit to stop Defendants from continuing their unlawful path to disaster.”

The plaintiffs claim that the companies have violated a California unfair competition law by endangering public health and interfering with the use of property, such as computer systems.

The law prohibits deceptive advertising, anti-competitive market behaviours and bait-and-switch tactics.

The advocacy groups also report having to divert resources to counter “near-daily crises” from the companies’ rapidly advancing AI models.

Turning a temporary court-ordered pause into a permanent ban raises tough questions about how to enforce the ban, how to verify that companies are following it, and ultimately, what legal thresholds are required before the freeze could be lifted.

One of the four plaintiffs – the Irreplaceable Education Fund, a New York-based nonprofit advocacy organisation focused on technology safeguarding for the public – told Al Jazeera it is demanding government regulation of AI development.

“A real freeze must specify what work has to halt, how compliance is verified, and the consequences of breaking the rules,” said Phil Aroneanu, founder and executive director of the Irreplaceable.

“This requires government inspections and the authority to halt prohibited work, not just a ban on publicly releasing the models. To help enforce this freeze, major computing facilities can be monitored.”

Pressed on what specific statutory guardrails they hope to establish, the group outlined a multi-tiered system of oversight.

AI development should be conditioned on “deliberate, considered decision informed by the general public,” said the nonprofit, adding, “There are a number of proposals that show promise, including federal independent evaluators and regulators, strict liability for tech companies and the products they create, and an independent agency to regulate them.”

Federal law, they stated, should establish minimum protections while preserving states’ authority to adopt and enforce stronger measures.

While the lawsuit targets AI titans in a California courtroom, the plaintiffs argue that pausing domestic development won’t hand a victory to tech rivals – notably China, provided Washington sets global rules and kick-starts talks with Beijing. AI firms and US President Donald Trump have repeatedly signalled the US is racing full throttle to beat Beijing in AI development.

“We anticipate that bilateral deals and an international treaty will be needed to ensure that we can reduce the negative impacts of AI and prevent catastrophe,” the Irreplaceable Education Fund said in a statement to Al Jazeera.

“If both sides are slowed by roughly the same factor, while the risk of losing control of our AIs is reduced, then this does not really harm the U.S. or China’s AI competitiveness, but it makes us all safer.”

The argument confronts Trump’s longstanding resistance to slowing down AI: the fear that any unilateral restraint shown by Washington would allow Beijing to set the path in global AI development.

The president, a proponent of AI rapid expansion, has previously said that it was important to continue leading the evolution of AI over China, because “whoever wins AI wins”.

Despite years of warnings, Congress has yet to pass legislation governing AI, the plaintiffs noted.

“Every day these companies race forward towards super-intelligent AI is another day that more people and more critical infrastructure are put at risk,” said the plaintiff.

Now, they’re hoping incoming Democratic lawmakers will heed their calls.

“The new Congress should start by implementing a freeze on new AI development,” the organisation said. “However, we can’t wait for lawmakers to act. Courts must provide relief.”

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: Why did Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resign, and who is Colette Kress?
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.author: Al Jazeera Staff
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has resigned following revelations that he had two extramarital affairs.

Nvidia’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress, has taken over as interim CEO while the company looks for a permanent replacement.

The company controls an estimated 90 percent of the market for advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips and is one of the world’s most valuable companies.

Here is what we know:

Huang stepped down on Thursday following several days of intense scrutiny over his personal relationships and potential national security issues.

On Sunday, Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife and apologised to his family and to Nvidia employees.

Huang moved to the United States from Taiwan as a child. His wife, Lori, has been with him since before he cofounded Nvidia in 1993.

Nvidia’s board initially backed Huang, saying on Sunday that it had confidence in his leadership. It also launched an independent investigation into reports that he had been targeted by Chinese intelligence.

But on Wednesday, the Reuters news agency reported the board was meeting to consider whether to remove him following further revelations of a relationship with Kimberly Powell, a senior Nvidia executive who reported directly to him.

The company announced his resignation on Thursday. Huang also resigned from the board, ending his 33-year tenure as chief executive.

Nvidia didn’t give a reason for his departure.

“Jensen’s contributions to Nvidia are profound,” the board said in a statement, thanking him for his “immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry”.

The allegations were related to reported extramarital affairs.

The first involved Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based tech company Megaspeed, who is alleged to have worked for Chinese intelligence.

The allegations have raised questions about national security, particularly given Huang’s support for allowing Nvidia to sell advanced AI chips to China.

Separately, The New York Times reported on Wednesday that Huang had an affair with Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reported directly to him.

The second reported relationship raised concerns about a potential conflict of interest involving a senior executive.

The controversy comes amid a debate in Washington over exporting advanced US AI chips to China.

Huang, 63, spent years campaigning against the restrictions on Nvidia chip sales to China.

In December 2025, President Donald Trump approved the export of Nvidia’s H200 chips to China, despite concerns that the technology could bolster Beijing’s AI capabilities.

The chips are about six times more powerful than the H20 models previously available to Chinese buyers.

Exports are subject to US inspections, limits on shipments, restrictions on military use and a 25 percent tariff.

According to Al Jazeera’s Osama Bin Javaid, Chinese companies reportedly ordered more than two million H200 chips, potentially worth $54bn.

“Worth remembering it’s orders, not completed sales,” he said.

Critics are concerned the technology could help China close the AI gap with the US.

The allegations raised questions about whether his personal relationships could have exposed sensitive information.

“There is no established evidence he knowingly assisted Beijing or that company secrets were compromised,” Bin Javaid noted.

Nvidia’s board has also said it has no reason to believe national security was compromised.

Kress has served as Nvidia’s chief financial officer since September 2013 and oversaw the chipmaker’s finances during a period of growth.

During her time at Nvidia, the company’s annual revenue rose from $4.13bn in fiscal 2014 to $215.9bn in fiscal 2026.

Before joining Nvidia, Kress held senior finance roles at Texas Instruments, Microsoft and Cisco.

She holds a bachelor’s degree in finance from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University.

Kress is also among America’s wealthiest self-made women, according to Forbes.

In a statement following her appointment, Kress said she was committed to building on the foundation Huang had created over the past 33 years.

Nvidia’s board has appointed Kress as interim CEO while it searches for a permanent replacement and considers both internal and external candidates.

Trump has suggested former Apple chief executive Tim Cook as Huang’s successor.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump praised Huang’s work at Nvidia and said Cook was the person to replace him.

“A Legend replaces a Legend,” Trump wrote.

Cook stepped down as Apple’s chief executive in September and now serves as the company’s executive chairman.

Speaking to Al Jazeera, technology and cybersecurity analyst Ritesh Kotak said choosing Nvidia’s next CEO would be a decision for the company’s board.

“At the end of the day, it comes down to the board,” he said.

Kotak pointed to the differences between Apple, which primarily sells consumer technology, and Nvidia, whose chips power much of the AI industry.

There has been no indication that Cook is interested in the position.

Trump has defended Huang amid the allegations.

Reporting from the White House, Al Jazeera’s Alan Fisher said Trump had offered a “very forceful defence” of the Nvidia founder, who accompanied him on a trip to China earlier this year.

Trump said he recently learned of the suspected spying scandal, although reports suggest he had been informed of the allegations before the trip.

Fisher said the president was likely to face further questions about “what he knew and when he knew it”.

Meanwhile, Huang’s departure has raised concerns about Nvidia’s future.

“He’s the captain that was steering the ship back since the early 90s,” Kotak told Al Jazeera.

“These are big shoes that need to be filled,” he added.

Kotak said the resignation could create uncertainty among Nvidia’s employees and customers.

“If you’re Nvidia, if you’re the employees, if you’re a customer, I think you’re worried right now,” he said.

Clement Delangue, chief executive of Hugging Face, which Nvidia has agreed to acquire, reaffirmed his commitment to open-source AI following Huang’s resignation.

Meanwhile, Lloyd Blankfein, former chief executive of Goldman Sachs, reflected on Huang’s departure in a post on X.

“Sad about Jensen. Shakespearean,” he wrote, quoting former French President Charles de Gaulle: “The graveyards are filled with indispensable men.”

Huang’s departure has also raised questions about the wider AI industry. Nvidia is not only a major chip supplier but also an investor in companies that build and rent out AI computing infrastructure.

The company is also preparing to invest approximately $10bn in AI developer Anthropic as part of its planned stock market listing, expected next week.

https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.title: Senegal’s wrestlers turn tradition into gold at Dakar Youth Olympics
https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.author: Nicolas Haque
https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.text:
She wasn’t even supposed to be there.

Sixteen-year-old Elisabeth Diatta is from the southern Senegalese region of Casamance. Football was her sport, not wrestling.

Yet, On Saturday, there she was on the sand at Saly beach, representing Senegal in beach wrestling at Dakar’s Youth Olympics, almost instinctively seizing her opponent and throwing her down. Then came the whistle, the referee’s look, the confirmation, the disbelief. She celebrated like Cristiano Ronaldo; the leap, the turn, the “Siu!”

At 16, she had beaten Japan’s Reisa Kojima 5-1 in the 55kg final to win Senegal’s first Youth Olympic gold.

A teenage girl had delivered a medal in a sport so often described as belonging to men.

The crowd roared. Diatta danced, defiant, before wrapping herself in green, yellow and red. Beneath the Senegalese flag’s green star, a new star was born.

Her path here began when her older sister Jeannine was injured and could not enter a wrestling tournament at a sport camp. Diatta took her place. She won her first bout. The footballer kept wrestling.

“They said wrestling would make me less feminine,” explains Diatta – the “they” she is referring to are the adults around here. Out of teenage defiance, she persisted in the sport.

Watching proudly was coach Isabelle Sambou, twice an Olympian herself. She had wanted this gold for Senegal long before her young wrestlers were old enough to compete.

“I wanted to win gold for Senegal when I was an athlete,” she said. “Today, I have my reward.”

She would soon have another reason to celebrate as another Senegalese teenage hopeful, 16-year-old Maguette Diop, stepped into the wrestling circle later on Saturday. Diop had been preparing for this moment long before the games, being held from October 31 to November 13 in the Senegalese capital Dakar and nearby towns of Saly and Diamniadio.

Three months in an intense training camp had helped Senegal’s young wrestlers adapt to beach wrestling, where the rules differed from those of their traditional sport.

In traditional Senegalese wrestling, a wrestler wins by bringing their opponent to the ground, typically onto their back, buttocks or knees, or by forcing them onto all fours. Unlike beach wrestling, there is no points system. One decisive fall can end the contest.

In beach wrestling, forcing an opponent outside the circle earns one point, as does a takedown. A throw onto the back earns three and ends the contest. Bouts last up to three minutes; the first to at least three points wins.

Diop had spent months preparing for this moment. On August 27, he had lost to Iran’s Reza Jalilian in the semifinals of the under-17 world championships in Baku. Barely two months later, on home ground, he was not about to let that happen again.

He reached the boys’ 80kg final feeling confident despite facing Azerbaijan’s Nihad Suleymanli, a two-time under-17 world champion. Suleymani wrestled with skill, ignoring the crowd cheering for Diop.

For a moment, the gold appeared to be slipping away. The referee awarded Suleymanli three points. Diop’s coaches urged a challenge. The replay reversed the decision: Those points belonged to Diop. He had won 4-0.

More dancing. More flags. Another Senegalese teenager with gold.

Here, wrestling runs deep. Long before the Olympic flame reached this Atlantic coastline, generations had gathered around circles of sand.

Laamb, Senegal’s traditional wrestling, carries the pride of villages and neighbourhoods. It is more than a contest of strength. Wrestlers seek spiritual protection through prayers, rituals and amulets believed to ward off evil spirits. All to the rhythm of sabar drums, traditional Senegalese percussion whose beats accompany the ceremonial dances, summoning courage and stirring the crowd.

In Casamance, where Diatta comes from, women have long wrestled too, even as men dominate the professional arenas.

“I hope this experience will give girls courage and determination,” said Ndeye Khady Anna Diatta, who added a third Senegalese gold in the 45kg category the following day.

By Thursday, Senegal stood sixth in the medal table – three of their five golds won wrestling on the sand.

For Africa, hosting its first Olympic sporting event, these victories offered something the rankings could not measure: young people seeing themselves in the athletes wearing gold, a familiar sport carrying them onto a world stage.

And for the girls watching Senegal’s female wrestlers, perhaps something closer still. A place inside the circle.
https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.summary: Senegal's first Youth Olympic gold medal was won by Elisabeth Diatta, 16. Diatta was representing Senegal in beach wrestling at Dakar's Youth Olympics. Diattan, from Casamance, won the 55kg final in the 55 kg category.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: UK mosque rebukes comission’s ‘warning’ following Palestine comments
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.author: Al Jazeera Staff
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
The Lewisham Islamic Centre (LIC) in London has rejected a warning issued by the UK’s independent Charity Commission, which reprimanded the mosque for comments on Palestinian suffering made by an imam during October 2023 sermons.

“The matters raised by the Commission represent a troubling attempt to scrutinise, restrict and penalise legitimate religious worship” and “the expression of solidarity with the Palestinian people,” the mosque said in an official statement issued Wednesday.

The statement comes after the charity watchdog accused the religious centre of including “content that was inflammatory, divisive and not in the charity’s best interests” during two separate sermons, as they issued an official warning urging the centre to “improve its handling of speakers and events hosted at the charity’s premises” on October 20.

The commission warned that if the mosque fails to “remedy the misconduct”, it may be subjected to further action.

The mosque also accused the commission of imposing disproportionate expectations on Muslim charities after the warning, describing them as “unnecessarily burdensome”. The religious centre explained that a sermon, or khutbah, is an integral part of Islamic worship and often speaks to the issues affecting the wellbeing of congregations and their communities. The LIC worried that the warning suggested the commission was “entitled to dictate which subjects Imams may address in their khutbahs”.

LIC added that they are currently seeking legal advice as to the best way to move forward following the warning.

CAGE International, a London-based human rights organisation, supported the mosque, and claimed the Charity Commission showed lenience when it came to pro-Israel charities.

“The Commission’s position treats the word ‘Zionist’ as inflammatory in itself,” CAGE said on Thursday. “This merges opposition to a political ideology with hatred of a people, and places Muslim religious expression under suspicion by default.”

“The Commission has told a mosque that naming who is responsible for Palestinian suffering falls outside acceptable religious practice,” a spokesperson for CAGE said. “This is the same regulator asking for the power to remove trustees for their views,” they added, referring to a recent government consultation to expand the Charity Commission’s powers.
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.summary: Lewisham Islamic Centre in London rejected warning issued by UK's independent Charity Commission. Charity Commission reprimanded the mosque for comments made by an imam during October 2023 sermons.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: Pro-Palestine philanthropist faces US extradition hearing in Spain
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.author: Graham Keeley
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
Madrid, Spain – The wife of a pro-Palestine philanthropist who faces extradition to the United States has urged the Spanish prime minister to grant him asylum, to save him from being sent to his own country.

James “Fergie” Chambers, a US citizen with a reported $250m net worth, has been charged with money laundering.

The US government’s case centres on Chambers’s alleged laundering of $7.5m, which he is said to have wired several years ago from a US bank account to Tunisia, where he lived at the time, allegedly using the cash to support Hamas. He is not charged with any “terrorism” offences and denies any wrongdoing.

“I am pleading with [Spanish Prime Minister Pedro] Sanchez to use his powers to ensure Fergie’s political asylum claim is expedited for urgent consideration by the panel of ministers,” his wife Stella Schnabel told Al Jazeera. “If [Sanchez] chooses not to act, he risks enabling [US President Donald] Trump to establish a precedent in Spain and across Europe which criminalises solidarity with the Palestinian people.”

Schnabel says that the money was to support Club Africain, a Tunisian football club, to pay off its debts and overdue salaries, to reconstruct a training centre and build pitches for youth sides.

Spain’s National Court will hear evidence from the US authorities on Friday, and a final decision will be made later.

Chambers, a self-proclaimed anti-imperialist, is also facing charges of riot and conspiracy to riot relating to a protest at an Israeli arms company in 2023 in the US, for which he could face up to 30 years of imprisonment.

Chambers was arrested in July in Ibiza as he and his partner, Schnabel, an actress, searched for a school for their son, after Interpol issued a Red Notice for his detention. Since his arrest, he has claimed asylum, alleging he is the victim of political persecution.

Chambers cannot be extradited until the asylum claim is resolved, and if it is successful, he cannot be extradited.

Lawyers for Chambers said mistranslations between the US criminal charge in English and the version presented to Spanish authorities in Spanish make the allegations seem more serious.

Under Spanish law, all extradition requests must be translated into Spanish.

The alleged mistranslations, which relate to protests in 2003 in the United States that targeted the US-based facilities of Elbit Systems, Israel’s largest weapons manufacturer, changed “direct action” to “direct violence”.

Lawyers also said there is no reference to violence in the original US criminal complaint, but the translated version submitted to Spanish authorities mentions “three fires” even though no fires are mentioned in the original text.

US authorities also changed the description of protesters’ “activation” of smoke canisters to “detonation”, which, defence lawyers say, is usually used to describe an explosive device, not the release of smoke canisters.

The most serious mistranslation, say defence lawyers, involved a conversation between third parties that in the original criminal complaint described Chambers as being part of a “global terrorism game”.

However, in the translated version submitted to Spanish authorities, this phrase is changed to “global terrorism activities”. Chambers has not been charged with any “terrorism” offences.

“It’s important to highlight that the US administration has not charged Fergie with material support for or financing terrorism or any terror-related offences, nor presented a shred of evidence that even a single cent has been used for violent or terrorist acts,” Aitor Martinez, one of the defence lawyers, told Al Jazeera.

“The reason not to charge him with those offences is clear: there is no evidence.”

If the court backs the US extradition request, defence lawyers for Chambers will appeal, dragging the case on longer.

However, the Spanish government’s Council of Ministers may have the last word on the case and could refuse to send him to the US if they believe the case is politically motivated.

The situation is complicated by the fact that Spain is holding an early election on November 29, which, according to the polls, the conservative People’s Party is likely to win, potentially requiring the support of the far-right Vox party.

Both right-wing parties may be more inclined to support extraditing Chambers than Spain’s Socialist prime minister Sanchez, an outspoken critic of Trump’s support for Israel’s genocidal war in Gaza.

Chambers, 46, is heir to the Cox family, owners of the Atlanta-based Cox Communications. As part of a deal in which his family cut ties with him at the time, he sold stock back to his family worth about $250m in 2003.

Since then, he has funded about 100 projects in 20 countries, Schnabel said.

The US Department of Justice declined to comment when contacted by Al Jazeera.

Two of the three charges in the US complaint – riot and conspiracy to riot – are related to allegations that he funded the legal fees of activists arrested in the 2003 protests against Elbit.

Chambers has commented publicly on Israel and Gaza.

In the wake of the 2023 Hamas attacks on Israel, he posted on X about Israel’s response: “Stop calling it ‘collective punishment’/There’s nothing to be punished for/No faction of the Palestinian resistance, Hamas or other, has done *anything* wrong/It’s simply genocide/Like it has been.”

On the day of the court hearing, demonstrations will be held in support of  Chambers outside Spanish embassies in London, Brussels. Amsterdam and Tunisia, where Chambers lived for some time.

https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/1.title: Home sales in the US are at their lowest level since 2016
https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/1.text:
Sales of previously owned homes in the US have hit the lowest level since 2010 as mortgage rates hover above 7 percent.

The National Association of Realtors (NAR) said on Thursday that home sales dropped 5.5 percent in October to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.75 million units. That was the lowest level since August 2010.

“Home buying is difficult when mortgage rates have climbed to their highest levels since 2000, aside from a single month in 2023. As a result, home sales fell to their lowest level since August 2010,” said NAR Chief Economist Lawrence Yun.

He said, “It is just a tough market for buyers and sellers.”

“Sales decreased by 8.8 percent year-over-year,” the NAR report found. “Month-over-month sales declined in the Midwest, South and West and held steady in the Northeast. Year-over-year sales declined in all four regions.”

The home sales used in the report are counted at the closing of a contract and are a look at previously occupied ones. October’s sales likely reflected contracts signed in August and September.

“Despite fewer transactions in October, the 88 million homeowners across the country are largely in a comfortable financial position due to sizable housing wealth accumulation,” said the report.

First-time buyers accounted for just 29 percent of home purchases last month, down from 31 percent in September and 32 percent in October last year, NAR said. First-time buyers have historically made up closer to 40 percent of home sales.

The US housing market has been in a slump since 2022, when mortgage rates increased from pandemic-era lows. Sales of previously occupied US homes were essentially flat last year, stuck at a 30-year low. Yun expects home sales this year will likely end up lower than in 2025.

The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage was 7.33 percent in October, according to the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation, more commonly known as Freddie Mac, up from 6.86 percent in September and 6.25 percent one year ago.

The rate, however, averaged 7.18 percent last week, down from 7.24 percent in the previous week.

Rates on home loans are influenced by inflation, Federal Reserve policy and bond-market investors’ expectations for the economy, among other factors. They generally follow the trajectory of the 10-year Treasury yield, which lenders use as a guide to pricing home loans.

Until the past few weeks, mortgage rates had been on the rise since late February, when the US war with Iran began, pushing up the price of oil and driving inflation higher. The run-up in rates also reflected heightened bond market volatility, which led to rising yields on US Treasuries.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: What to know about the Logan Circle shooting in Washington, DC
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.author: Umar Farooq
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
Police say a gunman is dead after he allegedly shot five people, killing one, in a busy thoroughfare in the centre of Washington, DC, on Thursday morning.

Mass shootings are not uncommon in the United States, but this one drew a swift and massive response from local police as well as federal security forces. Law and order in the capital city has been at the centre of a national debate about the administration of US President Donald Trump.

About 8am local time (13:00 GMT), during a busy rush hour commute, a gunman entered a gym in Logan Circle, a trendy neighbourhood near foreign embassies and fashionable restaurants, about 1.6km (one mile) north of the White House.

“Within seconds, there was a man who fell to the ground, and a pool of blood came out,” said James Spellman, who witnessed the attack and said there were about 50 people in the gym. “One gym member rushed to help him. He was instantly dead. He had been shot in the neck.”

Spellman said he and other gym members ran out of the gym and he heard more gunfire in the area of 15th Street. He said he heard about two shots fired in the gym and about five or six fired outside.

Law enforcement arrived within minutes, cordoning off the area and working to apprehend the suspect. They included personnel from the Metropolitan Police Department, the city’s law enforcement agency, as well as heavily armed officers from federal agencies including the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and the Secret Service.

Authorities sent out alerts to people in the area warning them to shelter inside because of an “active shooter” situation. Schools near the scene were placed on lockdown. “Go inside the nearest building, stay away from windows, and remain indoors until further notice,” police instructed the public.

Washington, DC’s interim police chief, Jeffery Carroll, said the suspect was a white male wearing a grey shirt.

The suspect, police said, opened fire inside the gym, then exited the building and entered another adjacent building, where he barricaded himself inside a room on the seventh floor. Officers then began trying to negotiate with the suspect, with specialised negotiators talking to him over the phone, as snipers kept watch from nearby rooftops. At one point, he shot at police through the barricaded door.

About an hour after they began speaking to him, police say they heard gunfire over the phone, and they decided to breach the room where the suspect had been holed up. They found him with a self-inflicted gunshot wound, and he was pronounced dead at the scene.

Washington, DC Council member Brooke Pinto said the suspect, identified as a physician named Matt Lambert, initially shot a person in the gym with whom he was involved in a court case over a dispute over the condominium where he lived.

Police Chief Carroll, speaking to reporters shortly after the suspect was found dead, said the shooting appeared to have stemmed from a “conflict between him and the homeowners association of the building”.

Some unconfirmed reports cited a social media account as possibly belonging to the suspect, which appeared to frequently feature posts about bad living conditions in a condominium in the area where the attack occurred.

Little has been released about the victims of the shooting. Authorities said one person had died, and another was in critical condition in the hospital.

An assault in the same Logan Circle area back in August 2025 was cited by President Trump as a reason for deploying troops to the capital, launching a national push that saw controversial deployments to several Democratic-controlled cities.

A former Department of Government Efficiency official said he was assaulted in the early hours in the same area by a group of teenagers attempting to carjack him and a woman he was with. Trump declared a crime emergency and said his administration was taking control of the federal district’s local police force.

Although Washington, DC, has a mayor and city council, it is not treated on equal footing with other states in the country, and Congress as well as the president have some authority over things like its budget and law enforcement activities.

Trump deployed thousands of National Guard troops to the capital, who continue more than a year later to patrol the city in groups, including in the Logan Circle area.

The troops are a regular presence inside metro stations and locations across downtown, but local officials have pointed out they have largely stayed away from areas of the city that experience higher crime, and their impact has not been as large as President Trump has claimed.

The troops themselves have also drawn attacks.

In November last year, a National Guard member was killed by a gunman while on duty near 17th and I Streets NW. A second National Guard member was wounded. And in October, another National Guard member was shot during a gunfight in southeast Washington, DC.

The presence of the soldiers has at times caused friction with local officials, including Washington, DC Mayor Muriel Bowser.

Speaking at a news conference alongside the police chief after the shooting on Thursday, Bowser praised local police for their quick response to the incident and dismissed the suggestion that law enforcement had treated it with unusual importance.

“I praise [DC police] for bringing down crime in this city, and I praise our prosecutors,” Bowser said. “It’s not typical to have an active shooter that guns down people in the city, so all our law enforcement responded.”

https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2026/.title: ‘Her hands are as cold as ice’: Gaza families struggle to keep warm
https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2026/.author: Maram Humaid
https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2026/.text:
Gaza City, Gaza Strip – At night, as temperatures drop inside their makeshift shelter in Gaza City, Amira Saad struggles to keep her four-month-old baby, Mohammed, warm.

The baby mostly only has thin summer clothes. Unable to afford winter clothing, 27-year-old Amira has borrowed a warm garment from a neighbour, but remains worried about the cold during the night.

She lives with 18 family members, including nine children, under a tarp offering little protection from the elements. Finding enough warm clothes and blankets for everyone has become increasingly difficult.

The family was displaced from Gaza City’s Shujayea neighbourhood earlier in Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, and now lives in a makeshift camp west of the city.

Recent heavy rain has flooded their shelter, soaking mattresses, pillows, and blankets.

“We were flooded while we were sleeping. The water came inside and soaked our blankets, mattresses and pillows. Everything was wet,” Amira says.

The children mostly have old, torn summer clothes. Amira’s mother-in-law, 60-year-old Basima Saad, is also worried about her own 23-year-old daughter, who has a disability, and needs warm clothes and medication.

“Her hands become as cold as ice. I keep her beside me in bed to warm her, just as I would a small child,” Basima says. “I dress her before I dress myself. I have to make sure she is warm first.”

With no regular income, the family relies on community kitchens for food. Spare money for winter clothes and blankets simply is not available.

“My husband does not have a job. Two days ago, he went out to work breaking up rubble, but he broke his hand. The situation is very bad, and the cold is extremely severe,” Amira says.

The danger to the Palestinians living in these conditions, and particularly the very young, is not hypothetical.

On Thursday, a nine-month-old baby, Kinan Ahmed Raqiq, died of hypothermia. His father told AFP that he woke up in his tent to find that his son’s skin had turned blue.

Tragedies like that make Amal al-Maydana, a 46-year-old other of seven, fearful.

She’s raising her children alone – her husband Hamza was killed by an Israeli quadcopter in January 2025, and her eldest son Haitham was killed by a sniper in November of the same year, age 25 at the time.

She is originally from Gaza City’s Zeitoun neighbourhood and has been displaced six times during the war, fleeing Israeli attacks and losing the family’s home, land, and car.

Now living in a tent, Amal struggles to provide for her children. Her younger daughters, Rimas and Malak, are still wearing summer clothes despite the arrival of winter.

“Everything is expensive… children’s clothes, shoes, everything,” she says.

Amal tries to make do with what is available, but it is not enough to meet her daughters’ needs.

Rain also seeps through the damaged tarpaulins covering the family’s tent. With no heating equipment, they rely on blankets to keep warm.

“We have no means of heating ourselves; we just cover the children with blankets,” she says.

Amal fears another storm will bring more rain and cold. “We just pray that God makes this winter easier for the people living in tents,” she says.

The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) says 94 percent of Gaza’s population urgently needs shelter assistance. Some 65 percent of households live in tents or makeshift shelters, while 650,000 children need winter aid, including warm clothing and blankets.

By September, aid agencies had secured enough winter clothing for just 9,000 households and bedding for 50,000 – far short of what was needed. OCHA said funding shortages were further hampering preparations for winter.

The UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has warned that winter conditions put children in Gaza at increased risk of hypothermia and respiratory infections – at least 11 children died from hypothermia last winter, according to the Gaza Ministry of Health. The agency is seeking $97.5m for its 2026-2027 winter response, which aims to support 540,000 children and their families across Gaza and the occupied West Bank.

Recent rains have worsened the crisis. UNICEF said on November 9 that flooding had affected more than 106,000 people, while some 950,000 displaced Palestinians were living in flood-prone areas.

More than three years into Israel’s genocidal war, which has killed more than 74,600 Palestinians and wounded over 176,000, homes and livelihoods across Gaza have been devastated. Nearly two million people have been displaced, many repeatedly, and hundreds of thousands remain in tents and damaged shelters.

As the war enters its fourth year, unemployment and rising prices have made basic necessities increasingly unaffordable, leaving families struggling to protect their children from the cold.

In Gaza City’s Rimal market, 25-year-old shop owner Mohammed Abu Shanar sees the same struggle among his customers. Many ask about winter clothing prices, but leave without buying anything.

“The prices are very high. They are not within everyone’s reach. People come in, ask how much something costs, and then leave because they cannot afford it,” he says.

Mohammed sells around four to six winter tracksuits a day. He says many children from nearby displacement camps still wear short-sleeved or lightweight clothes despite the cold.

He attributes the high prices to shortages of goods entering Gaza – the result of continued Israeli restrictions – and the cost of buying stock from wholesalers.

“First, there is a shortage of goods. The wholesalers hold on to their prices, and the merchandise is expensive for us, too. If these items were selling for 20 shekels ($6.25) or 25 shekels ($7.80) instead of 40 shekels ($12.60) or 50 shekels ($15.70), perhaps people would be able to buy them,” he says.

Mohammed says he has invested more than 20,000 shekels (about $6,265) in winter stock, but after three weeks of sales he has recovered less than 5,000 shekels (about $1,570).

People like Anas Hamad simply don’t have the money to buy from traders like Mohammed.

Anas and his family are displaced from Beit Hanoun in northern Gaza. Before the war, he ran a supermarket employing his four brothers. The war destroyed their homes and business, leaving all five university graduates without work.

With no income and unable to afford new clothes, Anas relies on second-hand markets and hand-me-downs to dress his three children.

He recalls how his five-year-old daughter, Jana, asked him for a new shirt. He could only point to the one she was wearing, which had belonged to her brother.

The family has lived in their badly torn tent for around two years. Despite his wife’s efforts to sew and patch it, rainwater enters from above and below. During the recent downpour, their bedding and belongings were soaked.

Anas says his three-year-old child was trembling from the cold, while the sound of rain hitting the tent frightened the children.

“I have to choose between buying food for my children, getting them warm clothes and blankets, or buying tarpaulins to protect our tent from the coming rain,” he says. “I don’t know what to prioritise or what to leave behind.”
https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2026/.summary: Family of 18 living in makeshift camp in Gaza City, Gaza Strip, has been displaced six times during Israel's genocidal war. UNICEF has warned that winter conditions at least 11 children died of hypothermia and hypothermics.

https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/liveblo.title: Italy 3-1 France: UEFA Nations League – as it happened
https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/liveblo.author: Patrick Keddie,Adam Hancock
https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/liveblo.text:
This page is now closed, but a summary of the game is available below, and you can click here for our full match report. Thanks for joining us at Al Jazeera Sport.

Thanks for joining our live coverage of Italy vs France in the Nations League.

We’ll be back soon for more international football as the Nations League group phase reaches a climax.

But, for now, from me, Adam Hancock, and on behalf of my colleague, Patrick Keddie, goodbye!

You can read a full recap of Italy’s famous victory here.

In case you missed it earlier … Manchester United have sacked manager Michael Carrick after a miserable start to the season.

Carrick’s departure, which had been imminent after United made their worst start to the English top flight in 40 years, was announced on Thursday by the club, which said it would “appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible”.

United, 13-time Premier League champions, have been heavily linked with US Men’s National Team coach Mauricio Pochettino.

Italy head coach Roberto Mancini has been speaking to RAI Sport.

“A great performance; the lads did so well. I am happy for the fans and hope they enjoyed themselves,” he said.

He was also asked about conceding the first goal: “Unfortunately, these things happen. We managed to stay calm, continued playing, and eventually thoroughly deserved the victory.

“Conceding a goal against France after 10 minutes could’ve destroyed us; instead, we stayed calm, and we got back on track.”

Les Bleus have work to do in their final Nations League fixture in Lyon on Sunday.

They’ll host Turkiye – a side that have already been eliminated from the group phase.

France need a point to guarantee qualification, although they could also go through if they lose and Italy beat Belgium in Brussels.

Those final fixtures take place on Sunday evening at 19:45 GMT.

Remarkably, tonight’s victory was Italy’s first home win over France in 64 years!

They last defeated Les Bleus back in September 2024, also coming from behind to win 3-1 in Paris.

It’s a funny old game.

Italy move to the top of the group but neither the Azurri nor France have secured qualification for the quarterfinals just yet.

More on that in a moment, but an update on the other game in this group first. Belgium came from behind to secure victory away at Turkiye and keep their qualification hopes alive.

Kevin De Bruyne and Charles De Ketelaere scored within three minutes of each other as the Red Devils recovered from conceding an early goal.
https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/liveblo.summary: Italy beat France 3-1 in their first Nations League match in 64 years. Michael Carrick was sacked by Manchester United after a miserable start to the season. The win was Italy's first home win over France in 64 Years. The match was also Italy's second home win in 64years.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: Prominent Israeli settler denied entry into France
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.author: Al Jazeera Staff
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
The head of an organisation representing illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank has been denied entry into France.

Israel denounced the move as “completely unacceptable” on Wednesday after prominent Israeli settler Yossi Dagan said French authorities turned him back last week when he flew into a Paris airport.

Dagan, who is a member of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party, was “subject to an administrative ban from the territory due to his active role in implementing the settlement policy in the West Bank” according to his office.

“Settlement building is contrary to international law and undermines the two-state solution,” the French ministry said.

According to the ministry, Dagan was “pulled aside and questioned” at the airport’s passport control before being informed that he was banned from entering French territory “due to his active role in implementing the settlement policy in the West Bank.”

Dagan said Wednesday that he was undeterred by the ban and was proud to “build the historic homeland of the Jewish people”, while Israeli’s foreign ministry said the measures against Dagan were based on “political and ideological grounds”.

“Israel will demand an explanation from the French government and consider its next steps accordingly,” it added.

The incident comes amid growing tension between Israel and European countries around illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank, which have proliferated under Netanyahu’s government.

France, along with 11 other countries, announced its intention to restrict trade with ⁠⁠⁠⁠illegal settlements in the Palestinian territory in September, which spurred outrage from Israeli officials.

On Monday, a French parliamentary committee approved a bill banning the imports of settlement goods and services contributing to settlement construction, with further discussion scheduled for November 19.

There are at least 148 illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank and 15 in occupied East Jerusalem, now home to about 750,000 Israelis, according to Israeli anti-settlement watchdog Peace Now.

Earlier this year, France banned far-right Israeli ministers, Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, who are both members of Netanyahu’s cabinet.
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.summary: Yossi Dagan says he was turned back by French authorities last week. He is a member of Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party. Dagan was told he was banned from entering French territory due to his role in implementing the settlement policy.

https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/democr.title: Democrats launch Nvidia investigation, write scathing letter on Huang’s ‘scheme’ with Trump
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/democr.author: Julie Bort
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/democr.text:
Democrats on Thursday opened an inquiry into how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China. Earlier on Thursday, the company ousted its CEO Jensen Huang. He also agreed to testify to a different set of Republican-led Congressional committees.

Huang was removed from the company he founded after he confessed to an extramarital affair amid reports of a relationship with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. (He has since been accused of having more affairs, with Nvidia employees.)

The alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, was an executive of Nvidia customer Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that U.S. officials suspect of helping route advanced Nvidia chips into China. The Democratic inquiry comes from Rep. Richard Neal (D-Mass.), the top Democrat on the House Ways and Means Committee, and Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), the top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee. As the minority party, they can ask questions but can’t compel answers.

Their humdinger of a letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick asks the department to preserve records about an arrangement they find questionable and, they allege, illegal.

“The scheme worked like this,” as the letter describes it. President Trump agreed to sales of Nvidia’s H200 chips to China as long as the chips, manufactured by Taiwan, were first shipped to the United States. On arriving, Trump added a tariff “effectively taking a cut of Nvidia’s sales to China through what appears to be an unconstitutional export tax system,” the letter said. Then the Commerce Department, under Lutnick, issued an export license.

By the way, the deal between Trump and Nvidia to share revenue was public. In August 2025, Nvidia and AMD both agreed to share 15% of their revenue from chip sales to China with the U.S. government as part of a deal to secure export licenses, the AP reported at the time.

But the letter questions why Lutnick continued to allow Megaspeed to buy chips even after he was reportedly informed by US intelligence of their suspicions of Alice Huang and of Jensen Huang’s relationship with her. It questionswhy the department reportedly green-lit other Asian companies to buy Nvidia chips “with no physical presence at their listed addresses.” So the inquiry is aimed at the administration, not just Nvidia and Huang.

The letter also questions how Nvidia’s donations to Trump’s projects factored in. It notes that the export deal was approved after Trump learned of “Mr. Huang’s compromised position” in sleeping with an alleged spy, and after Nvidia donated $26 million toward Trump’s projects, including the ballroom. It appears to be asking if Trump used his knowledge of the affair to secure donations from Nvidia.

Interestingly, in a “60 Minutes” interview with President Trump that aired on Sunday, he mentioned how he and his team had threatened an unnamed AI exec with jail, and after that, the exec “totally changed.”

This Congressional investigation into Nvidia’s China sales and its dealings with Trump is the second one, so far, since news of the alleged spy affair broke. The Republican-led group involves leaders from the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and the House Intelligence Committee. That group has demanded that Huang come to them and testify in a closed-door session. They had threatened to subpoena him if he didn’t voluntarily agree. On Thursday, after his resignation, he agreed.

The alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, was an executive of Nvidia customer Megaspeed

https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/muse-c.title: Muse can now place calls to U.S. businesses — if you pay
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/muse-c.author: Sarah Perez
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/muse-c.text:
After initially testing the feature in September, Meta’s consumer AI agent Muse is now able to place calls to U.S. businesses on behalf of its users. However, only paid subscribers have access to the feature, the company says.

Meta’s Muse, which now has over 10 million users, the company said last month, has been working to make consumer AI a mainstream product for everyday users. Placing calls is one of the ways it aims to get there, as it could handle another task on people’s to-do lists.

Notes Alexandr Wang, Meta’s Chief AI officer and head of its Superintelligence Labs division, the feature could be used to take care of calls people don’t want to make, like those to their cable company, the DMV, or to a restaurant that doesn’t offer online reservations.

Previously, only a select number of Muse early adopters were able to try this feature after asking the AI for access. Now, anyone who pays for Muse can make this type of request. Currently, Muse subscription plans start at $20 per month for 500 million Muse tokens per week. Heavier AI users can opt to pay $100 per month for 3 billion tokens.

Muse is not the only AI agent able to place calls to businesses; the startup Instinct has been offering a similar option, as has Google’s Gemini. However, while the AI tools are now certainly capable of handling the task, the reception on the other end of the line can be mixed. Many businesses and receptionists hang up on calls from AI agents as soon as they identify that it’s not a human on the phone. But with AI now better able to mimic a real human voice, being able to tell the difference between a customer and an AI working on the customer’s behalf will get tougher.

Despite the challenges, this feature is one that could appeal to consumers who have grown frustrated with the state of customer service over the years. For too long, customers have been forced to navigate complex phone trees, and then sit on hold waiting for a human representative to pick up. If they’re lucky, that person can actually help them, and not transfer them to another department. Now, those consumers could potentially use their AI, with its infinite patience, for this tedious task instead.

While calls remain a paid-only feature for the time being, the recently added option to make a Muse email address will soon roll out to free users, Wang said this week.

https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/nebius.title: Nebius tests the neocloud playbook with $40 billion in planned spending
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/nebius.author: Rebecca Bellan
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/nebius.text:
In its third-quarter earnings call Thursday, the neocloud company Nebius laid out $40 billion in planned spending for 2027, far more than Wall Street had expected. It’s an ambitious plan, but it rests on a string of planned projects that are already starting to show cracks.

Nebius plans to fund the buildout by relying on customer pre-payments and loans backed by customer contracts — essentially using the future value of its data centers to finance their construction. But that can be a risky strategy if those projects get bogged down by delays or cancellations.

“Building at this scale is hard, and delays are part of our industry right now,” CEO Arkady Volozh said during Thursday’s earnings call. “We are not immune.”

The earnings announcement comes on the heels of reports that Microsoft is cooling on neocloud deals that aren’t delivering on time. That’s a problem for companies like Nebius, whose financing strategy is becoming more dependent on repayments. Because if it can’t get to capacity on time, it will keep piling on costs while revenues slip.

One of Nebius’s largest customers is Microsoft, which is paying for AI computing capacity at a Vineland, New Jersey data center that is now months behind schedule. Nebius’s contract with Microsoft is worth up to $19.4 billion, but it’s already letting deadlines slip. Only just over half of the Microsoft capacity is now planned for delivery by the end of the year, with the rest coming in Q2 2027.

The delay is because DataOne, the third party operator of the site, “decided to wind down the temporary generation faster than it was expected,” according to Andrey Korolenko, chief product and infrastructure officer, as the site switches over to Bloom Energy fuel cells.

Still, that transition wasn’t entirely by choice. In August, the investigative site Floodlight identified at least 45 natural gas generators in operation at the DataOne site, even though it had not received any permits for operating gas generators. New Jersey regulators fined the DataOne facility $1.1 million in response, finding that the use of the generators violated federal law.

DataOne is also facing a noise-complaint lawsuit from nearby residents over a constant humming noise allegedly emitted by the data center.

According to Nebius’s summary of its Microsoft contract, Microsoft can terminate affected service after a grace period if dates are missed and no alternative capacity is offered. The tranches were originally meant to be deployed in 2025 and 2026, so a Q2 2027 delivery date falls well beyond that window. The contract also includes financial penalties for late delivery.

Nebius said that Microsoft “has been part of the planning process.” Nebius did not say whether Microsoft has agreed to the new dates, but Microsoft has not publicly canceled anything.

TechCrunch has reached out to Nebius, Microsoft, and DataOne for comment.

On the call, Marc Boroditsky, Nebius’s chief revenue officer said the company’s deals with Microsoft and Meta both came with significant prepayment, which arrived long before delivery. But Bloomberg reported last week that Microsoft is tightening oversight on projects run by third parties, including Nebius, IREN, and Nscale, and debating whether it’s worth signing new agreements. Microsoft also sent employees to the site in New Jersey, per Bloomberg.

In its own quarterly earnings report, Microsoft noted that its capex spend was lower than expected due to third-party delays. The company is clearly not above pulling back from planned agreements where its partner doesn’t meet its share of the bargain. Bloomberg also reported that Microsoft won’t use an option to more than double its Nscale agreement for a Texas data center and recently stopped being an anchor customer for Nscale’s planned Essex site after power delays.

Nebius says the delays it faces are coming from sites it doesn’t control, with the data centers it is building itself coming online on time or ahead of schedule. Those, Nebius says, will supply most of its new capacity from 2027. New deals signed in Q3 came with prepayments that more than cover the cost of building capacity behind them, says Boroditsky. Nebius ended the quarter with $7.4 billion in cash.

Total prepayments plus asset-backed financing of investment-grade contracts are expected to cover up to 85% of the $40 to $45 billion 2027 capex spend. CFO Maria Del Dado Alonso Sanchez named Microsoft and Meta as contracts that can be financed this way. Boroditsky also said Nebius could “tap prepayments to shore up any additional cash requirements.”

Nebius forecast 2027 revenue of $12 to $13 billion, and said it expects to break even on a pre-tax basis by the fourth quarter.

Nebius reported third-quarter revenue of $981 million, up 571% from a year earlier. Roughly a third of that was a one-time payment tied to a new partnership model. Nebius cut its 2026 revenue forecast by $200 million to $3 billion, citing delays to third-party sites like New Jersey. Shares ended the day down 17%.
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/nebius.summary: Nebius laid out $40 billion in planned spending for 2027, far more than Wall Street had expected. Nebius plans to fund the buildout by relying on customer pre-payments and loans backed by customer contracts. Nebus plans to use future value of its data centers to finance their construction.

https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/google.title: Google’s latest Search upgrade promises better answers to your most complicated questions
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/google.author: Sarah Perez
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/google.text:
Google Search is getting better at understanding complicated questions, including those with multiple parts, highly specific requests, or confusing typos. The updates are coming via the company’s newly released Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which Google claims is its “biggest model improvement to Search yet.”

While Google’s frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, are best at deep reasoning for hard problems, Hydrogen is designed for fast execution across a variety of agentic workflows, or tasks in which an AI carries out multiple steps on its own, the company explained in an announcement.

The idea behind the model’s release is that using the most powerful model isn’t always needed — sometimes a faster, cheaper, and reasonably smart one will do. Google says Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash, its previous fast model, but it’s still pretty smart, even beating the more powerful Gemini 4 Argon on one broad intelligence benchmark, the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, at its default high thinking level.

In Search, Hydrogen brings several improvements, including a better understanding of user intent, the ability to offer more helpful links and visual responses, and better answers across the different languages supported by Google’s AI Mode.

In terms of intent, Google says Hydrogen can handle more nuanced and complicated questions more quickly. This means people can ask their questions in their natural train of thought, including those that have multiple parts or that include highly specific requests. Hydrogen is also better at navigating hard-to-understand typos, Google says. Because of its improvements and better ability to follow instructions and call the right tools, Hydrogen is able to more precisely address each part of a user’s question.

Its advanced reasoning also improves Search’s fan-out technique, which breaks down a single user’s prompt into multiple subqueries. This allows people to discover websites related to the query that they may have otherwise missed, the blog post explains.

The addition of Hydrogen to Search will also mean more images, structured responses, comparison tables, and custom tools will appear as visual responses to users’ queries in AI Mode.

Google also says Hydrogen can work on its own for everyday work in areas like writing code, running tests, or verifying code changes, or it can be paired with Carbon and Argon in workflows that combine several models.

The model offers four thinking levels: low, medium, high (default), and a new, extra-high tier (“xhigh”), all of which are designed to complete tasks faster with fewer output tokens.

On multi-step tasks like deep research, data analysis, and broad codebase navigation, Hydrogen ranks No. 5 on Agent Arena’s benchmarks, the company pointed out.

In addition to Search, Gemini 4 Hydrogen is coming to all tiers of Google’s AI Studio, the Gemini API, the Gemini App, and the paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google’s Antigravity development platform.

Google says the Hydrogen update is rolling out to all Search users globally.

The updates are coming via the company’s newly released Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which Google claims is its ‘biggest model improvement to Search yet’

https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/nectar.title: Nectar launches an AI agent to automate creator discovery and outreach for brands
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/nectar.author: Lauren Forristal
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/nectar.text:
Nectar, an AI-powered operating system for marketing, is launching a new AI agent designed to take a lot of the manual work out of influencer marketing, from finding the right creators to contacting them, managing partnerships, and tracking results.

Founded by sisters Misbah and Farah Uraizee, both former Meta employees, Nectar came out of stealth last year and uses AI agents to help brands manage social media, customer conversations, content moderation, creator partnerships, and competitor research.

Announced Thursday, its new “Creator Agent” can search for creators, check their content and brand partnerships, send personalized messages, coordinate collaborations, and monitor how campaigns perform. Instead of having marketing teams spend weeks scrolling through social media, building spreadsheets, and sending individual DMs, Nectar wants its agent to handle much of that work automatically.

Nectar joins other companies introducing agentic AI assistants designed to automate influencer outreach, including Aspire and GRIN. The launch also comes as more brands turn to creators to reach customers. U.S. spending on creator advertising is expected to reach $44 billion in 2026, according to the Interactive Advertising Bureau. As companies work with hundreds or even thousands of creators, keeping track of relationships and measuring results can get pretty difficult.

Nectar says its Creator Agent searches more than 300 million creator profiles to find potential partners, including smaller creators who may not yet have a large following but are gaining traction. The system analyzes videos to understand what creators post about, how their content fits a brand, and whether their previous partnerships are appropriate. It also checks brand safety by reviewing content in context rather than simply searching for specific keywords.

Nectar then creates ranked lists of recommendations and adds new matches as creators become more popular.

Once it finds a potential match, the agent can draft and send messages in a brand’s voice, create custom landing pages to collect creator information, and help manage contracts, product gifting, and shipping details. It also remembers previous conversations and interactions, so brands can keep track of relationships without relying on spreadsheets.

“Brands can share voice guidelines in any format, and Nectar picks up the rest from their history,” CEO Misbah Uraizee tells TechCrunch. “On top of that sits a set of proprietary guardrails that keep every draft on tone and in context. Nectar understands what is being said in a video, reads the tone of the conversation, and knows the difference between a quote post on X and a TikTok comment section. A brand should not sound identical in both, and with Nectar it doesn’t.”

Another feature looks for personal milestones in creators’ lives, such as an engagement, a new baby, or completing a marathon. The agent can then suggest a personalized message or gift, helping brands build relationships that feel less like one-off advertising deals.

Creator Agent is available today globally and covers Instagram creators and TikTokers.

The company plans to make the agent available through its Model Context Protocol (MCP), allowing teams to use it through AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot, as well as their own custom-built agents.

This past May, Nectar raised a $30 million Series A round led by Menlo Ventures and its Anthology Fund, which is a joint initiative launched with Anthropic.

https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/micros.title: Microsoft’s Outlook email hit by new outage
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/micros.author: Zack Whittaker
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/micros.text:
Microsoft said its Outlook email service is currently experiencing an outage, preventing both business and consumer users from accessing their inboxes.

The issue was initially flagged as affecting the U.S. and the Americas, and later expanded to affect “any region.”

Microsoft hasn’t given a specific cause, but said that it was providing updates in its admin center, which wasn’t reachable at the time of publication. In a post on X for users who can’t access the admin center, Microsoft said some of its infrastructure was experiencing “elevated load,” and that it was “redistributing connection traffic across our broader worldwide infrastructure to help balance the load.”

In its latest update, Microsoft attributed this incident to “a large number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable,” for reasons it did not explain. Microsoft said it continues to investigate the outage.

Microsoft says its video conferencing tool Teams, file sharing platform SharePoint, and its AI tool Copilot are also unavailable. The company says its Defender XDR security system is also affected by the outage.

Consumers are also unable to access their OneDrive storage, Office (for the web), and several other Microsoft services during the ongoing outage.

TechCrunch will reach out to Microsoft for comment, as soon as our own email service has resumed.

The company’s last major incident was in September, when a days-long outage hit Microsoft 365, its online productivity suite that includes Outlook. During that outage, Microsoft blamed a “core authentication configuration” issue that prevented users from accessing the service.
