https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-14/w.author: Kate Christian
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-14/w.text:
BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Multiple police vehicles were sent to a rural property in Keysbrook in Perth's south.  (ABC News)

Police say a 44-year-old man was shot dead just before 9am (AWST) on a rural property in Keysbrook, about 70km south-east of the Perth CBD.

A 38-year-old man, who is known to the victim, was apprehended at the scene.

A woman and her child were inside the property at the time but were unharmed.

Homicide detectives are investigating after a 44-year-old man was shot dead at a rural property in Perth's south this morning, triggering a major police operation.

A 38-year-old man, who is known to the victim, is in custody after heavily armed police swarmed the Hilltop Orchard property in Keysbrook, about 70 kilometres south-east of the Perth CBD.

Police swarmed an orchard in Keysbrook after a serious incident.  (ABC News)

The victim's partner — a woman in her 40s — and her young son were inside the residence at the time of the shooting, but managed to flee to a neighbour's house where they called emergency services about 8.40am (AWST).

Members of the public were initially told to avoid the area as officers from the Tactical Response Group (TRG) descended on the secluded rural property, which includes an orchard, although it is unclear whether it remains operational.

The property was cordoned off as police contained the incident.  (ABC News: Lauren Smith)

Dramatic aerial footage showed officers systematically searching multiple structures, including a house, shipping containers and tin sheds, to ensure there was no ongoing threat to the community.

Detective Senior Sergeant Stephen Cleal said the 38-year-old man was found sitting in a vehicle at the property and was apprehended without incident.

Two officers stood guard over the man who was placed inside a police vehicle. (ABC News)

"It's believed that the person we have custody is known to the deceased, however, they are not family," he said.

Police seized a firearm from the residence and they do not believe the man in custody is a licensed firearms holder.

Detective Senior Sergeant Cleal said the mother and son who managed to flee had been confronted with a "horrific" scene.

"I'm glad they are not injured but what a terrible thing for them to go through, so my thoughts go out to them," he said.

An aerial view of the property, which includes an orchard. (ABC News)

He reassured the community that while the investigation was still in its infancy, there was no information to suggest the community was at risk.

"What has occurred in this house is tragic to say the least and my thoughts go out to the family and friends who knew the deceased," he said.

"This would have been a very confronting scene for all the [responders] who attended, so my thoughts go out to them."

Multiple police vehicles were sent to the property. (ABC News)

At least eight police vehicles, forensics officers and three St John ambulance crews were sent to the scene.

In a statement, police said the investigation remained ongoing.

https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-14/a.author: Clare Armstrong
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-14/a.text:
BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Topic:
Climate Change

Anthony Albanese and Chris Bowen were caught on a hot mic talking about phone radiation and "dicks" at the COP31 summit.

A private exchange between Anthony Albanese and Chris Bowen was inadvertently recorded at the COP31 summit in Türkiye.

The prime minister's office said the pair were joking between meetings, but the Coalition has criticised the hot mic moment as "weird and gross".

Mr Albanese has travelled to the Philippines for the ASEAN summit, while Mr Bowen remains in Türkiye.

A conversation between Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen about phone radiation and "dicks" has been caught on camera on the sidelines of a UN conference.

The Coalition has criticised the hot mic moment as "weird and gross", accusing the pair of behaving like "14-year-old schoolboys".

Mr Albanese's office said the pair was sharing a "joke" between meetings when the exchange was recorded by Australian media at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye.

The comments were captured shortly before a business roundtable spruiking renewable energy transition investment opportunities in Australia began overnight on Friday.

Anthony Albanese left Türkiye shortly after a business roundtable. (AAP)

Cameras were rolling ahead of the event, during which time Mr Albanese and Mr Bowen were privately chatting to each other.

Mr Albanese put his phone in his jacket pocket and — as he did so — told Mr Bowen he had heard it was better to store the device away from the heart because "it can interfere with your rhythm".

Mr Bowen responded in a joking tone, asking if it was because the phone was "a little bit radioactive".

The prime minister laughed, saying the idea "makes absolute sense".

Mr Bowen then responded he was more conscious about putting his phone in his pants pocket.

Mr Albanese asked, "Because of your dick?"

The pair laughed and Mr Bowen agreed, adding it was "arguably more important than the heart".

On Sunday, Liberal deputy leader Jane Hume said the gaffe undermined Labor's message about pitching Australia to the world on climate.

"It's bad enough that these guys sent almost 200 bureaucrats to Türkiye at a cost of more than $2 million and spent $36,000 [sic] of your taxpayer money on a coffee cart so that Greta Thunberg could have a free latte, but they justified it on the basis they were 'selling Australia to the world', 'attracting investment from overseas'," she said.

"Well, great salesmen you clowns are.

"The only thing you've attracted to Australia is ridicule on the world stage."

The exchange, which did not appear to be overheard by anyone in the room but was captured by a news camera microphone preparing to record the opening remarks at the event, was later broadcast by Channel 7 after it was noticed in production.

A spokesperson for Mr Albanese's office said, "They were having a joke in between meetings."

Labor frontbencher Murray Watt agreed that the comments were made in jest.

"This is really just about people having a joke," he said.

Mr Watt laughed off a question about where he kept his own phone, and defended Australia's presence and performance at COP31.

"I know there's been a lot of criticism from some quarters about every aspect of this COP, but the reality is participating in and in fact leading the discussions at COP is in Australia's national interest," he said.

During the official proceedings of the business roundtable, the prime minister made a pitch to international investors to back Australia's clean energy transition.

"If you're an investor, there's nowhere you'd rather be than Australia," he said.

Mr Albanese said having abundant renewable resources, critical minerals and a stable investment environment meant Australia was well placed to capitalise on the multi-trillion-dollar industry.

The prime minister left Türkiye shortly after the roundtable to travel to the Philippines for the ASEAN summit in Manila.

Mr Bowen has remained in Antalya, where he is playing a critical role as the co-president of negotiations for COP31.

https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-14/q.title: Questions remain after Nvidia CEO's departure
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-14/q.author: Annabel Bowles
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-14/q.text:
BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Jensen Huang was one of the world's most influential figures in the tech and AI industry. (Reuters: Mike Blake)

Mounting speculation over an espionage plot against Jensen Huang and his multiple alleged affairs reached a tipping point on Friday, when the tech billionaire quit as Nvidia's CEO.

The controversy centred around his relationship with Alice Huang, who US intelligence reportedly suspects to be a Chinese spy, before claims emerged he had another two extra-marital affairs.

While Mr Huang's resignation puts an end to his long reign over Nvidia, questions about America's national security and the US president's knowledge of the whole saga remain.

China's foreign ministry said allegations of spying in relation to Alice Huang and Jensen Huang (no relation) were "unsubstantiated" and "smears against China". (Reuters: CTI)

When reports of an espionage plot against Mr Huang first emerged almost a week ago, top Republicans called on the tech executive to front Congress later this month.

Senator Tim Scott reiterated those demands after Mr Huang's resignation, saying there were "serious concerns" to address.

Separately the chairs of three House committees — the foreign affairs panel, the China select committee and the intelligence committee — wrote to Mr Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter requiring them to appear for closed-door transcribed interviews on December 1 and 2.

After news broke of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset Nvidia's value plummeted. Why?

Mr Huang and Mr Teter have not publicly commented on the requests, but they could face subpoenas to compel their appearances.

"There are clear national security concerns that need to be addressed immediately," the three committee chairs wrote in the letter.

Mr Huang is also yet to comment publicly after reports emerged he allegedly had another two extra-marital affairs — both with Nvidia employees.

His last statement was on Sunday, local time, when he admitted to being "unfaithful" to his wife of over 40 years but did not name who he had been intimate with.

In that statement, he said he was "committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security".

Meanwhile, Nvidia and Mr Huang are facing a ‌proposed class action accusing them ‌of ⁠defrauding ‌shareholders.

Next to Mr Huang, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has been called on to testify in front of Congress on concerns he did not do enough to restrict AI chip shipments to China.

In December 2025 Donald Trump allowed Nvidia to sell its advanced chips to China in exchange for a cut of the sales, after Mr Huang argued that restrictions only accelerated Beijing's own AI development.

That was despite concerns from both sides of Congress about China's access to the technology.

Howard Lutnick is facing pressure over whether the US government was properly overseeing Nvidia's exports to China. (Reuters: Elizabeth Frantz)

Mr Lutnick has also been criticised for the administration's refusal to add dozens of Chinese companies to a trade blacklist.

In June, Reuters reported the Trump administration had held ⁠off adding more than 100 other companies flagged as national security risks to the list.

The US ⁠has not added to the list since October 2025, the longest stretch between new postings in more than a decade.

Previous reports said that Mr Lutnick's US Commerce Department had not blacklisted new Chinese companies for fear of escalating tensions between the US and China.

Under-Secretary of Commerce Jeffrey Kessler has been called on to testify at a December 3 hearing as well.

The Commerce Department did not respond to Reuters' request for comment.

In America's pursuit to lead the AI race, Mr Huang had become a close ally of Mr Trump and was one of the few people known to have a direct line to him.

He has visited the White House at least five times during Mr Trump's second term, is part of a council advising the president on science and technology, and accompanied Mr Trump on a trip to Beijing in May.

Just months ago Jensen Huang was on stage speaking about AI when he took a phone call from Donald Trump.

The Washington Post reported in mid-October that Nvidia committed $US25 million ($36.7 million) for Mr Trump's contentious White House ballroom project, while the president disclosed buying and selling Nvidia stock earlier this year.

The New York Times reported Mr Trump was briefed on intelligence findings about a suspected espionage effort against Mr Huang about a year ago, and took no action.

When asked in recent days whether he wished he had acted sooner on that information, Mr Trump said "I don't think so" and maintained that Mr Huang was an "honourable guy".

The president has continued to stand by Mr Huang and said the tech billionaire told him he had no idea Ms Huang was a spy, and that he believed him.

On the day Mr Huang admitted to his affair, Nvidia announced it had called an independent investigation into whether their then-chief executive had been the "target of a foreign intelligence effort".

But early in the piece, the company said it had "no reason to believe" either US national security or company secrets had been compromised.

There was no mention of the investigation when Nvidia announced its current executive vice-president and chief financial officer Colette Kress was stepping in as interim CEO.

Instead, Nvidia's new chair Harvey C Jones said: "We expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption."

It remains to be seen as to whether the investigation finds evidence Mr Huang gave away sensitive information — or whether its findings are publicly revealed.

The fallout after Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia boss.

Ms Huang, who's been identified as a former executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, has not commented publicly since the Nvidia scandal erupted.

The chief executive of the world's most valuable company and a close ally of Donald Trump admitted to an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Here's what we know.

China has denied she is a spy and US Attorney-General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Justice Department had not yet reached a conclusion on whether she was or not.

Last year, Megaspeed was accused of illicitly shipping advanced Nvidia computer chips into China, but in December said there was "no evidence" of such exports.

Singaporean authorities also said they questioned Ms Huang and confiscated her passport last year as part of an investigation into Megaspeed's exports.

They concluded there wasn't enough evidence that she had committed a crime, but suspected she provided "inaccurate information" to downplay her role at Megaspeed.

Ms Huang left Singapore in February when she received her passport back and was banned from re-entering the country.

She is currently living in Beijing with the knowledge of security officials, Bloomberg News reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The Singapore home affairs ministry said investigations into Megaspeed and six individuals were ongoing.

Megaspeed said on Thursday it took compliance obligations under US export control laws "extremely seriously", adding it had cooperated with US inspections.

https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-14/y.title: Australia wins six Youth Olympics medals as African Games hailed
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-14/y.author: Simon Smale
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-14/y.text:
BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Marley Dodd and Elsie Apps were Australia's flag bearers at the Youth Olympic Games. (Supplied: AOC)

Australia has come away from the 2026 Youth Olympic Games with six medals as Senegal held up its hands for the Olympic movement in Africa.

The Dakar Games were the first Olympic event to be hosted in Africa, with organisers hailing the success as further proof of the continent's ability to host major international competitions.

South Africa, which staged the men's FIFA World Cup in 2010, is among countries in talks with the IOC about hosting the 2036 Olympic Games.

Nearly 2,700 athletes aged 14 to 17 competed across 25 sports and 153 medal events over two weeks in Senegal.

"I think that everyone came here with certain expectations and I think those expectations have been far exceeded," International Olympic Committee President Kirsty Coventry said on Thursday.

"It has been an magnificent journey. It has been extremely magical.

"I think we've shown the world the capability that we have and now we need to choose to take that forward," the Zimbabwean two-time Olympic champion added.

Australia's six medals included four silvers and two bronzes.

Boxer Marley Dodd claimed silver in the men's 55kg event, while Mackenzie Macdonald claimed Australia's first ever taekwondo Youth Olympic Games medal in the 49kg category.

Marley Dodd won silver on the penulimate day of the competition. (Supplied: AOC)

Australia's cyclists excelled, with Elsie Apps winning silver and Caleb McKenzie bronze on the same day in the women's and men's road races.

Tasmania's McKenzie, who was diagnosed with the autoimmune illness Hashimoto’s disease earlier this year, led the race via a brave breakaway right up until the final lap before sprinting for bronze.

"I wasn't on the bike for a long time," McKenzie told Olympics.com.

"I couldn't ride my bike, I couldn't train and nothing really went well for me.

Caleb McKenzie rode in the breakaway for the majority of the men's road race. (Supplied: AOC)

"I finally pulled it together at the end of this year and had a really good ride. I had the confidence. We talked about it before we raced about having confidence in yourself, and we said, 'If you believe, you achieve'."

Apps, meanwhile, sprinted to silver.

"I'm so grateful for the opportunity that I was given to be able to go out there and get a medal," Apps said.

"It's been really inspiring. To have a little taste of what it would be like, it really makes you want more and hopefully I can make it there [to Brisbane 2032]."

Elsie Apps came second in the women's road race. (Supplied: AOC)

Queensland's beach volleyball pairing Thomas Turner and Ryan Edgar won bronze, while the women's rugby sevens teams were only denied gold in an extra-time thriller against Kenya, which claimed a first ever Olympic rugby sevens title for the nation.

Apps and Dodd were named as closing ceremony flag bearers, with Chef de Mission Kenny Wallace said the success gave him a lot of positivity heading to Brisbane 2032.

"To summarise the last two weeks … it would come down to being proud," he said.

"I'm inspired by what our Australian sporting ecosystem has in store leading into LA28 and into Brisbane 2032.

"When we came into this campaign, we hoped Dakar would become that important milestone for our emerging athletes with Brisbane 2032 on the horizon.

"It's been incredibly inspiring to see the athletes developing even further here in Dakar and understanding what it means to be part of an Australian team.

"That is what a Youth Olympic Games can do. I really look forward to seeing some of the faces that we've had in the team here in Brisbane."

Elisabeth Diatta was one of Senegal's gold medal winners at her country's first home Olympic event. (Getty Images: Francois Nel)

Beach wrestling's Olympic debut brought particular pride to Senegal, where wrestling is a national sport, with 16-year-old Elisabeth Diatta's win the first for the host nation.

Other Youth Olympic debuts included baseball5, a simplified version of baseball, skateboarding, and the Chinese martial art wushu.

China finished with the most gold medals, 18, followed by Japan with 11 and Russia with eight.

Three African countries came next: Egypt with six, and Ethiopia and Senegal with five each.

The IOC staged the first summer Youth Olympic Games in 2010 in Singapore, however it has delayed naming the host for the next event, set to take place in 2030.

Kirsty Coventry hailed Africa's first Olympic event. (Supplied: AOC)

"We took a pause … and we are analysing and that's where we are. We are still analysing. The data we will collect from Dakar will be added," Coventry said.

"As we move forward, the way we want to engage with young people is extremely important. We have to analyse what will be the best way for the movement to continue in the future."

Coventry noted that just 15 per cent of athletes who have competed at the Youth Olympic Games have gone on to compete at the full Olympics.

Jess Fox and Emma McKeown are notable Australians who made the leap, winning gold at the Youth Olympic Games before going on to claim 20 Summer Olympic Games medals between them.

"We have to be very realistic about what we want the Youth Olympics to be," Coventry said.

https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-14/r.title: Regional bands say it's now cheaper to do a gig in London than interstate
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-14/r.author: Joseph Hathaway-Wilson
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-14/r.text:
BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

By Joseph Hathaway-Wilson

Topic:
Air Transport Industry

It now costs Arnhem Land band King Stingray more to fly to gigs interstate than to shows in the US. (Supplied)

Managers of internationally-renowned Aussie bands say high airfares are pricing regional artists out of the market.

It comes as the Productivity Commission this week revealed a widening gap between regional and metropolitan airfares.

Yothu Yindi manager Alan James says travel costs will put emerging artists out of business before their careers have taken off.

With the cost of regional airfares soaring, musicians and band managers say touring has become untenable for both famous bands and emerging artists from regional Australia.

An interim Productivity Commission report released this week revealed a significant price gap between regional and metropolitan flight routes.

It found long regional and remote flights cost 67 per cent more on average than major city routes, while short regional flights cost 173 per cent more per kilometre.

Alan James says high airfares are pricing Yothu Yindi "out of the market" for live music. (ABC News: Dane Hirst)

Yothu Yindi manager Alan James said the cost of travel had forced the internationally-renowned band from Arnhem Land to turn down shows within Australia.

"It's $5,200 return from Gove to Brisbane, it would be cheaper for us to go do a concert in London than it would be to do a concert in a capital city of Australia," he said.

Yothu Yindi bassist Stuart Kellaway — who now manages fellow Arnhem Land rock band King Stingray — said the next generation band's recent flights to shows in the United States cost less than domestic flights.

Yothu Yindi played the 2025 Garma Festival but had to turn down shows interstate. (ABC News: Che Chorley)

"We've had to turn down three or four shows in the past month or so because it just wasn't going to work financially with the airfare components," he said.

Mr Kellaway the sky-high airfares were affecting the ability even of artists in the prime of their careers to make a living.

"With streaming and everything else, gigs are one of the last, decent income streams for bands," he said.

Mr James said while all bands were impacted by the exorbitant airfares, for new artists in particular, the costs could make sustainable careers in the music industry impossible.

"If you're an emerging group, you've got no shot, you're out of the business," he said.

"It really means for musicians, if you're not based in a capital city, then you're not in the market anymore."

King Stingray manager Stuart Kellaway (third from left) says bands based outside capital cities are "not in the market anymore". (ABC / Matt Garrick)

Both Mr James and Mr Kellaway said they had noticed a decline in the number of airlines servicing Arnhem Land throughout the course of Yothu Yindi's career.

Their observations align with the findings of the Productivity Commission's report, which noted competition in regional aviation was severely limited.

Fears FIFO specialists will soon need to pass rising flight costs onto vulnerable country patients.

Several airlines have reduced NT services recently, leaving flights between Darwin and capitals such as Sydney, Adelaide and Canberra serviced only by Qantas and its subsidiary Jetstar.

In a statement, a Qantas spokesperson said rising costs had dramatically influenced the price of tickets in and out of the NT.

"Aviation costs, including labour, airport charges and government air traffic control fees, are rising faster than the rate of inflation, while fuel costs also remain significantly higher," they said.

"Great value fares can still be found on flights to and from the Northern Territory and we encourage customers to book ahead whenever possible to secure the best fare."

https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-14/j.title: Rope barriers at parliament round out prickly week for government
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-14/j.author: Keane Bourke
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-14/j.text:
BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Topic:
State and Territory Government

Rope barriers were placed outside Parliament House on Thursday. (ABC News: Keane Bourke)

If the government wanted to signal it was in touch with community concerns, walking through Hollywood-style velvet ropes and gold posts at parliament was probably not the best way to do it.

The ritzy accoutrements, aimed at separating politicians from the media as they arrive at parliament, seem more "let them eat cake" than cozzie living.

It was an image the government could have done without as it closed out a particularly challenging week.

Let's start with the extraordinary scenes of Labor MPs trying to shepherd their colleague, Riverton MP Jagadish Krishnan, past waiting media and into parliament.

Journalists have been asking MPs questions at that entrance for decades.

It's not the only way into the building, but it's often the only one media are waiting at.

Colleagues shielded Labor MP Jags Krishnan from the media on Wednesday.  (ABC News)

Which makes it all the more extraordinary that when Dr Jags, as he's known, chose to walk through that entrance, MP Terry Healy tried to get between his beleaguered colleague and reporters before fellow MP Pierre Yang tried to pull him through the doorway.

The contribution of Cockburn MP David Scaife, who told reporters to be "ashamed of yourselves", didn't help — although he apologised the following day, saying he had been worried about politicians' safety claiming the entry was blocked by the media.

When the barriers were installed the following day by parliamentary staff, not a single MP who spoke that morning was supportive of them.

The rope barriers were seemingly intended to prevent journalists from getting too close to MPs as they entered the building.   (ABC News: Keane Bourke)

The premier's office subsequently admitted one of its staff had asked two unnamed MPs to "support" Dr Jags on his way into parliament.

"This is now a government with total contempt for transparency," opposition leader Basil Zempilas said.

"They have lost a handle on how to act, both in the chamber, outside the chamber, and with just about everything that they do."

The issue of course isn't really the barriers — which are more of a symbolic than practical obstruction — or whether MPs like the media or not.

It's about the ability for an issue in the public interest — the business dealings and disclosures of Dr Jags — to be fully ventilated, and the appearance which is created when that doesn't happen.

Dr Jags Krishnan in parliament.   (ABC News: Andrew O'Connor)

The former GP is being sued in the United States over accusations of failing to pay back a million-dollar loan, which he's vowed to "vigorously defend".

Reporting in other media — which has not been verified by the ABC — has also raised questions about whether Dr Jags complied with the rules by telling parliament about his debts and any gifts he receives.

The opportunity to ask him directly about those issues was lost when he was swept into parliament.

The next day, during an ill-fated bid by the opposition to force an inquiry into the issues, Dr Jags said he was in the final process of selling a network of doctors' surgeries he had built and that "all outstanding matters will be resolved upon settlement".

"I have taken legal advice about my parliamentary declarations and I am confident that these are in order," he added.

The other lingering headache for the government is its handling of issues in the child protection system, first brought to light by media reports more than two months ago.

Some progress was made when Cook and Child Protection Minister Jessica Stojkovski met with Dorothy Papertalk, who says the system failed her three grandchildren before they were murdered by their mother.

But those problems do not begin or end in the child protection system, which is why elders and the opposition started questioning what role Aboriginal Affairs Minister Don Punch was playing in improving the lot for First Nations communities.

On Monday the premier denied it had taken Punch months to visit Port Hedland, before his minister admitted later that day it was his first visit since July.

The pair eventually managed to explain Punch's role in listening to Aboriginal communities and providing that information to cabinet, but couldn't really explain what difference that had made.

Don Punch admitted he hadn't been to Port Hedland since July.  (ABC News: Briana Shepherd)

On Thursday he quoted from Pilbara Indigenous leader, Doris Eaton, who wrote that his attendance at an on-country meeting was "greatly appreciated" and a "great example" of collaboration.

But he failed to mention less favourable parts of that letter, including a section which notes her requests from 2024 and 2025 "are yet to be fully addressed or realised" and encouraging him to share her "concerns" with colleagues to instigate "much needed action".

The government was left on the backfoot this week, forced to defend longstanding issues instead of focusing on anything constructive it was doing.

"I want to be talking about cost of living, health and housing, that's my priorities and that's what it will always be," minister John Carey said on Thursday.

John Carey speaks to journalists outside WA parliament, after the rope barriers were set up.  (ABC News: Keane Bourke)

And there is plenty to talk about in that space, including concern that the federal government's negative gearing changes may reduce rental supply.

It's yet another potential challenge facing the government at the end of a year which has grown increasingly difficult, after it lost a heartland seat in Secret Harbour to One Nation and struggled to gain support for its university merger proposal.

The summer break presents an opportunity to reset and return with a fresh focus in the new year.

For Labor, that can't come soon enough.

https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-14/m.title: Litany of missed opportunities in Floreat murder tragedy
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-14/m.author: Lucy Murray
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-14/m.text:
BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Missed opportunities in the lead-up to the Floreat murders were examined during the inquest. (ABC News: Ruby Littler)

It was a crime that shocked Perth: a family and domestic violence murder in the heart of Perth's affluent western suburbs.

In what Mark Bombara's daughter, Ariel, would later describe as "planned choices … made to murder, underpinned by a lifetime of power, privilege, control and entitlement", Bombara forced his way into the home of his wife's best friend, Jennifer Petelczyc, in May 2024.

Bombara was looking for his estranged wife, Rowena; instead he found medical receptionist Jennifer, 59, and her 18-year-old daughter, Gretl.

Gunman's daughter Ariel Bombara speaks outside court after Floreat murders coronial inquest

"When he realised my mum wasn’t in your home, rather than walking back out of that house he decided time was up, and murdering your whole family would be the next best punishment," Ariel Bombara would tell an inquest into their deaths this week in an devastating disavowal of her father's actions.

Held over five days, the inquest laid bare a cascading series of police errors and missed opportunities to save the lives of the Petelczyc women before they were murdered in cold blood.

The gunman killed Jennifer and Gretl Petelczyc in 2024 in a horrific shooting. (Supplied)

The startling revelations include a two-decades-long failure to review gun licences, four separate pleas to police for help that went unheeded, and multiple Triple Zero (000) calls — made as the murders were unfolding — left on hold.

As the women pleaded for their lives, Gretl twice tried to call emergency services, but both times she waited on the line for more than one minute to be put through to police.

The calls disconnected before she could talk to an officer.

Yet, counter to police policy, no-one called her back.

Ariel Bombara got through to police as she and her mother, Rowena, listened to the murders in real time while on the phone with Jennifer Petelczyc.

Ariel was forced to wait two minutes and 18 seconds for her call to be connected.

When she finally got through and explained the situation, the job was designated a priority two by the call taker.

The two women were killed in their Floreat home. (ABC News: David Weber)

It took five minutes to be upgraded to a priority one.

The first police arrived 11 minutes after the call, just in time to hear the last of five gunshots, with which Mark Bombara took his own life.

Detective Senior Sergeant Matt Edmunds told the court he did not think there was time for officers to intervene and save the women.

Matt Edmunds did not think there was enough time to save the victims when officers arrived. (ABC News: Julian Robins)

Acting State Coroner Sarah Linton agreed, but said if Gretl had spoken to an officer on the phone, she would have at least been reassured help was on the way in her final moments.

About two months before the murders, police escorted the gunman's estranged wife into the family home to collect her belongings.

The inquest into the deaths of Jennifer and Gretl Petelcyzc hears new details about the day they died and the gunman's interactions with police weeks before the shooting.

Rowena had left her husband just weeks beforehand, moving out of the home with daughter Ariel.

She and other family members warned the attending officers about Mark Bombara's fragile mental health, with son Isaac telling police there may be firearms in the gun safe or "other locations".

Despite this warning, police officers did not seize the weapons of a suspected domestic violence perpetrator, search the home for unsecured guns or inspect the safe.

If they had, they would have discovered more than 1,000 rounds of illegal ammunition.

Constable Shaun King entered the house first and accepted a cup of tea from Mark Bombara, whose behaviour was the "opposite" of what he was expecting.

"I hate to say it, but he seemed like a nice guy," Constable King said, admitting he had been impressed by Bombara's opulent home with its "million dollar view".

The court heard Mark Bombara manipulated police in the weeks before the shooting. (Supplied)

This had impacted the inexperienced officer's ability to assess Bombara's character, he admitted.

Superintendent Andrew Wilson reviewed body-worn camera footage and said Bombara "groomed" the attending officers into a false sense of security.

"I believe [his behaviour] was manipulative … calculated … in an effort to place seeds of doubt in the attending officers' minds," Superintendent Andrew Wilson said.

The day before, Rowena and Ariel had attended Mirrabooka Police Station to make a formal complaint of domestic violence, asking for a police order — issued when police think a person is likely to commit an act of family violence.

Ariel Bombara made several appeals to police about her father. (ABC News: Lucy Murray)

They feared for their lives, they told police, recounting a long history of abusive behaviour and noting Mark Bombara had access to firearms.

The coroner in the Floreat murder-suicide inquest questions why a desperate call to Triple Zero stating someone had been shot in a family violence situation was initially marked as a priority two situation.

They were told the grounds to make a police order were not met.

They tried again. Ariel phoned both the Perth police station and the Family Violence Division, warning her father was increasingly unstable and had access to 13 guns.

Still no police orders were made.

An internal report found officers should have issued a 72-hour police order giving police the power to seize his firearms.

Eight officers were found to have not performed their duty and were subject to internal disciplinary action.

The inquest also revealed Mark Bombara should never have been able to hold a licence for the two Glock handguns he took to the Petelczyc home.

Bombara held a collector's licence on sentimental grounds, despite that no longer being a valid reason to hold guns.

The inquest heard the gunman should not have had the weapons he took to the Floreat home. (ABC News: Julian Robins)

But since no-one was checking the online licence renewal system for about 20 years, his licence was re-issued illegally, six times, from 2005 onwards.

Less than 12 months before the murders, police wrote to Bombara with questions about his weapon storage locations.

He said he would get back to them but never did, despite two follow-up letters.

The man who shot dead a mother and daughter in their Floreat home should not have been able to renew his licence for the murder weapon, a coronial inquest is told.

A computer system upgrade then wiped all records relating to gun storage non-compliance orders.

Police yesterday conceded mistakes had been made.

"WA Police accepts there were important lessons to be learnt from this tragedy," Commissioner Col Blanch said in a statement at the conclusion of the inquest.

"WA Police has been open about the shortcomings identified in the police response leading up to this tragedy."

Col Blanch acknowledged police failures. (ABC News: Jake Sturmer)

This included "failures in the assessment and management of risk", which had led to 18 recommendations to improve responses to family and domestic violence — of which 14 have been completed, according to the commissioner.

Acting State Coroner Sarah Linton is expected to hand down her recommendations next year.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.title: U.S. Air Force captain arrested in Okinawa for alleged drunk driving
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
Japanese police arrested a U.S. Air Force captain Saturday on suspicion of drunk driving in Okinawa, a police spokesman said, in the latest twist to strains between the Pacific allies.

The arrest comes just a week after Tokyo and Washington agreed to measures aimed at preventing crimes by U.S. service members on the island of Okinawa after a murder allegedly involving an American marine triggered outrage.

The U.S. military has around 54,000 personnel stationed in Japan, mostly on Okinawa. Crimes committed by its members have been a thorn in relations between the close security allies.

U.S. officials also said last week they would extend a curfew to lower-ranking service members through Dec. 7, while banning all service members from drinking alcohol outside their homes between midnight and 5 am.

Police arrested the 27-year-old as he “was driving on a road in Okinawa City at around 3:09 am Saturday,” a spokesman for Okinawa prefectural police said.

“It is not clear if he violated the curfew” imposed by U.S. officials, he said.

The arrested captain was assigned to Kadena Air Base on Okinawa, Kyodo News reported.

Officials at the base were not immediately available for comment.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.summary: The arrest comes just a week after Tokyo and Washington agreed to measures aimed at preventing crimes by U.S. service members on Okinawa. The U.N. military has around 54,000 personnel stationed in Japan, mostly on Okinawa.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.title: 6-year-old Gaza burn victim caught in Israeli dispute over aid
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: Nidal Al-mughrabi
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
CAIRO/GAZA – The excruciating burns run around the side of Masa Yassin’s tiny face, behind her ear, over her scalp and down her neck.

Since her family’s tent burst into flames when a nearby cooking gas tank exploded in July, part of the 6-year-old girl’s treatment has been a clear plastic 3D-printed mask, which helps manage swelling and control the scars on her face.

But soon she will outgrow it, and the international medical charity Medecins Sans Frontieres, which operates the only clinic in Gaza that can make her a new one, says it has been barred by Israel from importing the plastic.

“Should there be no masks, my daughter will grow more scar tissue,” said Masa’s mother Islam Yassin, as she gently adjusted straps on the mask of the girl on her lap on a plastic chair in their tent in a camp in Gaza City.

“We would have to resort to surgery instead of masks, and there are no such surgeries in Gaza.”

More than a year since a ceasefire halted major fighting in Gaza, the entire population of more than 2 million Palestinians lives confined to around a third of the tiny enclave’s territory, mainly in makeshift tents and damaged buildings.

Israeli forces still control everything that enters and exits. Israel says it allows in all needed medical equipment and supplies. But many aid groups say restrictions make it impossible to provide basic treatment desperately needed by a vulnerable population besieged inside a conflict zone.

The custom masks provided by MSF for scores of Gazan burn victims have become embroiled in a dispute between the international medical charity and Israel over Israeli demands for information about local staff working for foreign groups.

Israel has banned MSF’s international staff from Gaza and barred the group from importing any supplies since the end of February, after MSF refused an Israeli demand to submit names of all its local staff in Gaza. MSF says it cannot provide such lists without assurances staff would be safe, because hundreds of medics have been killed during the war.

In a response to a request for comment, COGAT, the unit of the Israeli military responsible for aid to Gaza, confirmed it had barred imports by MSF for failure to comply with requirements, including supplying staff lists needed to prevent “the misuse of humanitarian aid by terrorist organizations.”

It said that unlike MSF, other aid groups had complied and were operating freely. It had approved the entry of more than 24,000 tons of medical supplies into Gaza, it said, and rejected accusations that it was blocking medical aid as a falsehood spread by Hamas militants.

MSF says complying with the Israeli registration requirement would put its staff in danger, and that the victims of the restrictions are vulnerable Palestinian patients like Masa.

“A child’s mutilated face can no longer receive even a basic treatment, not because the technology or the expertise is lacking, but because Israel imposes a regime under which healing itself is a privilege,” Filipe Ribeiro, MSF’s head of mission for Palestine, said in a message.

At an MSF clinic in Gaza City, technicians measured Masa’s face to try to see if they could make adjustments to her existing mask so she can keep wearing it for longer as she grows, since they do not have supplies to make a new one.

“We have now exhausted our stock of plastic sheets and printer filament,” said Mohammed Al-Qatrawi, supervisor of physiotherapy for MSF France in Gaza at the clinic. Once Masa grows and her mask no longer fits properly, it could cause her pain and limit the benefits, he said.

Demand has been surging. There are 70 patients, including 50 children, receiving treatment for facial burns, 20 of whom need masks urgently, he said. With so many children needing new masks, MSF has been decorating some of them with drawings of cartoon characters such as the Smurfs and SpongeBob SquarePants.

If the clinic were forced to halt its service, patients such as Masa would “develop scar-related complications that can affect speaking, eating, drinking, vision, and facial movement,” he said. Children would have worse deformities that could leave them ostracized.

Back outside her tent, Masa plays marbles in the dirt with her twin sister and their younger sister. You can see her face beneath the clear plastic as she smiles.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.summary: Medecins Sans Frontieres says it has been barred by Israel from importing the plastic. The international medical charity operates the only clinic in Gaza that can make her a new one. The custom masks provided by MSF for scores of Gazan burn victims have become embroiled in a dispute between the international medical charities.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.title: Former Nvidia CEO Huang had a relationship with a second employee, sources say
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.text:
SAN FRANCISCO – Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second employee, according to two people familiar with the matter.

The revelation follows two other extramarital affairs that led to his resignation Thursday. The two women are Alice Huang, who U.S. intelligence suspects of being a Chinese spy, and Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care.

Reuters is not naming the second employee. Attempts to reach the woman were not successful.

Nvidia declined to comment. Powell, Jensen Huang, and a representative for Nvidia’s board did not reply to requests for comment. Alice Huang could not be reached for comment.

Jensen Huang admitted to an affair in a Nov. 8 statement following the reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, without referring to her by name.

The former Nvidia CEO’s decision to resign from the company could disrupt the AI industry that he helped shape. Nvidia has used its financial strength to help create an industry around AI through complex financial arrangements that ease the purchase of the company’s chips. It has backed cloud computing companies and AI labs in order to do so.

Pressure on Jensen Huang, who is 63 and married, to resign mounted after reports of his affair with Alice Huang.

Nvidia’s board appointed finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO while it conducts a search to replace Jensen Huang. The board is considering internal and external candidates for the job.

Earlier this month, Nvidia’s board launched a probe, led by independent directors with outside legal counsel, into whether Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. It also expressed confidence in him at the time.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.summary: The two women are Alice Huang, who U.S. intelligence suspects of being a Chinese spy, and Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care. The two woman are Alice and Kimberly. Attempts to reach the woman were not successful.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.text:
Microsoft Corp. said access has been fully restored to its flagship software, ending an outage that paralyzed government offices, traders and businesses around the world.

“All products are operational,” according to a service health status update on its website. A “backlog of email messages has been processed, thus this issue is remediated,” it said of its Microsoft 365 services.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.title: Japan and Philippines to ink deal on oil reserve cooperation
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.text:
Japan and the Philippines are expected to sign a memorandum of understanding on strengthening cooperation on oil stockpiling in the Southeast Asian country.

Under the partnership, Japan’s public and private sectors will help the Philippines develop a national oil reserve system as part of measures to enhance its energy security.

The MOU is set to be signed early next week by industry minister Ryosei Akazawa and a Philippine official ahead of a summit of the Asia Zero Emission Community framework in Manila on Tuesday.

The Philippines declared a state of national energy emergency in March amid growing turmoil in the Middle East and has since been working to bolster the resilience of its oil supply.

The memorandum will cover a joint study on cooperating with oil-producing countries such as Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates as well as the development of systems needed to establish a national oil reserve plan.

Meanwhile, Japanese engineering firm Chiyoda Corp. is expected to sign an MOU with Philippine National Oil soon on technological assistance for oil reserve facilities.

Japan’s Partnership on Wide Energy and Resources Resilience Asia, or POWERR Asia, a framework announced in April to provide about $10 billion in financial aid to Asian countries for enhancing their energy supply networks, is seen as a possible source of funding for the measures.

Like Japan, the Philippines depends on the Middle East for more than 90% of its crude oil imports. As of May 3, the country held reserves of oil equivalent to only 53 days of domestic consumption, far below Japan’s public- and private-sector reserves capable of covering 207 days.

Having experienced fuel shortages and supply confusion following the de facto closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a key oil transport waterway in the Middle East, the Philippines is working to establish a national oil reserve system while raising stockpiles at its private sector.

The country plans to construct storage tanks for national reserves for completion in 2027 and later, aiming to eventually increase its oil reserves by 15 million barrels, equivalent to 30 days of consumption.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.summary: Japan and Philippines to sign memorandum of understanding on oil stockpiling in Southeast Asian country. The Philippines declared a state of national energy emergency in March amid growing turmoil in the Middle East. Japan's public and private sectors will help the Philippines develop a national oil reserve system.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: No Author

Japan is considering setting its total defense spending for the next five years at around ¥60 trillion, as it revises its three key national security-related documents by the end of this year.

The Defense Ministry estimates that necessary defense expenditures for the five-year period will total ¥70 trillion to ¥80 trillion, while the Finance Ministry is arguing for spending below ¥60 trillion, sources said Friday.

With Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi reportedly reluctant to raise taxes to fund defense spending, a battle between the Finance and Defense ministries over spending levels and how to secure the necessary funding is intensifying.

WASHINGTON – U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio delivered an aggressive and unrepentant challenge to international law in a speech on Friday, warning that the U.S. would never submit to the “sterile vision of radical judges or soulless global bureaucrats.”

His address singled out the International Criminal Court, as President Donald Trump and his administration have done many times over the course of his first and second terms. Rubio dismissed international law as an instrument that elites — whom he didn’t name — use to advance their own interests.

“If they’re foolish enough to try to enforce their paper decrees on Americans, our answer will probably be the same as the Roman general Pompey when he said to those who were trying to invoke their city’s charters against his legions, he said, ’Stop quoting laws to men with swords,’” Rubio said.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.title: Pentagon No. 3 hails subs as ‘indispensable’ to deterring foes in Pacific
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
The U.S. Navy’s submarines are an “indispensable” part of the U.S. arsenal when it comes to deterring adversaries in the Pacific, the Pentagon’s policy chief told an industry audience this week.

Elbridge Colby, the undersecretary of defense for policy, didn’t mention China before the audience of submarine contractors and Navy officials on Thursday in an address to the Naval Submarine League, an industry group. But the reference was unmistakable.

“In a region defined by distance and maritime geography, submarines complicate an adversary’s plans in ways few other capabilities can even approach,” Colby said. “Moreover, as the sea surface becomes more observable and more contested, the undersea domain takes on even greater strategic value.”

Next week, U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping will hold their third summit this year on the sidelines of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen.

Colby said the “silent service” is crucial when it comes to denying an adversary control of the “first island chain” encompassing Japan, Taiwan, portions of the Philippines and Indonesia.

He said U.S. attack submarines play an “outsized role” in helping undermine the confidence of geopolitical rivals in securing a quick, decisive military victory in operations at or across large bodies of water — a possible reference to deterring any Chinese move against Taiwan.

Elbridge Colby didn’t mention China before the audience of submarine contractors and Navy officials on Thursday.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
BANGKOK – ASEAN is under increasing pressure at its upcoming summit to ease a five-year ban on Myanmar’s military-backed leaders attending high-level meetings, after Thailand and several other members stepped up engagement despite the country’s ongoing civil war.

Leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations are set to review their decision to exclude Myanmar when they meet in Manila from Nov. 15 to Nov. 17.

Myanmar has been in turmoil since 2021, when then-military chief Min Aung Hlaing ousted the elected government in a coup, unleashing armed conflict across much of the country that has killed more than 100,000 people.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
Sen. Chris Van Hollen, a progressive from Maryland, is challenging Sen. Chuck Schumer to lead the Senate next year, escalating a fight inside the Democratic Party over how aggressive to be in forcing an end to the Iran war and taking on corporate power.

Van Hollen cast Schumer as a status quo leader unprepared to meet the moment, insisting the sweeping Democratic election victories are a mandate for big changes in an economy he argues is rigged against working people.

Crucially, Van Hollen has called for defunding the Iran war immediately, rather than postponing the confrontation until the new year and a new Congress. Schumer has said Democrats should use the power of the purse to end the war, but has not laid out a strategy to do so.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.title: White House demanding Japan triple host-nation support for U.S. troops
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
The United States is demanding that Japan provide a total of ¥3 trillion over the five years starting in fiscal 2027 for U.S. forces stationed in the country under its Host Nation Support program, about three times the current five-year total of around ¥1 trillion, sources have said.

Meanwhile, the Japanese government is estimating the amount at around ¥1.5 trillion for the next five years, taking into account the yen’s depreciation and rising prices.

Although the two governments aim to reach an agreement by the end of this year, negotiations are likely to be difficult.

Tokyo’s host-nation support for the five years through fiscal 2026, which ends in March 2027, totaled ¥1.06 trillion, averaging about ¥210 billion annually. Even under Japan’s estimate, the annual average would rise to ¥300 billion.

“Even the impact of foreign exchange rates alone would increase the amount to about 1.5 times the previous level,” one source said.

The Japanese government is also considering proposals to build shelters and take other measures to ensure that U.S. military bases in Japan can maintain their functions even if attacked.

During the first administration of U.S. President Donald Trump, Washington reportedly demanded more than four times the amount provided under the program at the time.

“We’re working hard to make adjustments in response to the high demands,” a Japanese government source said.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.summary: The U.S. is demanding that Japan provide a total of ¥3 trillion over the five years starting in fiscal 2027. The Japanese government is estimating the amount at around ¥1.5 trillion for the next five years. The two governments aim to reach an agreement by the end of this year.

The three leaders will meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese city, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/202.title: ‘Love Village’ is a warts-and-all take on the realities of middle-aged romance
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/202.author: Mike Fu
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/202.text:
[Editor’s note: This article contains spoilers for season three of “Love Village.”]

After 23 episodes of “Love Village,” you, too, may start to hum The Police’s “Every Breath You Take” with a swell of emotion whenever you catch sight of Mount Fuji. The 1980s hit is the musical leitmotif of the Netflix reality show’s third season, proving to be a poignant and versatile soundtrack for interpersonal dramas big and small.

On the surface, “Love Village” hasn’t changed its formula since it debuted in 2023. Capsule hotels, themed love hotels, traditional ryokan inns and more — Japan has no shortage of specialized accommodations depending on your needs. But where do you go when you want to literally get away from it all?

Japan’s camping scene has the answer: Wherever you want.

Thanks to a majority of the country being covered by forested mountains, both official and unofficial campgrounds abound in Japan. And with the weather across many regions currently in a sweet spot of autumn temperatures, now is a good time to pack up some necessities and pitch a tent for a night in Japan’s great outdoors.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/life/2026/1.author: Owen Ziegler
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/life/2026/1.text:
No company in video games is committed to doing things its own way quite like Nintendo.

In the months and weeks leading up to the Nov. 19 release of Rockstar Games’ “Grand Theft Auto VI” — the most anticipated title of the decade and potentially the most expensive piece of media ever produced with a budget rumored to exceed $1 billion — numerous studios postponed the release of new games to avoid being overshadowed.

As expected, though, Nintendo marched to the beat of its own drum, releasing not only an exceptional remake of the action-adventure classic “The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time” on Nov. 5 but also “Nintendo Switch Sports Resort,” the latest entry in its motion-controlled sports simulator franchise, on Oct. 22.

https://www.scmp.com/news/world/europe/a.title: Turkey detains 6 over deadly steel blast that killed 17
https://www.scmp.com/news/world/europe/a.author: Agence France-Presse
https://www.scmp.com/news/world/europe/a.text:
The deadly blast at one of Turkey’s top steel producers also left around a dozen people injured, at least one in critical condition

Six people were arrested overnight after a huge blast at a steel plant near the western city of Izmir killed 17 workers, with grieving families waiting on Tuesday to receive their loved ones’ bodies for burial.

Onlookers said Monday’s massive explosion felt like “an earthquake” when it ripped through the Habas steel factory in Aliaga, a district 60km (37 miles) north of Izmir known for ship-breaking and heavy industry.

Police have so far detained six people in connection with the incident, with Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar warning “the number could rise”.

https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-zelenskyy-.text:
The US has broached the idea of Kyiv giving up the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership, the Ukrainian president said.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said US peace envoys asked whether Kyiv would withdraw from its eastern region of ‌Donbas ⁠in exchange ⁠for joining NATO, according to remarks to the media published on Saturday.

The suggestion was made following the latest round of peace talks in Abu Dhabi to bring Russia's nearly 5-year war in Ukraine to a close.

The Ukrainian leader told reporters: "The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would ⁠Ukraine ​withdraw from Donbas?'"

Zelenskyy repeated Kyiv's position that it was not willing to cede territory to Russia. But he added that if the country reached a comprehensive deal, including security guarantees, a ‌strong ​and well-funded Ukrainian army and funds to rebuild, he would put the question ​to the public in a referendum.

"That ​is why ⁠I believe NATO is back on the ⁠agenda. ​But you have also heard [Russian President Vladimir] Putin's signals, and this is an extremely difficult conversation."

Zelenskyy said the prospect of NATO membership in exchange for withdrawing from Donbas has not been raised before.

He also warned about Moscow's plan to  change the continent's security architecture, saying it could lead to more conflict.

Putin has demanded that NATO pull back its troops from the Russian border, which European Union leaders have strongly criticized.

"This is dangerous because, in my view, it is precisely things like this that lead to wars or escalations," Zelenskyy added.

"Real security in Europe means the EU and NATO. That's it. There is no other security in Europe."

On Friday, the EU said several European diplomats would take part in future Ukraine peace talks, including Germany, France, the United Kingdom and Poland.

Moscow has long insisted that European states be excluded from the negotiations because they support Ukraine.

The comments come as Russia’s Defence Ministry said its ⁠forces ⁠had captured the ​settlement of Tersianka in ​Ukraine’s southeastern ​Zaporizhzhia ‌region, news agency Interfax reported.

Interfax cited the ministry as saying that Russian ​forces had struck Ukrainian energy and ​transport infrastructure used by ⁠the ​military, along with ammunition ​depots and ​drone production ‌and storage sites.

Russia has targeted power stations across Ukraine in waves of ballistic and cruise missile attacks, cutting power and heating to millions of people as temperatures plunge.

Zelenskyy warned that Putin was "betting everything" on this winter's war campaign, which Kyiv insists is aimed at hurting public morale.

https://www.dw.com/en/new-facilities-in-.title: New facilities in Laos and Cambodia: Is China expanding its military presence in Southeast Asia?
https://www.dw.com/en/new-facilities-in-.text:
China has been growing its economic relationships in Southeast Asia. Now new military facilities in Laos and Cambodia are causing smaller countries to worry China's military networks are also expanding.

It's often said that maintaining good relations with your neighbors is essential. So in early November, China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi invited his counterparts from Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Thailand and Myanmar to Beijing.

There the six countries agreed on closer economic and security cooperation.

The visit is just one example of China's growing influence on Southeast Asia. It's not just about trade or infrastructure either, it's also increasingly about military cooperation.

For instance, at the end of September, China and Laos opened a joint military support and training center north of the Laotian capital, Vientiane. Initially Laotian air force pilots are to be trained at the Ban Keun airfield, China has said.

Earlier in 2025 China expanded its footprint at Cambodia's Ream naval base. China uses the facility on the Gulf of Thailand for logistics and training. And while Japanese and Vietnamese ships can visit the port, they're docked at a southern quay and it's unclear if other navies can use the same facilities under the same conditions as China.

"It remains to be seen how this [Ban Keun] will change China's military access to Southeast Asia," says Marco Bünte, a professor of Asian politics at the University Erlangen Nuremberg in Germany.

In recent years, China has significantly expanded its economic influence in the region.

The China-Laos railway and other infrastructure projects connect Laos more closely with its northern neighbor. Laos is also heavily indebted to China.

Bünte points out that Laos and Cambodia have been close military partners of China for some time and the new facility in Laos can be seen as another step towards deepening cooperation.

If that proves correct, "China would gain strategic depth in mainland Southeast Asia," Bünte explained. "It would also give China better military access to the South China Sea."

Johann Fuhrmann, head of the Konrad Adenauer Foundation's Beijing office, points out that one should distinguish between training Laotian pilots and any potential use of the facilities by Chinese armed forces later.

"China gains influence when it co-designs the training and operation of such facilities over several years," Fuhrmann told DW.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

But nobody should underestimate China's military positioning, Bünte continued. "China is expanding its military operational capabilities here although I wouldn't speak of military hegemony because China hasn't achieved that yet."

With regard to the Laotian airbase, China says that Laotian pilots will be trained there. But beside military transporters and helicopters, Laos actually only has three light combat aircraft by Russia's Yakovlev works.

According to the aviation media outlet FlightGlobal, four more K-8s, Chinese two-seat intermediate jet trainer and light attack aircrafts, are in service there. Satellite images analyzed by the Reuters news agency in early October show eight K-8s at the base — even thought this doesn't necessarily mean they are stationed there permanently.

Fuhrmann doesn't think anybody should jump to conclusions about this.

"The idea of ​​a Chinese air corridor is more of a future scenario than something that has already been proven," he says.

For example, the runway at Ban Keun is only 2,000 meters (6,562 feet) long, which makes it too short for large Chinese bombers. These usually require 3,000 meters.

The crucial question is what rights China will be granted, Fuhrmann continues: "Will China have to obtain the approval of the respective government for every new use? Or are there longer-term commitments that both sides can invoke, even in times of crisis?"

Surrounding countries are reacting differently to what appears to be China's growing influence in Laos, Cambodia and Myanmar because these countries are already considered closer to China.

Other Southeast Asian nations are hedging, trying to expand their relationship with China without severing ties with the US and also maintaining economic links with other Western nations. China's involvement offers them additional options and Beijing wants to explore those possibilities. That's just pragmatic though, Bünte says of the smaller Asian nations.

"Overall, these states… try to keep as many options open as possible," he notes.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Vietnam and the Philippines are watching developments particularly closely. Both have territorial disputes with China in the South China Sea. But Vietnam also has close historical ties to Laos and trained its own military there.

In early November, the Vietnamese government declared that any military cooperation must serve peace and stability and referred to the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia, commonly known as the ASEAN Treaty. China is not an ASEAN member but has also stated that its activities are not directed against any third parties.

"So far, these are individual steps," Bünte adds. "We would have to wait and see if this leads to a broader military alliance in the years to come."

Fuhrmann says that Western nations should help strengthen the smaller countries in the region and take their interests seriously.

"Ultimately, a counterweight can only be achieved through tangible contributions, not through warnings or lectures from Europe," he says.

This story was originally published in German.
